title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Marine and Coastal Tourism Development
abstract: This study aims to analyze the evolution, structure, and research trends in global marine and coastal tourism development between 2020 and 2025, as well as to identify key research themes, influential contributors, leading countries, and collaboration networks shaping the field. A descriptive bibliometric analysis was conducted using data retrieved from the Scopus database, combining quantitative performance analysis through the Bibliometrix R package with network visualization using VOSviewer, including the application of Lotka’s Law to examine author productivity patterns. title: Limited atmospheric iron availability increase during the Younger Dryas in the Northern Hemisphere
abstract: Iron (Fe) availability modulates phytoplankton blooms in High-Nutrient Low-Chlorophyll (HNLC) regions, i.e., ocean areas characterized by an abundance of major nutrients but low marine productivity. Fe can be delivered to the oceans through atmospheric dust deposition, making ice cores unique archives for reconstructing past changes in aeolian Fe deposition. However, while it is known that during dustier periods atmospheric Fe depositions increased, uncertainties remain regarding the fraction of Fe actually available to phytoplankton. Consistent drivers of coastal biodiversity across the tree of life
abstract: Coastal ecosystems are threatened by global change but remain understudied despite their importance for biodiversity and human society. For instance, most coastal studies and monitoring programs focus on a few groups of organisms owing to methodological limitations. However, high-throughput sequencing of environmental DNA (eDNA) now facilitates taxonomically broad studies of coastal biodiversity. title: Region-specific LOI–TOC conversion models for marine sediment blue carbon assessment in the Western Irish Sea
abstract: Continental-shelf sediments (< 200 m water depth; ~ 9% of the global seafloor) store large amounts of organic carbon (OC) and accumulate OC annually, but management and accounting applications require regional evidence and transparent uncertainty. Loss-on-ignition (LOI) is a rapid, low-cost proxy for organic matter and OC, but LOI-to- total organic carbon (TOC) conversions vary with sediment type and analytical protocol. This study used multiagency Western Irish Sea data to test whether region- and sediment-specific LOI-to-TOC regressions improve OC estimation relative to a pooled conversion.

title: Satellite-Derived Relative Bathymetry Mapping of Kopa Dam Using Sentinel-2 Level-2A Imagery and GIS Techniques
abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) provides a remote-sensing approach for characterizing spatial variations in water depth-related information without requiring complete conventional hydrographic coverage. This study developed a relative satellite-derived bathymetry map of Kopa Dam, Tafa Local Government Area, Niger State, Nigeria, using Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery and ArcGIS 10.8. Sentinel-2 Bands 2 and 3, representing the blue and green portions of the visible spectrum, were used to derive a logarithmic spectral-ratio called Relative Bathymetry Index (RBI). title: Plastic debris in the Ecuadorian shoreline, coastal and deep-water zones of the eastern Pacific margin
abstract: Although 28 studies worldwide have documented plastic debris on the deep-sea floor, only one has addressed the eastern Pacific margin. Equally uncommon are long-term beach monitoring programs that integrate debris counts with oceanographic and meteorological records. This study delivers the first combined evidence of abyssal contamination and a six-year coastal time series in the equatorial eastern Pacific, establishing a rare dual perspective on plastic transport and deposition across connected marine environments. title: Lebanese faunal legacy collections uncover 400,000 years of woodland resilience and distinct hominin ecological strategies
abstract: Abstract The Levant is a key biogeographic corridor, yet historical instability has limited research creating a polarization toward its southern region. To address this geographical bias, we reassessed three legacy faunal collections from Lebanon: Naame, Nahr Ibrahim, and Ras el-Kelb. For the first time, we obtained direct dates for these assemblages and, through zooarchaeological methods, dental wear analysis, and landscape modeling, reconstructed aspects of ungulate and hominin ecology and behavior. title: Identification of Marine Borer Species on Ternate Beach, North Maluku, Indonesia
abstract: The Ternate coast is a tropical marine area characterized by warm temperatures and high salinity, supporting various marine organisms, including borers that cause wood biodeterioration. These organisms inflict severe damage on wood-based coastal infrastructure, including piers, stilt houses, and vessels. This study aimed to identify marine borer species in Ternate and determine the infested coastal wood types. title: Ultrasonic parametric investigation of a coral slab: prospects for in situ non-destructive testing of coral microatolls.
abstract: Coral microatolls are natural tide gauges whose growth records provide valuable information on long-term sea-level variations that may be linked to global climate change. At present, investigating coral microatolls requires cutting a slab with a hydraulic chain saw to analyze their growth patterns. This approach is logistically demanding, damages both the coral and the surrounding ecosystem, and is inherently destructive. title: Integrating underwater photo transects and environmental DNA to assess coral genus composition in nearshore reefs of Madura, Indonesia
abstract: Understanding coral community composition is essential for reef conservation, particularly in data-limited tropical regions such as Indonesia. This study compares genus-level coral detections from Underwater Photo Transect surveys and environmental DNA metabarcoding on nearshore reefs of Gili Genting and Gili Labak, Madura, Indonesia. title: Linking spring hydrologic variability to estuarine nutrient loading and stoichiometry: insights for land–river–coastal management in South Korea
abstract: Riverine nutrient exports influence estuarine and coastal water quality by delivering carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus from inland watersheds. Streamflow variability and nutrient concentrations jointly determine nutrient loads, which remains uncertain depending on a region of interest. Here we investigate how inter-annual variability of boreal spring streamflow is associated with the magnitude of Total Organic Carbon (TOC), Total Nitrogen (TN), and Total Phosphorus (TP) loads, and their stoichiometric composition (C:N:P ratios) at 19 estuarine sites of South Korea. title: EVALUATION OF SEAWATER INTRUSION VULNERABILITY USING THE G-ALDLcR METHOD, CASE STUDY: KRUI, PESISIR BARAT, LAMPUNG
abstract: Coastal areas play a crucial role in social, economic, and ecological activities, but are vulnerable to environmental degradation due to seawater intrusion, which occurs when seawater infiltrates inland aquifers as a result of hydraulic pressure imbalances between freshwater and saltwater. Excessive groundwater exploitation leads to a decline in the water table, which in turn opens up opportunities for seawater to enter the aquifer system, thereby reducing groundwater quality in several coastal areas. title: Deep Sea hydrothermal vent habitats support gravid Antarctic krill
abstract: The long-term resilience of the Southern Ocean ecosystem relies on healthy populations of Antarctic krill, but climate change and increasing fishing pressure are placing this species at risk. Protecting Antarctic krill requires identification of key habitats for critical life history stages. Here, we present multiple lines of evidence that reproductively active female Antarctic krill utilize deep-sea hydrothermal vent habitats. title: Epifaunal communities differ between tropical and polar mesophotic marine animal forests
abstract: Understanding marine biodiversity in polar regions remains limited compared to tropical ecosystems, where coastal habitats have been more extensively studied; however, both regions exhibit a substantial lack of knowledge regarding mesophotic marine biota. Marine Animal Forests (MAFs), key components of oceanic biodiversity, remain largely unexplored at mesophotic depths (30–200 m) due to accessibility constraints. abstract: Marine gels constitute a large yet poorly explored ocean carbon pool. Shadow imaging was tuned to detect particles at two sensitivity levels: high-optical density particles (HODP), resembling the particles captured by most imaging systems, and low-optical density particles (LODP), representing a vastly more abundant and gel-dominated pool. title: A novel widely distributed marine Staphylococcus phage representing a new virus genus
abstract: Bacteriophages play critical roles in marine microbial ecology and evolution, partly through their carriage of auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs). Staphylococcus is widely distributed across seawater, sediments, and marine organisms, contributing to biogeochemical cycling. The presence and ecological roles of Staphylococcus equorum in marine environments remain largely unexplored, and the characteristics of marine phages infecting S. equorum and their interactions remain poorly understood. title: Mapping Coastal Resource–Environment Carrying Capacity in an Intensively Developed Coastal Area: Evidence from Rui’an, China
abstract: Abstract Coastal zones are dynamic land–sea interfaces where development pressures often approach ecological and environmental limits. Here, we operationalize a pressure–condition–response (P–C–R) framework to deliver a customized, high-resolution ( 30 × 30 m ) assessment of coastal resource–environment carrying capacity (RECC) for Rui’an (Zhejiang, China) using 2017 multisource geospatial, environmental, socioeconomic, and planning data sets. title: An advanced modelling study on the role of dimethyl sulfide in new particle formation in the pristine marine boundary layer
abstract: New particle formation (NPF) enhances the concentration of cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) over the oceans, thereby affecting the radiative balance and, consequently, Earth's climate. The literature suggest that marine NPF predominantly occurs in the free troposphere, as the extensive surface area of sea spray aerosols and limited precursor gases suppress NPF in the marine boundary layer (MBL). title: Comparable temperatures but different microbiomes: long-term time series exposes seasonally divergent Baltic Sea prokaryotic communities
abstract: Abstract Marine microbiomes exhibit seasonal dynamics in many ocean regions. While we can characterize the biodiversity and composition of ocean microbiomes, we lack a systematic understanding of how environmental drivers shape the seasonal succession of marine microbes. To leverage the pronounced temporal changes in growth conditions in the temperate waters of the Baltic Sea, we here report on dynamics in the prokaryoplankton community over 13 years at the Linnaeus Microbial Observatory (LMO), focusing on both free-living (FL; 0.2–3 μm fraction) and particle-associated (PA; >3 μm fraction) pr

title: Generation and Preservation of Submarine Terraces: Insights From Records Imprinted on the Topography of Dokdo Volcano
abstract: Abstract Marine terraces archive sea‐level and tectonic history, yet their relationship to individual highstands remains contentious. While most studies focus on subaerial terraces in uplifting settings, submerged terraces in subsiding settings are less explored. We develop a 1‐D wave‐erosion model and apply it to Dokdo — a subsiding volcanic island in the East Sea (a semi‐enclosed marginal sea bordered by Russia, Korea, and Japan) — using high‐resolution bathymetry to evaluate terrace generation and preservation. title: Modeling of near-source conditions of alkalinity injection in marine environment for precipitation assessment
abstract: The permanent sequestration of carbon dioxide via Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement offers a promising pathway for large-scale climate mitigation. However, the operational safety of alkaline discharges is contingent upon avoiding secondary calcium carbonate precipitation, which occurs when the seawater aragonite saturation state exceeds critical thresholds. This study investigates the near-field mixing dynamics of bicarbonate-enriched effluents using high-resolution Large Eddy Simulations across various seasonal stratification and buoyancy regimes. title: Plio-Pleistocene Stratigraphy, Paleoenvironments, and Isotope-Derived Water Temperatures at Beeline Quarry, Orange County, Florida, U.S.A.
abstract: Plio-Pleistocene marine sediments from Florida record glacial-interglacial sea level cycles and the evolution of shallow shelf ecosystems of the Florida Platform. These deposits also provide opportunities to reconstruct coastal ocean temperatures during past interglacial highstands and evaluate long term changes in West Atlantic oceanography. title: Human pressure, habitat heterogeneity and species traits jointly determine the level of dark diversity in coastal fish communities
abstract: Understanding how anthropogenic pressures and environmental gradients shape coastal fish communities is a central question in biogeography and marine conservation. Yet, the set of species expected to occur at a site given ecological conditions but being absent – the so‐called dark diversity – has received far less attention than observed species, even if they hold key information about local extirpations and conservation effectiveness. title: Current knowledge of marine crustaceans in Mauritius and their global importance in a changing climate
abstract: Abstract Marine crustaceans are ecologically and socio-economically important components of coastal and marine ecosystems; however, in Mauritius, knowledge of their biodiversity, functional roles, and responses to climate change remains limited and fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes available information on Mauritian marine crustaceans, with particular emphasis on the class Malacostraca, while identifying key knowledge gaps and research priorities relevant to their ecological importance and climate-change vulnerability at both local and global scales. title: Benthic communities on recent and historical volcanic lava flows of an oceanic island
abstract: Understanding how benthic communities develop on newly formed marine substrates is essential for explaining ecological succession after large natural disturbances. However, different benthic components may respond at different temporal scales. title: Symbiotic interactions and climate change implications of the octocoral microbiome
abstract: Octocorals are vital components of tropical, temperate, and cold-water benthic marine ecosystems. Their associated microbiomes, comprising microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses, are increasingly recognised as central to host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defence. Metagenomics and amplicon sequencing have uncovered taxonomic and functional complexity within these microbial communities, revealing patterns of host specificity and health status, along with seasonality and geographic structuring. title: Assessment of tropical cyclone vulnerability in East Africa coastal areas using a GIS-based Analytic Hierarchy Process: the case of Dar es Salaam Metropolitan City, Tanzania
abstract: Dar es Salaam Metropolitan City, Tanzania, faces an emerging tropical-cyclone threat because of its coastal setting, dense population, low-lying terrain, and uneven adaptive capacity. Using the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change framework, this study assessed vulnerability through 17 indicators grouped under exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. Indicator weights were derived through GIS-based Analytic Hierarchy Process pairwise comparisons, informed by literature and a consensus discussion among three experts in meteorology, agrometeorology, and natural-resource management. abstract: Abstract During a 2023 survey of higher crustacean biodiversity along the reefs of Mayotte, small fish-baited bottle traps were deployed. One of these traps contained a considerable number of a previously unknown amphipod species. Although the specimens were readily recognized as belonging to the superfamily Lysianassoidea Dana, 1849, their assignment to family and genus was initially uncertain. title: Relationships Between Oceanic Primary Production, Human Habitation and Variation in the Life‐History Traits of Coral Reef Fishes Across the Northern Line Islands
abstract: ABSTRACT Biophysical processes associated with large‐scale nearshore oceanographic upwelling can influence coral reef communities by increasing the delivery of nutrient subsidies and food resources to reefs. However, these processes occur alongside anthropogenic activities that may alter ecological patterns across coral reef ecosystems. abstract: The Mw8.8 Kamchatka earthquake occurred offshore southern Kamchatka on July 29, 2025, generating a tsunami that propagated across the Pacific Ocean and produced a measurable sea-level disturbance along the Mexican Pacific coast. In this study, we analyze tide-gauge records along this coast to document the arrival times, duration, maximum wave-heights, and spatial variability of this far-field tsunami. abstract: Organic nitrogen (ON) in marine aerosols is not only an important fraction of atmospheric nitrogen deposition but also a vital contributor to light-absorbing organic aerosols. However, observational evidence is lacking on the driving factors of ON formation or its role in organic aerosol absorption, especially in marine atmosphere. title: Environmental Gradients as a Dominant Force in the Macroevolution of a Host-Associated Marine Bacterium
abstract: Natural selection is imposed by both abiotic environmental filtering and biotic interactions, yet their relative roles in shaping the deep phylogeny of widespread, generalist host-associated bacteria remain unclear. Here, we integrate large-scale phylogenomics, environmental sequencing, functional genomics, and global metagenomic analysis to demonstrate that tidal zonation overrides host association as the dominant macroevolutionary force structuring the marine bacterial genus Ruegeria. abstract: Abstract As coastal communities confront accelerating sea-level rise, planning practice faces a growing tension between preserving heritage and ensuring climate resilience. A critical gap exists regarding how designation practice has hampered the integration of community-defined historic places (sites whose significance is rooted in local narratives, social relationships, working landscapes, and social continuity) into local hazard resilience planning systems. title: Drone-Transect: a non-destructive operational protocol for drone-based conservation studies on intertidal coral reefs
abstract: With many functions attributed to drone use, different applications have been employed along the coastal environment. Most studies have focused on quantifying live and non-live cover, without measuring or quantifying species at the individual level. Thus, we proposed the Drone-Transect method, which, based on aerial images captured by drones, can identify benthic organisms on a broad spatial scale, determining abundance and spatio-temporal distribution. title: Surveying Biodiverse Coral Reef Ecosystems Across the Tree of Life With Environmental DNA
abstract: A central challenge in evaluating biodiversity using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is that each primer set has biases resulting in selective amplification of taxonomic diversity. Here we test 11 primer pairs to assess Central Pacific coral reef diversity in the five kingdoms of marine eukaryotes: Chromista, Fungi, Metazoa, Plantae and Protozoa. Zero-width OTUs (ZOTUs) were compared to public sequence databases and resolved to the finest taxonomic rank possible. abstract: ABSTRACT High‐density polyethylene (HDPE) is widely applied in marine engineering infrastructures, but its service in sustained dynamic impact scenarios is severely constrained by the inherent mismatch among tensile strength, impact toughness, and environmental stress cracking resistance (ESCR). To break through this performance bottleneck, this work develops a synergistically modified HDPE composite using basalt scales (BS) and basalt fibers (BF) as reinforcing phases, paired with a hybrid compatibilizer system of polyethylene‐grafted maleic anhydride (PE‐g‐MAH) and polyolefin elastomer‐graft

abstract: Evidence-informed architectural heritage planning requires a robust understanding of long-term urban morphogenesis. This paper reconstructs the spatial evolution of Bejaia (Bougie), Algeria, from 1833 to 1962 and tests how diachronic Geographic Information System (GIS)-based indicators can substantiate safeguarding priorities in Mediterranean coastal historic centres. title: Is Deep-Sea Mining the New “Green Frontier”? A Corpus-assisted Discourse Analysis of Arguments on the Climate Crisis and Deep-Sea Mining in the Pacific
abstract: With its abundance of minerals identified as essential for the green transition, the ocean floor is regarded by Deep-Sea Mining (DSM) proponents as the new “green frontier” of resource extraction. This framing of DSM is particularly significant for the Pacific Island Countries (PICs), which are positioned at the geographic center of DSM pursuits. title: Wind and turbulence conditions encountered by vessels and wind-assisted propulsion systems at sea
abstract: Time-resolved measurements of the open-ocean marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL) are essential for characterizing wind conditions encountered by wind-assisted propulsion systems (WAPS). A unique dataset obtained using two upward-facing continuous-wave profiling lidars during four trans-Atlantic crossings of a tanker is presented. title: Observational Evidence for Accelerated Warming and Salinification Propagating Into the Deep Mediterranean
abstract: Abstract Acceleration, rather than a gradual linear response, is emerging as a defining feature of ocean change in the Anthropocene. Surface‐forced warming propagates into the deep ocean over decades to centuries, but semi‐enclosed basins such as the Mediterranean Sea may respond more rapidly. Here, we analyse an in situ Mediterranean‐wide multiplatform data set spanning 1950–2025 and show that warming and salinification of the upper 1,000–2,000 m are not only continuing but accelerating, at increasing rates over the record. title: Community-level eDNA decay patterns in marine zooplankton: Implications for optimizing eDNA-based marine environmental monitoring
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has the potential to greatly transform marine ecological monitoring, yet its capacity for accurate biodiversity estimates is constrained by its decay process. Previous research has largely focused on laboratory-cultured single species, and thus the dynamics of mixed-species eDNA from natural communities remain poorly understood. title: Mitigating the impacts of oligotrophication and thermal stress on Pacific oyster Magallana gigas aquaculture through solar-powered artificial upwelling
abstract: Abstract Recent oligotrophication and rising water temperatures in the Seto Inland Sea of Japan have led to a decline in oyster production in Hiroshima Prefecture. This study developed and evaluated the “Seawater Pump-up Apparatus for Localized Oceanic Warming-mitigation” (SPALOW), a device designed to supply cool and nutrient-rich bottom water and diatom resting cells from the sediment to the surface layer. title: Identifying Optimal Hiking Locations Using a GIS-Based Suitability Model
abstract: The growth of ecotourism and hiking is one pillar of Saudi Vision 2030. However, the Kingdom lacks an up-to-date national spatial classification that would enable systematic coverage and strategic decision-making on potentially suitable hiking areas. In response, this study developed a GIS-based MCDA framework to classify hiking zones and assess their suitability across mountainous, desert, and coastal environments. title: Ant Diversity of the Xisha Islands: Community Structure, Exotic Species Colonization, and Ecological Functions in a Tropical Coral Archipelago
abstract: ABSTRACT The Xisha Islands in the South China Sea are a typical tropical coral archipelago at the forefront of global climate change and anthropogenic disturbance, yet their ant diversity and ecological functions remain uncharacterized. In this study, we systematically surveyed ants across seven islands, integrating morphological identification with molecular species delimitation (based on COI barcodes, with ABGD, ASAP, and bPTP methods) to compile the species inventory, and analyzed the effects of island geographic traits, anthropogenic disturbance, and vegetation type on ant communities. title: Immersive human–computer interaction simulation and emergency buoyancy control of submerged body in the South China Sea internal solitary wave
abstract: Oceanic internal solitary waves (ISWs) produce strong nonlinear variations in density stratification and flow fields, posing considerable risks to submerged body navigation. In this study, high-resolution ISW data in the South China Sea were simulated using the Massachusetts Institute of Technology General Circulation Model (MITgcm), and a continuous three-dimensional visualization of ISWs was developed based on isopycnal depth extraction. title: Ecosystem management analysis study in tourist villages
abstract: Background: Arborek Island (8.2 ha), within Raja Ampat's Dampier Strait Marine Protected Area, is a global hub for community-based marine ecotourism and rich biodiversity. Surging tourism imposes acute socio-ecological pressures on fragile habitats and threatened megafauna (Mobula alfredi, Chelonia mydas), exposing vulnerabilities inherent to small-island systems. title: Hidden Ecosystems of an Endangered Giant: Microbiomes of Leatherback Sea Turtles
abstract: Abstract The leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) is a migratory, globally endangered marine species whose associated microbiota remain understudied. Characterizing these communities may inform animal health and conservation. We hypothesized that different turtle body sites and nests host distinct microbial communities. abstract: ABSTRACT Uranium extraction from seawater represents a vital route for exploring non‐conventional uranium resources. Enhancing the mass transfer performance and antifouling capabilities, and constructing synergistic promotion are crucial for improving adsorption efficiency and durability of uranium extraction materials in large‐scale marine tests. Herein, a novel adsorbent PAO‐G‐SBMA was developed by introducing zwitterion and polyguanidine groups into polyamidoxime fibers. abstract: We propose a continuous multidimensional multispecies model of planktonic cell invasion in phototrophic biofilms that incorporates phototaxis as a key mechanism driving directed movement along light gradients. The biofilm is modeled as a homogeneous, viscous, incompressible fluid, with the velocity field governed by a Darcy-type law. title: Amphipoda (Crustacea, Peracarida) associated with the octocoral Carijoa riisei (Cnidaria, Anthozoa) in estuarine and reef environments of northeastern Brazil
abstract: Carijoa riisei is a branching colonial octocoral widely distributed in reef and estuarine environments along the coast of Pernambuco, northeastern Brazil. Owing to the structural complexity of its colonies, it provides both habitat and substrate for a diverse assemblage of associated organisms. This study investigated the structure of the amphipod community associated with C. riisei in two contrasting environments on the southern coast of Pernambuco: Porto de Galinhas Beach and the Rio Formoso Estuary. title: Respiratory virology dashboards for primary care and public health insight in England
abstract: BACKGROUND: Effective community surveillance of respiratory diseases relies on the timely collection and analysis of high quality clinical and virology data. The aim was to develop interactive dashboards for general practice, public health, and researcher groups. This would improve the visualisation, utilisation, and quality of virology data from an English sentinel network, support disease trend monitoring, early outbreak response, and thereby reduce poor health outcomes and their societal impact. title: Bathymetric structuring of scavenging amphipods in two sub-Arctic fjords
abstract: Abstract The removal of carcasses and consequently recycling of organic matter from food falls depends on a variety of benthic scavenging species in marine ecosystems. Amphipods, more specifically lysianassids, are among the most important scavengers in the deep sea and coastal habitats. Arctic coastal waters were found to have a highly diverse amphipod community, while very little is known about the lysianassid distribution and species composition in sub-Arctic ecosystems. title: The Carbonate Raman Processing and Plotting Tool: A Software Application for 2‐Dimensional Raman Image Peak‐Fitting and Visualization
abstract: ABSTRACT We present the Carbonate Raman Processing and Plotting tool (CaRPP), designed to perform peak‐fitting and visualization on two‐dimensional Raman maps of calcium carbonate specimens. The CaRPP software enhances transparency and image‐processing capabilities specific to carbonates compared to existing alternatives. Although designed for visualizing peak width and wave number spatial patterns in the shells and skeletons of marine calcifying organisms, CaRPP has potential to be used for Raman spectra peak‐fitting and plotting on a wider range of sample types.

title: Flood Risk Assessment and Environmental Change Analysis Using GIS and Remote Sensing
abstract: Floods can be very destructive natural hazard; it causes significant environmental, social, and economic impacts. Havza is a district in Northern part of Türkiye, experienced major flood events in May 1998 and May 2026, which emphasize the need of identify flood-prone areas and analyze the factors that influence flood vulnerability. title: Dynamic emperor penguin colonies
abstract: Abstract Understanding how species respond to environmental change is critical for predicting their resilience to future climate impacts. For emperor penguins, relocation of breeding colonies may provide an important mechanism for coping with changing sea ice conditions. Using medium and very high-resolution satellite imagery, we study penguin colony locations in West Antarctica and show that five colonies have moved significant distances over the last decade. title: The contribution of marine benthic habitats for maintaining fish biodiversity
abstract: Abstract Elucidating how biodiversity is distributed across marine habitats is essential to guide conservation efforts at a time of unprecedented anthropogenic impacts. However, the relative importance of different benthic habitats for maintaining fish biodiversity remains unclear because studies have typically focused on a single marine substrate. title: Salinity challenges and community adaptation: insights from coastal Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract Rising sea levels and increasing cyclone intensity are exacerbating salinity problems in coastal regions globally, threatening freshwater availability and public health. To address gaps in understanding community adaptation, we employed a multi-faceted approach comprising meta-analysis, water testing, surveys, focus group discussions (FGDs) and key informant interviews (KIIs) to: ( i ) examine rainwater harvesting trends, ( ii ) assess stored rainwater quality, and ( iii ) investigate community practices, perceptions, and health outcomes in coastal Bangladesh. title: Sensing a Changing Tide: Community‐Based Monitoring and Collaborative Governance in Mexico’s Small‐Scale Fisheries
abstract: This article examines how small-scale fishing cooperatives on Mexico’s northern Pacific coast integrate technologies into community-based marine governance. Drawing on ethnographic research with cooperatives in Baja California Sur, it asks how oceanographic sensors are used, adapted, and made meaningful in citizen science and co-constructed governance practices, and what that reveals about empowerment and blue justice in coastal communities. title: Lithochloron , a new genus of green algae residing in coral skeleton (Cladophorales, Chlorophyta)
abstract: Coral skeletons host diverse microbial communities, including endolithic green algae that contribute to holobiont functioning. The siphonous green alga Ostreobium (Bryopsidales) is arguably the best-known coral endolith, but recent environmental sequencing has indicated that other lineages of green algae may also inhabit the coral skeleton, including members of the Cladophorales. abstract: The capacity for governance is a critical factor that influences the success of implementing public policy. However, studies focusing on the capacity for governance in relation to the development of blue economy development policies are scarce. A previous research has mainly been conducted on the topics of climate change, urban issues, and covid-19, while blue economy research has mainly focused on economic and environmental aspects. abstract: Halocynthia papillosa is one of the most common ascidians inhabiting coralligenous and sciaphilic benthic communities on Mediterranean rocky bottoms. Despite its ecological relevance, its broad-scale distribution patterns and environmental drivers remain poorly understood. This study investigates the spatial and bathymetric distribution of H. papillosa along the Ligurian coast (NW Mediterranean Sea) using standardized ROV video surveys conducted between 2015 and 2025 in 37 sites located at 40–100 m depth. abstract: Abstract Corals with rapidly progressing tissue loss marginated by a brown band on exposed skeleton are typically given a field diagnosis of brown band disease (BrB). It is associated with scuticociliates, protists capable of causing epidemic mortality in a wide range of marine organisms, but with uncertain pathogenic role in BrB. title: Profile-wide desalinization is associated with increased deep-soil microbial biomass and reduced iron-bound carbon in coastal wetland restoration
abstract: Tillage- and mulching-based interventions are increasingly used to control invasive plants and modify soil hydro-salinity, but their effects on subsoil carbon (C) stabilization are poorly quantified. We conducted an 18-month field experiment in a Spartina alterniflora–invaded estuarine wetland to compare plastic mulching (PM) and deep tillage (DT) and to resolve microbial–mineral controls on C across the 0–100 cm profile. title: Immersive geospatial learning for flood disaster education: Integrating GIS, augmented reality, spatial literacy, and ecopedagogy
abstract: Flood disasters remain a recurring challenge in many regions and underscore the importance of educational approaches that help students understand environmental risks and develop preparedness capacities. Although Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Augmented Reality (AR), spatial literacy, and environmental learning have gained increasing attention in disaster education, these elements are often implemented independently, limiting opportunities for more integrated learning experiences. title: Population structure and gene flow in the endangered Caribbean reef-building coral, Acropora palmata
abstract: Abstract Populations of the Caribbean reef-building coral, Acropora palmata , have declined sharply since their genetic structure was first characterized in the early 2000s. Previous analyses comprehensively sampled coral colonies across the Caribbean and western North Atlantic but genomic resolution was limited by the number of loci assayed. title: Waterbirds of Atrangarai Estuary, Southeastern India: A First Baseline Assessment with Emphasis on Breeding Waterbirds at a Traditional Fishing Center
abstract: Estuarine ecosystems provide important feeding, roosting and breeding habitats for waterbirds, yet many smaller coastal wetlands remain poorly documented. Atrangarai Estuary, a traditional fishing center on the southeastern coast of India, has received no systematic ornithological attention. We conducted monthly surveys (August 2025 to July 2026) to document the composition, richness, abundance and breeding activity of waterbirds. title: Public support for establishing marine protected areas: an Italian case study
abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are management tools aimed at protecting and restoring marine ecosystems and promoting the sustainability of social-ecological systems. Their success, however, depends on stakeholders’ relationships with marine resources and on the quality of the governance processes through which MPAs are designed, calling for research on stakeholders’ perceptions of MPAs long before they are established. abstract: The evolution of distinct reproductive strategies within the same species can offer unique insights into adaptive divergence. Since the discovery of European flounder (Platichthys flesus) in the freshwater environment of the isolated Lake Pulmanki in the 1970s, the evolutionary origin and reproductive strategy of this euryhaline fish has remained a mystery. abstract: Soil fertility assessment is fundamental for sustainable land management and precision agriculture, particularly in semi-arid regions where soil properties exhibit considerable spatial variability. This study investigated the spatial distribution of major soil fertility indicators across Banaskantha district, Gujarat, India, using a systematic 15 × 15 km grid-based sampling approach integrated with Geographic Information System (GIS) analysis and multivariate statistics. abstract: Satellite observations can extend benthic biodiversity monitoring beyond sparse point surveys, but their value depends on robust field validation and transparent uncertainty. abstract: Abstract Introduction Mediterranean coastal wetlands are biodiversity hotspots increasingly threatened by climate change, particularly by salinization, which strongly constrains plant recruitment during early life stages. abstract: Abstract Post-fledging periods represent one of the most vulnerable stages for juvenile seabirds. Adélie penguins Pygoscelis adeliae must quickly develop foraging skills while minimizing predation risk immediately after fledging. In the Antarctic Peninsula (AP) region, where populations are declining, previous studies have suggested that an acute post-fledging survival bottleneck exists. title: Futurities: human extinction, space visualization and the other side of sustainability
abstract: This paper explores how speculative practices engage with evolving ideas on human extinction, space cosmology, post-humanism, and sustainability through expanded photography. Focusing on two projects—Here There Are Lions by Ioannis Galanopoulos Papavasileiou and Alien Landscapes by Ioannis Kontos—it examines how these works reframe themes of planetary precarity, space migration, and ecological collapse. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems in the Niger Delta constitute the largest mangrove forest in Africa and provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, coastal protection, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood support for coastal communities. However, these ecosystems have experienced extensive degradation due to oil pollution, deforestation, land-use change, urbanization, and unsustainable resource exploitation. abstract: This study investigates, in a two-dimensional wave flume, how idealized reef-flat roughness and reef-flat length affect the transformation of solitary-wave-induced bores. title: Seasonal water quality assessment and GIS-based pollution mapping of the Brantas River toward sustainable water management and SDG 6
abstract: Abstract The Brantas River is an important freshwater resource supporting domestic, agricultural, industrial, and ecological functions in East Java, Indonesia. Increasing urbanization, industrial expansion, agricultural intensification, and population growth have contributed to substantial environmental pressures on river water quality, creating challenges for sustainable watershed management and Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6) implementation. abstract: The Philippines contributes significantly to marine plastic pollution, yet little is known about microplastics (MPs) in its many estuaries. This study was the first to examine how many MPs are present, where they are located, and what types are present in Brgy. Baybay Sur, Miagao, Iloilo. Surface water samples were collected from three sampling sites: sample site 1 (SP1), sample site 2 (SP2), and sample site 3 (SP3) along the estuary, then separated, and MPs were isolated. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates long-term spatial and temporal rainfall homogeneity, variability, concentration, and trends across northern Bangladesh, a climate-sensitive region where rainfall variability has important implications for water resources and agriculture. Daily rainfall records from eight meteorological stations covering the 42-year period (1982-2023) were analysed. abstract: Parameters that refer to fish existence can be identified by remote sensing techniques using satellite sensor data. Identification of potential fishing zones with the aid of remote sensing technology is a crucial need for the fisher flocks to get profitable catch by less fuel consumption, effort, and time as well. In this study, two different parameters, chlorophyll concentration and sea surface temperature (SST), were taken from satellite-derived data. abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) governs key carbon-cycling processes within coastal and estuarine environments, yet its transport and characteristics are not fully understood. In this study, we investigated depth-dependent patterns of DOM in the Saguenay Fjord (Quebec, Canada), a deep sill-bounded and stratified fjord that receives freshwater inputs from the Saguenay River and saline water intrusions from the St. Lawrence Estuary. title: Analysis of rain-on-grid modeling tools for simulating flood risks in urban-coastal landscapes
abstract: ABSTRACT Floods are increasing globally, causing significant economic strains on cities. This study evaluates the trade-offs between computational efficiency and model accuracy in flood prediction using rain-on-grid approaches. We compared two open-source rain-on-grid models (LISFLOOD-FP and Itzi) with a commercial one (InfoWorks ICM) to assess flood risk for Cambridge, Massachusetts, at spatial resolutions of 1, 3, 5, and 10 m, with and without drainage networks. title: A scenario-based estimate of sediment organic carbon storage in Posidonia oceanica meadows of the Croatian Adriatic
abstract: Coastal vegetated ecosystems are increasingly recognised for their role in long-term carbon sequestration, yet spatially explicit estimates of sediment organic carbon (C org ) stocks remain unavailable for many Mediterranean regions. In the Adriatic Sea, no region-specific sediment carbon core data currently exist, limiting regional blue carbon assessments and their integration into ecosystem-based management. title: Efficient hydrogen peroxide synthesis from seawater via Na- and Pb-codoped SnSe under moderate temperature gradient
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) plays a crucial role in environmental remediation, chemical synthesis, and energy storage. Nevertheless, its industrial production is energy consuming with significant environmental burdens. Here we show a proof-of-concept thermoelectrocatalytic strategy for H2O2 production directly from seawater, driven solely by low-grade waste heat. title: Insult to Injury: Population Impacts of Sublethal Entanglement and Vessel Strikes of Common Bottlenose Dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in Barataria Basin, Louisiana, 2011–2023
abstract: ABSTRACT Human interactions, specifically fishery entanglements (FI) and vessel strikes (VI), threaten marine mammals, including the Barataria Bay Estuarine System (BBE) Stock of common bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ). abstract: This study revisits the uppermost Jurassic-lowermost Cretaceous succession of Serra Gelada (Alicante, SE Spain) based on new field observations and petrographic analyses. abstract: This study investigates the fabrication and performance of hydrophobic nanothermite powders prepared by combining liquid polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) prepolymers with thermite powders in a dispersion medium. abstract: This article presents the results of a study on the distribution and monitoring of the large humpbacked saxaul locust found in saxaul agrophytocenoses of the Southern Aral Sea region. abstract: Facing lithium resource and cost bottlenecks, low-cost and abundant sodium-ion batteries provide an attractive complement for grid storage. abstract: Magmas produced at depth pass through the upper mantle before they form oceanic crust at spreading centers, but the timescales and thermal evolution of magma replenishment remain poorly constrained. title: Development and Web-Based Visualization of a Domain-Specific Semantic Model for Coffee Culture and Production Processes
abstract: The global agricultural supply chain is a complex network with different data silos, complicated cultivation parameters and highly subjective sensory evaluation metrics. Formal knowledge representation is a must, if real semantic interoperability is to be achieved across this multidimensional domain. abstract: Abstract This study proposes a disaggregated modeling approach to estimate building-level demolition probabilities and project future material output. Many existing Material Stock and Flow Analysis (MSFA) studies rely on aggregated spatial units at national, prefectural, or municipal levels, which limits their ability to capture intra-urban variation. abstract: We present a comprehensive synthesis of recent developments in methodological approaches to combine experimental and genomic studies of picophytoplankton-virus interactions. abstract: Abstract Key Message In temperate coastal forests in Japan, Lauraceae species, particularly Machilus thunbergii Siebold & Zucc. and Neolitsea sericea (Blume) Koidz., are commonly planted following pine decline. abstract: Green hydrogen produced through renewable-powered alkaline water electrolysis represents a promising pathway toward decarbonization; however, large-scale deployment requires integrated optimization of site selection, electrolyzer operation, and energy system design. abstract: This article reconstructs and analyzes the evolution of sustainability in regional-scale spatial planning in Chile between 1994 and 2021. It identifies four phases of normative evolution, from the first legal frameworks to the incorporation of Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) and recent policies, using a qualitative–quantitative mixed design that combines content analysis of 11 instruments with exploratory visualization through MDS and clustering and inferential testing through PERMANOVA. abstract: Bacteria emit volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that can be targeted for disease detection. Biological olfactory systems have keen senses of smell, can detect VOCs at low concentrations, and are naturally adapted to classifying mixtures of VOCs as odors. Here, we employed locust (Schistocerca americana) olfactory neural circuitry to differentiate biofilm and planktonic cultures of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus using their odors. abstract: ABSTRACT Marine protected areas increasingly depend on social legitimacy, customary authority and community participation, yet the interaction between sense of place and conservation behaviour remains insufficiently understood in small‐island settings. This study examined how place attachment, place dependence, place identity, perceived Tara Bandu effectiveness and co‐management satisfaction were associated with conservation behaviour in Beloi Village, Atauro Island, Timor‐Leste. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous contaminants in river-estuary systems but their distribution in the water column vs surface sediments in tropical regions is still poorly understood. The present study aims to investigate the spatial and temporal distribution of MPs abundance and properties in water and surface sediments at the Jawi River–Kakap Estuary, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. abstract: Groundwater is one of the most reliable freshwater resources globally, but overexploitation has led to declining water tables, deteriorating water quality, and increased water scarcity. These problems have raised serious questions about how sustainable groundwater management can be achieved. abstract: Identifying suitable farmland is crucial for sustainable crop production and enhancing climate resilience in drought-prone regions. abstract: This study investigates how online discourse on sport tourism was structured during the COVID-19 pandemic and reshaped as tourism entered a period of recovery and restructuring. abstract: Hippophae salicifolia D. Don (sea buckthorn) is a valuable medicinal and multipurpose shrub native to the Himalayan region, recognized for its exceptional nutritional, pharmaceutical, and ecological importance. Despite its considerable economic potential, large-scale cultivation in Uttarakhand remains limited due to the lack of standardized propagation techniques and the dioecious nature of the species, which necessitates the maintenance of an appropriate male-to-female plant ratio for successful fruit production. abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, the dynamic behaviors of the generalized (3 + )‐dimensional Kadomtsev‐Petviashvili equation, an important mathematical model for nonlinear wave propagation, are examined through interaction solutions. Using interaction solutions such as breather, two‐wave, and lump periodic solutions, the interactions between the solitary wave solutions of the equation and their dynamic characteristics are analyzed in detail. title: Acoustic assessment of industrial noise generated by operational installations in the RA1K refinery, Skikda (Algeria)
abstract: Industrial noise pollution poses significant occupational and environmental challenges in large petrochemical plants. This study presents an acoustic assessment and GIS-based spatial modelling of noise in the RA1K refinery, Skikda (Algeria). Field measurements using an A-weighted sound level meter were used to determine LAeq (equivalent continuous sound pressure level), LAmax (maximum sound pressure level), and LAmin (minimum sound pressure level) at multiple monitoring locations. title: Quality planting material production, cultivation and harvesting techniques of Sea buckthorn berries with special reference to Uttarakhand Himalaya
abstract: This study investigates the propagation, cultivation, soil management, harvesting, and post-harvest processing techniques of seabuckthorn (Hippophae salicifolia), with particular emphasis on its cultivation potential in the Uttarakhand Himalayas. By integrating traditional knowledge with modern agronomic practices, the research aims to develop efficient and sustainable cultivation strategies for this ecologically and economically important species. title: Effects of mild membrane cleaning and feed temperature on process performance and biofouling microbiome in intermittent membrane distillation process
abstract: This study comprehensively evaluated the process performance and biofouling of microbiomes during intermittent seawater membrane distillation (MD). The intermittent MD process was operated at various feed temperatures (30 °C, 45 °C, 60 °C, and 75 °C) and membrane-cleaning conditions (water flushing and low-level chlorination). The results showed that the MD flux increased with operating temperature; severe fouling was not observed at temperatures below 60 °C, whereas pronounced fouling occurred at 75 °C. title: Reproductive Biology of Bombay Duck (Harpadon nehereus) as a Basis for Sustainable Management in the Malacca Strait
abstract: The Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus), a common bycatch species found in various coastal fisheries, has experienced a global population decline. Studies on its reproductive biology, distinguishing between males and females, are still limited, particularly in the Strait of Malacca. This study aimed to investigate sexual dimorphism in the reproductive biology of H. nehereus, including body length distribution, length-weight relationship, growth pattern and coefficient, condition factor (K), hepatosomatic index (HSI), sex ratio, and gonadal maturity stage (GMS). title: Communicating When Hazards Arrive: Adding Arrival Time Information to Hurricane Hazard Maps
abstract: Hurricane Threats and Impacts (HTI) graphics communicate the spatial extent and severity of tropical cyclone hazards but provide limited information about when hazards will arrive, creating challenges for time-sensitive protective decision-making. We evaluated whether adding arrival time information to redesigned HTI-like graphics improves temporal comprehension, influences risk perception and protective actions, and is perceived as usable. title: Population genomics, demography, and circum-Baltic connectivity of Early Medieval southwestern Finland
abstract: BACKGROUND: Knowledge of Early Medieval Finland (1050-1250 CE) relies primarily on archaeological evidence, as contemporary sources are scarce. The available evidence indicates two distinct cultural-economic zones: coastal and inland. Using newly generated genomic data from 34 ancient individuals alongside modern Finnish genomes, we characterise Late Iron Age and Early Medieval ancestry in southwestern Finland, reconstruct demographic patterns, and place individuals within a circum-Baltic relatedness network. title: Sex-dependent behavioural responses of Palaemon varians to submarine power cable electromagnetic fields
abstract: The expansion of submarine power cables (SPCs) associated with offshore renewable energy is increasing the prevalence of electromagnetic fields (EMFs) in coastal environments. These fields fall within the sensory detection range of many crustaceans, however behavioural consequences, particularly in smaller decapods, remain poorly investigated. The estuarine shrimp Palaemon varians provides an ecologically relevant model for examining behavioural responses to SPC relevant EMF exposure. title: Lithospheric water contribution in geothermal systems of northern Sumatra: Insights from OLWC-based isotope reconstruction and Cl–B–Li geochemistry
abstract: The origin and evolution of fluids in subduction zones are still poorly understood, largely because of the complex interactions between deep lithospheric fluids and meteoric water in the shallow geothermal systems. Therefore, this study aimed to estimate the contribution of lithospheric fluids to geothermal systems in northern Sumatra, Indonesia, using the Ocean-Origin Lithospheric Water Curve (OLWC). title: The marine drug plitidepsin alleviates osteoporosis in estrogen-deficient mice by suppressing ROS-mediated NRF2/HO-1 signaling and osteoclast formation
abstract: Abstract Marine-derived compounds represent an important source of innovative therapeutics owing to their structural diversity and broad bioactivity; however, their potential in osteoporosis therapy remains insufficiently explored. This study investigated the effects of plitidepsin (Pli), a marine-origin cyclic peptide, on osteoclast differentiation and bone loss associated with estrogen deficiency. title: Intergenerational equity in cost-benefit analysis of multifunctional flood adaptation measure: Case study on a superdike project in the Netherlands
abstract: The large uncertainty in sea-level rise projections and long lifetimes of flood adaptation measures can lead to lock-in effects and suboptimal outcomes in the long term. To account for these temporal distributional effects, this study incorporates lock-in and intergenerational equity in a comprehensive cost–benefit analysis. We use a novel approach to quantify the potential switching costs from one adaptation measure to another at the adaptation tipping point. title: Optimal Ratio between Ponds and Mangroves in the Management of Silvofishery in Indramayu Regency
abstract: Communities’ dependence on aquaculture ponds as their main source of livelihood has resulted in the extensive conversion of mangroves, which then becomes a serious concern for the sustainability of coastal areas in Indramayu Regency, West Java. The economic advantages of aquaculture should be in line with the ecological role of mangroves in achieving sustainable silvofishery management. title: Assessment of the Current Sanitary and Technical Condition of Irrigation Reservoirs in Azerbaijan
abstract: The article presents a comprehensive assessment of the current sanitary and technical condition of irrigation reservoirs in Azerbaijan, analyzing the operational characteristics of hydraulic structures, the level of technical deterioration, and the primary risk factors affecting their safe operation. The study aims to determine the condition of reservoirs vital to irrigation systems, identify factors influencing operational reliability, and evaluate the applicability of modern monitoring and management approaches. title: TOS²CA: The Thematic Observation Search, Segmentation, Collation and Analysis System
abstract: Background Thematic Observation Search, Segmentation, Collation and Analysis (TOS 2 CA) is an end-to-end system that allows the user to define, collect, and visualize data relevant to naturally occurring phenomena that can be used for current and future Earth science missions and research. Methods TOS 2 CA is a cloud-native, Python-based software library that allows users to define physical phenomena using a conditional threshold to identify occurrences of them in a dataset, tracking them spatially and temporally, and generating a series of masks for the user. title: Gambierdiscus dokdoensis sp. nov. (Gonyaulacales, Dinophyceae), a new benthic-epiphytic dinoflagellate from Dokdo, Korea: morpholgy and phylogeny
abstract: An epiphytic dinoflagellate belonging to the genus Gambierdiscus was isolated from macroalgae collected around Dokdo, East Sea of Korea, and a clonal culture was established. Morphological characterization revealed anteroposteriorly compressed cells (52.0 ± 3.7 μm in length, 87.4 ± 7.6 μm in width, 80.7 ± 6.1 μm in depth), a thecal plate formula of Po, 3′, 7′′, 6c, 6s, 1p, 5′′′, 2′′′′, a centrally located nucleus, and a distinct 1p plate morphology, including a length-to-width ratio of 1.38 ± 0.08. title: Use of fixed-wing unmanned aerial systems to improve the accuracy of Pacifi c salmon spawning assessments in the water bodies of Kamchatka Krai
abstract: The aim of the work was to modernize methods of Pacific salmon assessment by employing digital aerial photography tools to improve the accuracy of spawning estimates. Working methods included digital photogrammetric processing of aerial photography data from fixed-wing unmanned aerial systems, GIS analysis of spatial data, integration of decoding results into united digital database. Processing of orthophotomaps, vectorization of clusters and spatial distribution of spawners were carried out using specialized software (GIS and photogrammetric packages). title: Surveillance of Mytella strigata using eDNA and local ecological knowledge: implications for management and alternative feed use
abstract: The brackish-water mussel Mytella strigata, native to Central and South America, has recently spread to Asian waters, raising concerns for aquaculture and biodiversity. This study presents a regional assessment along India’s southwest coast, integrating local ecological knowledge (LEK), environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring, and nutritional analysis. Interviews and surveys with fisherfolk in Kerala revealed the species' rapid spread and associated issues, including clogging aquaculture cages, disrupting green mussel and oyster farms, and competing with native clams and mussels. title: Instance segmentation model applied to automated palynofacies area-ratio quantification analysis for black shales of T-OAE
abstract: For the purpose of this study, an instance segmentation pipeline based on the YOLOv26 model was used for automated detection, classification, visualization, and quantitative analysis of palynofacies in black shales from the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event (T-OAE). With the help of the dataset which contained 564 microscopic images and 2964 annotations in four classes amorphous organic matter (AOM), phytoclasts, palynomorphs, and background, the model achieved a mean average precision at 0.5 IoU threshold (mAP@0.5) of 94.1% on segmentation masks, with aggregate precision of 93.1% and recall of 92

abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the in vitro inhibitory activity of different Angelica dahurica-Ligusticum sinense extracts (ethanolic, aqueous, and cold-pressed) against planktonic cells and biofilms of Malassezia furfur. METHODS: Ultra-performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) was used to quantify the major constituents. title: A Global Compilation of Blue Whale Strandings
abstract: ABSTRACT Marine mammal strandings are common occurrences that attract public and scientific interest. Stranding data can provide important information for rarely sighted species, but while regional and national stranding databases do exist in some areas, cross‐database communication and data sharing are limited. Here, we present the first global compilation of blue whale ( Balaenoptera musculus ) strandings based on museum specimens, published research, and unpublished verified sources. title: Post-Flood WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) Crises and Women's Health: A Case Study of District Nowshera, Pakistan
abstract: Climate-induced disasters disproportionately affect vulnerable populations, particularly women in low-and middle-income regions where socio-cultural and infrastructural barriers compound disaster impacts. This study examines the physical, psychological, and reproductive health impacts of the 2022 climate-induced floods on women in District Nowshera, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, and also evaluated community response and coping mechanisms during post-disaster recovery. title: Spatial turnover and bioregional structure of reptile assemblages across Türkiye
abstract: Türkiye represents one of the most important biogeographic transition areas in the Mediterranean Basin, linking Mediterranean, Euro-Siberian, and Irano-Turanian biotas. Owing to its complex topography, climatic heterogeneity, and geological history, the country harbors exceptionally diverse reptile assemblages. However, large-scale quantitative analyses of reptile community structure across Türkiye remain limited. title: Effect of processing and germination on the nutritional and bioactive properties of black amaranth ( Amaranthus hybridus ) cultivated over 2,700 m above sea level in Apurimac
abstract: Black amaranth (Amaranthus hybridus), an Andean pseudocereal, was evaluated to assess the effects of germination, roasting, and cooking on its nutritional profile, protein structure (SDS‒PAGE and FTIR), color, polyphenol content, antioxidant capacity (DPPH and ABTS), and flavonoids. Grains from Atancama and Marcahuasi (Apurimac, Peru) were analyzed using analysis of variance, Tukey's test (p < 0.05), and principal component analysis (PCA). title: Climate change impacts and resilience pathways in somalia through a systematic review
abstract: Somalia is among the most climate-vulnerable countries worldwide, characterized by predominantly arid and semi-arid regions increasingly affected by recurrent droughts, irregular precipitation, rising temperatures, land degradation, and water scarcity, all of which compromise livelihoods, food security, and socio-economic stability. This study addresses the limited synthesis of recent, spatially explicit evidence on climate change impacts in Somalia by bringing together current literature and institutional reports to analyze the effects of climate change and identify adaptation and resilience

title: DNA metabarcoding illuminates nestling diet of the at-risk Western Purple Martin ( Progne subis arboricola )
abstract: The Western Purple Martin (Progne subis arboricola) is an aerial insectivore of conservation concern throughout the Pacific Northwest in the continental USA. In contrast to the widely studied eastern subspecies (Progne subis subis), there is a paucity of information on Western Purple Martin life history and ecology. Aside from anecdotal observations, there is no information on prey use or diet of the Western Purple Martin. title: Photochemical production of ammonium from dissolved organic nitrogen in arctic surface waters
abstract: In sunlit freshwaters, dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) can be degraded photochemically to ammonium (NH4+; photo-production of NH4+). While this NH4+ could be an important source of N to primary and secondary producers, there are too few studies to assess its relative importance in sunlit freshwaters. This study quantified rates and controls of photo-production of NH4+ in ten stream and lake waters in the Alaskan Arctic. title: Biocontrol potential and genomic analysis of novel lytic bacteriophage CABI-SEA 2302 against multidrug-resistant avian pathogenic Escherichia coli associated with colibacillosis
abstract: Multidrug-resistant avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (MDR-APEC) causes critically high first-week mortality in chickens, resulting in substantial economic losses in the global poultry industry. This study aimed to isolate and characterize a novel bacteriophage as an effective safe alternative for the control of colibacillosis. A lytic bacteriophage CABI-SEA 2302 was obtained from E. coli lesion samples collected from commercial poultry farms. title: Rancang Bangun Integrated Ship Water Ballast System
abstract: This study aims to design and develop an Arduino Mega 2560-based Integrated Ship Water Ballast System to improve the monitoring and control of ballast water distribution on a ship prototype. The system integrates A02YYUW ultrasonic sensors to measure water levels in four ballast tanks, an MPU6050 sensor to detect pitch and roll angles, relay modules to control eight ballast pumps, and a web dashboard for real-time monitoring. title: Detection of Heavy Metals from Dry Fish and Evaluation of their Toxic Effects on the Swiss Albino Mice Model
abstract: Sea-dry fish is a popular protein-containing food in Bangladesh. During the processing of dry fish, it can become contaminated with heavy metals, which is a major health concern for humans. The present investigations were carried out to detect selected heavy metals (Nickel, Chromium, Cadmium, Arsenic, and Lead) in three sea dry fish (Churi, Tuna, and Surma), and to evaluate the toxic potential of the dry fish in Swiss albino mice. title: Are PFAS a Problem for Aquatic Life in the Casco Bay Watershed?
abstract: To investigate whether PFAS are a problem for fish and shellfish in the Casco Bay Watershed, staff of Friends of Casco Bay partnered with Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences in East Boothbay to design a study of PFAS levels in waters from below Sebago Lake to outer Casco Bay. title: Impact of Urbanization on Agriculture and Wetland Management in Makurdi LGA of Benue State, Nigeria
abstract: Wetlands are among the most productive ecosystems, providing essential ecological, hydrological, and socio-economic services, including flood regulation, groundwater recharge, water purification, biodiversity conservation, and agricultural support. However, rapid urbanization has accelerated the conversion of wetlands to built-up areas and agricultural land, threatening their ecological integrity. This study assessed the impact of urbanization on agriculture and wetland management in Makurdi Local Government Area, Benue State, over a twenty-year period (2004–2024). title: A field-deployable colorimetric loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay for the point-of-care diagnosis of the mariculture pathogen Photobacterium damselae subsp. damselae
abstract: Photobacterium damselae subsp. damselae (PDD) is a ubiquitous marine pathogen responsible for devastating epizootics in global aquaculture, demanding rapid, point-of-care diagnostic interventions. However, the reliance on sophisticated laboratory infrastructure for nucleic acid purification remains a critical logistical bottleneck. To address this limitation, we engineered a robust field-deployable loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay targeting the PDD-specific ureC locus. title: The biogeography of giant viruses and interactions with Eukaryotes across European lakes
abstract: Abstract Advances in genomics have revealed a diversity of nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (phylum Nucleocytoviricota) that infect eukaryotes, but their ecology beyond the oceans remains poorly understood. We recover 208 Nucleocytoviricota genomes, including 205 putative new species and 33 novel virus-host linkages by sampling 87 lakes spanning 30° of latitude from southern Italy to northern Norway. title: First report on morphometrics, length–weight relationship, feeding habit, and diet composition of Trichopodus trichopterus from Tra Su, An Giang, Vietnam
abstract: Abstract This study aimed to provide preliminary biological data on Trichopodus trichopterus (Pallas, 1770), an ecologically and economically essential freshwater species in the Mekong Delta, focusing on its external morphology, growth pattern, feeding habit, and diet composition. Specimens were collected from Tra Su (An Giang Province) in March 2025 and analyzed in the laboratory. title: Temporal variation in picophytoplankton pigment phenotypes of two urban rivers
abstract: Picophytoplankton are a group of photosynthetic, unicellular organisms, making them key primary producers in aquatic ecosystems. These cells numerically dominate in oceans and lakes where picophytoplankton communities contain phenotypic subpopulations that correspond to biogeographic patterns. In rivers, however, such community dynamics are less studied. title: Bacterial extracellular vesicles as players in biofilm dynamics and community interactions
abstract: The ability to use vesicles to deliver cargo safely across distance is a valuable strategy that appears to be universal across all life. The ability of prokaryotes to accomplish this is a relatively new idea, but one that is expanding rapidly. In this review, we will describe what bacterial extracellular vesicles (bEVs) are and where they come from. title: Genome-wide association analysis reveals SNPs and candidate genes associated with thermal tolerance in the Yesso scallop (Patinopecten yessoensis)
abstract: The Yesso scallop ( Patinopecten yessoensis ) is a commercially important aquaculture species in northern China. However, as a cold-water species, it has been severely impacted by the continuous rise in seawater temperatures caused by global warming. Frequent high summer temperatures have recently triggered mass mortality events of the species, resulting in substantial economic losses. title: SeaMamba: Frequency-Stabilized Selective State-Space Multiscale Detection for SAR Ships in Complex Maritime Scenes
abstract: Ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery remains challenging because near-shore clutter, coherent speckle noise, dense scattering responses, and large target-scale variations often obscure vessel boundaries and weaken small-ship signatures. Although single-stage detectors provide efficient inference, their predominantly local convolutional modeling and fixed multiscale fusion strategies are insufficient for capturing long-range sea-surface context and adaptively emphasizing discriminative ship responses. title: Securing the global digital backbone: trends in international action plans for undersea cable security and resilience
abstract: Undersea cables are essential to global digital connectivity and support cross-border energy transmission. They face accidental risks from anchoring, fishing and environmental hazards, alongside intentional disruption through espionage, sabotage and hybrid coercion. Governments, regional organisations and industry are developing frameworks to strengthen prevention, detection, response, repair and deterrence. title: An ecologically important leopard seal aggregation site in South Bay, Livingston Island
abstract: Abstract Leopard seals ( Hydrurga leptonyx ) are apex predators that shape Southern Ocean food webs through consumption of a wide range of prey. Despite their ecological importance and broad circumpolar distribution, consistent aggregation sites are poorly documented. During the 2025–2026 austral summer, we identified and monitored a previously undocumented aggregation of leopard seals in South Bay, Livingston Island, Antarctica. title: AN INTEGRATED ASSESSMENT OF GROUNDWATER PHYSICOCHEMICAL QUALITY AND LAND USE/LAND COVER DYNAMICS IN THE PENNA RIVER BASIN, YSR KADAPA DISTRICT, INDIA
abstract: Groundwater is a critical component of water security in the semi-arid landscapes of southern India, where seasonal recharge, geology, agriculture and changing land cover can jointly influence water chemistry. This study presents an integrated assessment of groundwater physicochemical characteristics and land use/land cover (LULC) dynamics in the Penna River Basin within YSR Kadapa District, Andhra Pradesh, using the study framework and results developed during the 2022–2026 assessment period. title: Barrier island geomorphic complexity drives storm and post-storm response
abstract: Barrier islands are at the forefront of climate-driven changes, with their resiliency threatened by rapid fluctuations in the physical drivers that shape them. Quantifying magnitudes and directions of storm-driven sediment fluxes and rates and modes of sediment recovery is essential for predicting barrier island trajectories. Yet scarce shoreface observations have limited such efforts. title: Subdued surface expression of deep cave collapse
abstract: Cave systems can be difficult to recognise where karst landforms are subdued or overprinted with other landscape processes. Subtle linear depressions on carbonate platforms are commonly interpreted as fluvial or tectonic landforms, but may also mark collapse above underlying cave systems. We test this on the Nullarbor Plain, southern Australia, a stable >200,000 km² carbonate platform exposed for >14 Myr. title: Strategic summaries: A visual synthesis of Malaysia's hydrogen economy technology roadmap
abstract: National hydrogen roadmaps are substantial strategic documents whose breadth and depth of content can hinder effective communication with key stakeholder groups. A case study based on Malaysia's Hydrogen Economy & Technology Roadmap demonstrates how detailed techno-economic modelling can be distilled into concise visual strategic summaries. title: Geopolitical Risk and Economic Uncertainty in Small Open Economies: Rethinking Resilience in the Caribbean
abstract: The global economic system is undergoing profound transformation, shaped by heightened uncertainty, intensifying geopolitical tensions, economic fragmentation and enduring structural vulnerabilities. Small Island Developing States, particularly those in the Caribbean, are disproportionately exposed to these shifts because of their economic openness, narrow production bases, high import dependence, limited fiscal space and vulnerability to climate-related shocks. Yet within this turbulence lies an opportunity to redefine economic relations, strengthen resilience and diversify pathways to growth

title: Long-term diatom response to anthropogenic stressors in a Neotropical lake
abstract: Understanding tropical lake ecosystem responses to anthropogenic disturbance over long timescales is critical for assessing resistance, resilience, and regime shifts; however, such perspectives are rare in the Neotropics. We combined paleolimnological, limnological, and remote-sensing approaches to evaluate the response of a shallow tropical maar lake in the Sierra de Los Tuxtlas (eastern Mexico) to deforestation-driven disturbance over the last ~200 years, with emphasis on ecosystem trajectories following peak impact in the late twentieth century. title: Nitrogen threshold for successful eelgrass (Zostera marina) restoration in Danish estuaries
abstract: Eutrophication is a major cause of seagrass decline in coastal waters. Limited natural recovery is evident in areas that have experienced a state change, despite reductions in nutrient discharge, due to non-linear recovery trajectories. Assisted recovery can be successful in some locations, but require thorough site-selection, because multiple stressors can hinder restoration. title: From vulnerability to resilience: Understanding social responses to climate-induced hazards in peri-urban and natural resources-dependent communities – The case of Tanga City in Tanzania
abstract: Over the past two decades, climate change (CC) has been and continues to be considered among the greatest challenges of our time. Its escalating risks are increasingly evident and more intense, particularly in natural resources-dependent and rapidly growing communities of sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined the interplay of climate-induced hazards, social vulnerability, and adaptation strategies used among communities in peri-urban areas of Tanga City in Tanzania. title: Relationality in civic data investigation: three cases of relational dilemmas
abstract: Abstract Drawing on the construct of relationality — reciprocal relations of answerability between actors – we bring a lens to data literacy for citizenship that centers around the question of how relationality is embedded throughout the data investigation process. title: Carbon Stocks of Urban-Influenced Mangroves of Jamaica, West Indies
abstract: Abstract Mangroves are globally important coastal systems providing numerous ecosystem services. They store large amounts of carbon in their living and non-living parts. Mangroves associated with urbanised areas such as Kingston Harbour, Jamaica are exposed to threats that result in the loss of valuable ecosystem functions, including carbon sequestration. Quantifying carbon stocks is therefore essential both for their valuation and as a baseline for future comparative studies. title: Quantitative assessment of lower eyelid morphology following orbital floor fracture repair
abstract: Introduction Orbital floor fractures are treated using various surgical approaches; however, objective quantitative evaluation of postoperative lower eyelid morphology remains limited. This study assessed approach-specific changes in postoperative eyelid configuration. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 35 patients with orbital floor fractures, including 26 surgically treated and 9 conservatively managed patients.
