abstract: Abstract In California’s Central Valley, a unique science collaborative built around a shared telemetry network has been developed to track and understand the factors affecting the survival and movement of anadromous species such as salmonids and sturgeons throughout their migration to and from the ocean. The Interagency Telemetry Advisory Group (ITAG) gathers scientists from state and federal natural resource management agencies, universities, and consulting companies that work collaboratively to maintain this science program. abstract: Abstract A unique aquaculture practice for masu salmon ( Oncorhynchus masou masou ) has been developed in Miyazaki Prefecture, Japan, in which fish are transferred from seawater (SW) to freshwater (FW) following the SW culture period to extend the shipment season through summer. title: Spatial Analysis of Groundwater Quality and Its Suitability for Drinking Purpose in SARGODHA City
abstract: Groundwater is the principal source of drinking water for Sargodha Tehsil, Punjab, Pakistan, but its quality is increasingly influenced by urbanization, agricultural activities, and changing land-use practices. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive spatial assessment of groundwater quality, evaluate its suitability for drinking, and identify areas vulnerable to potential health risks. abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of an ethnopedagogy-based pop-up book on the beginning reading skills of second-grade students at SDN Padike III. This research was motivated by students’ low beginning reading skills and the limited use of contextual learning media. Previous studies have shown that pop-up books have been widely used to support students’ interest, learning outcomes, and reading skills; however, few studies have specifically integrated local culture into beginning reading instruction. journal: IJGIE (International Journal of Graduate of Islamic Education)

title: CO2-emissions reduction potential of LNG compared with conventional fossil fuels and the influence of port manoeuvres
abstract: This study evaluated the CO 2 -emission reduction potential of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in maritime transport and examined the influence of vessel operational profiles on emissions performance. A roll-on/roll-off passenger case study indicated an estimated 17.07% reduction in CO 2 emissions using LNG relative to conventional-fuel use, which was lower than the 25%–30% reduction reported previously. title: Impact chain driven data management for multi-risk analysis at urban scale
abstract: Urban areas are increasingly exposed to complex multi-hazard dynamics, where interacting events amplify risk across interconnected physical and socio-economic systems. Despite advances in risk assessment, existing approaches often remain hazard-specific, data-intensive, or limited in their ability to integrate diverse vulnerability dimensions. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a data-driven, interoperable multi-risk framework based on the impact chain approach. title: Bibliometric Analysis of CRM Practices and Their Descendants: Impact on Business Outcomes and Strategic Development
abstract: The current research The current research performs a bibliometric analysis of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) practices and their offspring, looking at their contributions to business performance and strategic formation. Based on data obtained from the Scopus database, it provides an extensive view of the scholarly environment, identifying primary trends, popular studies, and upcoming themes in CRM. title: Soil Salinization Characteristics and Multi-factor Risk Assessment in an Arid Lakeshore Zone: A Case Study of Chaiwopu Lake, Xinjiang, China
abstract: Drylands are highly vulnerable to salt accumulation, particularly near shrinking inland water bodies where strong evaporation, shallow groundwater, and terrain interact. To quantify this process, 39 surface samples (0–20 cm) were collected from a 94.18 km² belt surrounding Chaiwopu Lake, and nine indicators—ESP, pH, slope, aspect, distance to the lake, groundwater-level decline, Simpson’s diversity index, vegetation coverage, and elevation—were integrated into a composite index. title: Enhanced production of phomapyrrolidone a through culture-condition optimization and morphological regulation in Didymella sp. FATR0054
abstract: Phomapyrrolidone A (Ppd A) is a hirsutellone-type macrocyclic alkaloid derived from marine fungi, exhibiting significant activity against triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, its low fermentation yield has limited further drug development. This study established a systematic optimization strategy integrating medium optimization, mycelial morphology regulation, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to enhance Ppd A production by the marine-derived filamentous fungus Didymella sp. title: From the Ancient Tethys to Modern Mountain Springs: A New Operculum‐Projection‐Bearing Family of Truncatelloidea
abstract: ABSTRACT The superfamily Truncatelloidea represents one of the most diverse radiations among microgastropods, yet its systematics remains challenging due to extensive morphological homoplasy and small body size. Yunnan Province in south‐western China, located at the intersection of three global biodiversity hotspots, is known for its high endemism of freshwater truncatelloideans. abstract: Sediment samples were collected and analysed for microplastic concentrations and identification in the Almendares River, both upstream and at the river mouth, and in Havana Harbour. title: Architectural Strategies and the Challenges of Pluvial Flooding in Port Harcourt Metropolis
abstract: The study examined Architectural Strategies and the Challenges of Pluvial Flooding in Port Harcourt Metropolis. The methodology integrates both primary and secondary data sources. With a population of 1,416, a sample frame of 708, and a sample size of 512 determined using the Taro Yamane method, the study employed field observations, surveys, and statistical analysis, including descriptive statistics. title: A multi-omics approach reveals molecular alterations in the digestive gland of Mytilus galloprovincialis following fluoxetine exposure
abstract: Antidepressant consumption has increased markedly in recent years, a trend further amplified by the COVID-19 pandemic. Among these compounds, fluoxetine (FLX), a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), is one of the most widely prescribed worldwide. Although the effects of FLX on aquatic organisms are well documented, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain insufficiently understood and are essential for a comprehensive assessment of its environmental impact. title: Land Use and Land Cover Dynamics and Environmental Impacts in Garanduwa Lagoon, Weligama, Sri Lanka (2013–2023)
abstract: Garanduwa Lagoon, located within the Weligama Divisional Secretariat in southern Sri Lanka, is one of the remaining ancient mangrove ecosystems and holds significant ecological and cultural value within the locality. However, increasing human activities and unplanned land use changes have threatened the sustainability of the lagoon ecosystem, yet limited research has been conducted to monitor these changes over time. title: Improving preschool children’s understanding of water pollution through experiential learning
abstract: Water pollution is a major environmental challenge with important implications for sustainability, public health, and environmental education. This study explored how an experiential learning program was associated with preschool children’s understanding of water pollution in a developmentally appropriate way. The study was conducted over a two-week period in a public kindergarten in Greece and involved 18 children aged 4 to 6 years. title: Spatial–temporal distribution characteristics and influencing factors of immovable cultural heritage in Jiangxi Province, China
abstract: Immovable cultural heritage (IMCH) constitutes a vital material record of human civilization and represents a precious asset shared by all humanity. This study integrates Geographic Information System (GIS) spatial analysis and the Geodetector model, taking 1,032 IMCH sites in Jiangxi Province as the research object, to systematically investigate their spatiotemporal distribution characteristics and driving factors, and on this basis proposes strategies for their conservation and sustainable development. title: Spatio-Temporal Dynamics and Variability of Rainfall in North-Western Rajasthan, India (1991–2024)
abstract: In this research, the spatial and temporal distribution of annual rainfall in North-Western Rajasthan is studied between 1991 and 2024 based on the Climate Hazards InfraRed Precipitation with Station (CHIRPS) v2.0 rainfall data and GIS technology. Annual rainfall data was analyzed through QGIS and Microsoft Excel was used for tabulating and plotting of statistical graphics. title: Distribution and preservation of Kimberella quadrata from the Ediacara Member, South Australia
abstract: The fossil Kimberella quadrata is one of the most morphologically complex members of the soft-bodied Ediacara Biota. Kimberella and its trace fossil, Kimberichnus teruzzii, are largely known from the White Sea region of Russia, where Kimberella occurs abundantly. Kimberella occurs rarely in the Flinders Ranges area of South Australia, previously identified almost exclusively from float material. abstract: Microplastics (MPs), nanoplastics (NPs), and engineered nanoparticles (ENPs) are increasingly recognized as interconnected contaminants in wastewater treatment systems and receiving environments. This review examines their occurrence, interactions, treatment performance, transport pathways, persistence, and ecotoxicological implications, with emphasis on evidence from primary studies. abstract: Mobulidae are large filter-feeding cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) that migrate in the world's oceans. However, how their skeletal tissues have adapted to varying environments remains poorly understood. abstract: This study examines how visitors describe their travel motivations, destination experiences, and practical concerns in online reviews of Demre, Antalya. The researchers organized 210 unique TripAdvisor reviews, posted between 1 January 2021 and 1 July 2026 across five attraction groups, in a structured analytical matrix; stated visits range from 2020 to 2026. abstract: Abstract Between 1937 and 1940, a team of Mexican archaeologists led by Alfonso Caso excavated at Monte Negro, a defensible mountaintop settlement in western Oaxaca. Their foundational insights into the Late Formative period (ca. 300–100 BC) were later augmented by surveys and excavations in other valleys of western Oaxaca, which revealed the emergence of contemporaneous hilltop centers. abstract: Saudi Arabia's rapid development of remote coastal, desert and heritage tourism destinations create a distinctive pediatric emergency preparedness challenge. Children differ from adults in airway anatomy, physiology, medication dosing, equipment needs, communication and psychosocial response; low-frequency, high-acuity events can therefore expose serious capability gaps in isolated facilities. abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of acute oral hemorrhage in emergency settings is frequently complicated by saliva, high vascularity, and microbial presence. This scoping review maps the emerging field of multifunctional, dental-inspired biomaterials. abstract: Aquacultural industry is undergoing a shift in salmon production with the emergence of land-based recirculated aquaculture systems (RAS). The use of RAS has the potential to farm salmon on land in a sustainable and intensive way, which largely reduces the direct negative impact on marine and wild stock. abstract: Abstract The formation of Candida albicans biofilms is a key factor contributing to clinical antifungal treatment failure and multidrug resistance (MDR). Overcoming biofilm formation is an urgent priority in antifungal therapy. Here, we report a synergistic strategy utilizing farnesol (FAR) combined with berberine (BBR) to inhibit Candida albicans biofilms. title: Spatializing Simdogihaeng travelogue (1906): place recognition and heritage authorization on Ganghwa Island
abstract: In the early 20th century, Go Jae-hyung authored Simdogihaeng, a travelogue focusing on Ganghwa Island. This study explores the narratives in Simdogihaeng, leveraging theories of cognition and literature as its theoretical foundation. abstract: X-ray Computed tomography (CT) is increasingly used to estimate ice contents in permafrost samples. In this study, CT-derived estimates of volumetric ice content obtained from medical CT scans were compared with laboratory measurements for 261 samples from northern Canada (Nunavut and Yukon). title: The Evolution of Environmental Impact Assessment and its Contribution to Sustainability
abstract: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) has emerged as a fundamental instrument in environmental planning and decision-making processes across the globe. It provides a structured and systematic approach for identifying, predicting, and evaluating the potential environmental, social, and economic impacts of proposed development activities prior to their implementation. This review paper examines the current state of the art in Environmental Impact Assessment by tracing its historical evolution, reviewing contemporary methodologies, and analyzing its application across various development sectors.

abstract: Endoscopic band ligation (EBL) is performed for hemostasis in patients with colonic diverticular bleeding (CDB) due to its low rebleeding rate. abstract: Understanding when and why species loss affects community function in natural communities remains an open question in ecology. Recent cross‐system analyses have shown that functional dominance is associated with whether species loss matters: in communities dominated by few high‐performing species, lost species contribute little to function. abstract: Land suitability evaluation is crucial for sustainable plantation development, particularly in transmigration areas designated as emerging regional economic growth centers. These areas often exhibit heterogeneous land characteristics and management constraints that may limit agricultural productivity. This study assessed the actual and potential land suitability of three major plantation commodities: coffee, oil palm and rubber in the Padang Ulak Tanding Transmigration Area, Bengkulu Province, Indonesia. abstract: ABSTRACT Unraveling the regulation of electrode local geometric curvature on bubble dynamics is essential to mitigate mass transport losses for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). abstract: The genus Graptacme Pilsbry & Sharp, 1897 comprises 18 species worldwide, six of which occur in Brazil. Among them, only Graptacme obtura Fogarolli & Simone, 2024 is endemic to the country. abstract: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of a LoRa-based vehicle tracking system, emphasizing its hardware architecture and field performance. abstract: This study presents a high-resolution reconstruction of Marine Isotope Stage 5 (MIS 5; 129–71 ka BP) vegetation dynamics from Girraween Lagoon in northern Australia's Top End, highlighting the central role of non-eucalypt taxa in shaping savanna structure and function. abstract: Picosynechococcus sp. strain NKBG15041c is a cyanobacterium isolated from the ocean and while it is known for rapid growth, the basis of its high proliferation capacity remains unclear. abstract: Traditional literature reviews rely on selective reading and thematic categorization, a process that is both time-consuming and prone to subjective bias. abstract: The Malang–Batu corridor is a high-volume tourism system in East Java, but economic benefits remain concentrated in large commercial attractions while tourism villages operate as fragmented peripheral destinations. This study formulates a corridor-based integration model that combines smart tourism, community-based tourism (CBT), environmental protection, and cross-regional governance. abstract: Deforestation in the inland regions of West Sulawesi has been increasing alongside the expansion of patchouli plantations and the high dependence of the patchouli oil distillation industry on fuelwood. abstract: Climate change affects agricultural land productivity. This risk is more pronounced in agrarian economies, where land constitutes farmers' primary asset. title: Unveiling pollution of benzophenone and triazine-derived ultraviolet filters in fishing-port sediment: Implications for ecological risk management
abstract: Benzophenone-derived ultraviolet filters (BP-UVFs) and triazine-derived UVFs (TA-UVFs) have garnered important attention in recent years due to their environmental persistence, potential for bioaccumulation, and associated toxicity. However, there is limited understanding of their co-occurrence and ecological risks in fishing port sediments. In this study, ten BP-UVFs and nine TA-UVFs were investigated in 24 fishing port sediments from Northern China (Dalian area). title: Untargeted LC-HRMS/MS and Feature-Based Molecular Networking Reveal Distinct Metabolic Signatures in Edible Dahlia Types
abstract: Abstract Edible flowers represent chemically diverse food matrices whose characterization increasingly relies on advanced metabolomic approaches. This study employed untargeted liquid chromatography–high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) combined with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN) to characterize and differentiate the metabolic profiles of flowers and roots from five edible dahlia types cultivated under organic conditions. title: Improved primary production and gross respiration measurements using the H 2 18 O technique with membrane inlet mass spectrometry and introduction of a small volume–uniform irradiance incubation chamber
abstract: Abstract An improvement in the H 2 18 O technique for phytoplankton gross primary productivity (GPP), net primary productivity (NPP), and gross respiration (GR) is described that reduces cost, labor, and time over the traditional isotope ratio mass spectrometer (IRMS) method. Membrane inlet mass spectrometry (MIMS) was optimized to measure small (3 mL) samples with low isotope enrichment (1% 18 O) and at high analytical precision (~1 per mil). title: Wild-harvested Marphysa madrasi for biosecure aquaculture: nutritional profiling, pathogen screening, and phylogenetic assessment
abstract: Abstract Polychaetes are widely used as high-value aquaculture feed, yet India continues to depend heavily on imported species despite the availability of locally abundant taxa. However, the nutritional potential, biosafety, and taxonomic clarity of indigenous polychaetes remain poorly characterized. This study addresses this gap by assessing the suitability of the underutilized speciesMarphysa madrasi Hutchings, Lavesque, Priscilla, Daffe, Malathi & Glasby, 2020 as a sustainable , locally sourced feed resource for aquaculture. title: Greenhouse Gas Mitigation Potential of Biogas in Boarding Secondary Schools: An Exploratory Multiple-Case Study in Dar es Salaam and Pwani, Tanzania
abstract: Biogas offers a potential pathway for improving institutional cooking-energy systems, organic-waste management and greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation. This exploratory study assessed the theoretical biogas potential and modelled GHG-emission reductions in ten boarding secondary schools in two coastal regions of the United Republic of Tanzania in East Africa, with nine schools included in the comparable mitigation analysis. title: Applications of virtual reality technology throughout the perioperative period in breast cancer patients: a scoping review
abstract: Objective This scoping review aimed to summarize the application status, implementation methods, and effects of virtual reality (VR) technology in the perioperative period of breast cancer patients, so as to provide references for future research and clinical practice. Methods In accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review guidelines, we systematically retrieved and analyzed relevant studies regarding VR technology applications in the perioperative management of breast cancer patients. title: TB-YOLOv8n: an improved YOLOv8n-based model for tip-burn detection in plant factory-grown pakchoi under LED lighting
abstract: Introduction Plant factory-grown pakchoi is prone to tip-burn under high-density cultivation, limited airflow, and rapid growth conditions, which reduces leaf integrity and commercial quality. Image-based detection of small or mild visible tip-burn symptoms remains challenging because the affected regions are usually small, irregularly shaped, low in color contrast, and easily disturbed by red-blue LED lighting, leaf overlap, curled leaf margins, and heart-leaf occlusion. abstract: OBJECTIVE: To build a computational, hypothesis-generating framework that links gut microbiota-related metabolites with osteoporosis (OP) while retaining upstream microbial source and substrate information, and to prioritize candidate host targets, pathways, and modules for subsequent testing. METHODS: Metabolites and human intestinal host targets were obtained from gutMGene and structures from PubChem; candidate targets were predicted with SEA and SwissTargetPrediction, and osteoporosis targets from CTD, GeneCards, and OMIM. title: Do we need a Noah’s Ark to innovate? The value of biodiversity sampling for biomimetics and bioinspiration
abstract: Bioinspiration and biomimetics rely on biological diversity to generate novel design solutions, yet research remains heavily biased toward a small number of well-studied model organisms, often limiting innovation to incremental advances. A major challenge lies in determining how much biodiversity must be sampled to effectively capture the range of morphologies relevant to biological function and extract design principles. title: Assessment of Microplastic Contaminations in African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) From Selected Fish Farms in Awka Metropolis, Anambra State, Nigeria
abstract: This study assessed microplastic contaminations in African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) and water samples from selected fish farms in Awka Metropolis, Anambra State, Nigeria. It also examined the microplastic abundance, particle length, color, morphology, and polymer composition in different fish tissues (gills, intestines, and muscle) and water samples. Microplastic extraction was done using density separation techniques, and polymer identification was conducted using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. title: Channel-scale tidal currents from vessel-mounted ADCP in three navigation channels of the Colombian Pacific: phase-dependent vertical structure and its dissociation from stratification
abstract: Tidal currents in port access channels are usually characterized from single bottom-mounted moorings, yet in bathymetrically heterogeneous channels the vertical structure and asymmetry of the flow can vary along the channel, and vessel-mounted surveys remain underused as a channel-scale alternative. Here we characterize the tidal currents of the navigation channels of Tumaco, Buenaventura, and Málaga bays (Colombian Pacific) from vessel-mounted ADCP surveys carried out between 2020 and 2024 (1.48 million profiles, 18.9 million binned observations), CTD profiles with concurrent CTD–ADCP pairs,

title: Seaweed-associated bacteria from the Gulf of Mannar show prey-lytic and predator-like activity
abstract: Prey-predator interactions are crucial for maintaining the diversity and stability of the ecosystem. In contrast to the extensively studied macropredators, the diversity and ecological significance of the micro-predators remain understudied. The aim of this study was to understand the diversity of bacterial predators and to isolate the predators associated with algal samples collected from the Gulf of Mannar. title: LMDI-Tapio analysis and scenario-based carbon emission reduction pathways for the southern power grid region in China: insights from comparative reference regions
abstract: Decarbonizing regional power systems is essential for achieving China’s carbon-neutrality targets. However, analyses conducted only at the national or provincial level may overlook the functional interdependence among electricity demand, generation structure, and cross-provincial power transfers. This study examines the southern power grid region in China, which includes Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, and Hainan, as an integrated electricity system rather than as a simple geographical or administrative unit. title: Trace-element bioaccumulation in Mytilus sp. from the Mallorquín swamp, Colombia: Association with water physicochemical conditions
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heavy metal exposure remains an important concern for environmental public health. AIM: This study assessed the associations between water physicochemical conditions and trace-element concentrations in Mytilus sp. from the Mallorquín swamp in Barranquilla, Colombia. METHODOLOGY: Water and mussel samples were collected during two sampling periods (S1 and S2), and physicochemical parameters, including pH, temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and redox potential, were measured in situ. title: Examining Trust Among Veterans from Camp Lejeune Exposed to Environmental Toxicants: A Qualitative Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Serving Veterans with military environmental exposures is a top priority of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). This priority is critical for over 1 million Veterans and civilians who were exposed to contaminated drinking water at United States Marine Corps (USMC) Base Camp Lejeune (CL) between 1953 and 1987. Since 2012, VHA has enacted various legislation to provide healthcare coverage and monetary relief for harm caused by water contamination. abstract: Reliable island-scale wave-energy appraisal requires joint assessment of resource magnitude, spectral shape, directionality, persistence, and technology relevance. title: Highlighting the structural complexity of Europe’s leading seafood processing hub: Building a social-ecological network with actor-network theory
abstract: The seafood sector faces multiple challenges that threaten its contribution to food security. For developing effective governance strategies in response to those transformations, this study proposes a theoretical framework grounded in Actor-Network Theory (ANT), applied to the construction of a Social-Ecological Network (SEN), to better understand the structural complexity of the seafood sector SES in Boulogne-sur-Mer, Europe's leading seafood processing hub. Pyrolyzed hydrochar, a promising carbon-rich adsorbent whose performance is subjected by pyrolysis conditions. title: Contemporary challenges of Schistosomiasis mansoni in Brazil: a review of epidemiological indicators, SUS protocols, and control strategies (2010–2026)
abstract: This scientific review analyzes the contemporary epidemiological landscape and public health management of Schistosomiasis mansoni in Brazil for the 2024–2026 triennium. The main objective of this study is to provide multiple diagnostic and environmental engineering dimensions, extending beyond normative official manuals to analyze systemic surveillance vulnerabilities, detection biases, and the chronic morbidity legacy in an aging population. title: Strategic Directions for Cooperation Between Oil and Gas Companies of the Russian Federation and the People's Republic of China in the Context of Decarbonization and Sustainable Development
abstract: Climate regulation is intensifying worldwide, and the resulting energy transition is reshaping the strategic environment for the oil and gas sector. Russia and China are no exception: their bilateral energy relationship has rested for decades on fossil fuel trade, and decarbonization now presents both a structural challenge to that model and an opening for technological and industrial collaboration. title: A blooming dilemma: maintaining access to California crab while managing biotoxin health risks
abstract: The widespread and persistent 2015–16 domoic acid- (DA) producing algal bloom along the US West Coast led to fishery closures, resulting not only in significant economic losses to California’s commercial Dungeness and rock crab fisheries, but also substantial social impacts and disruption throughout the seafood system. The closures highlighted the need to identify and evaluate strategies for managing and building resilience to future blooms to minimize losses of access and impacts to the seafood system while protecting public health. title: Spatial pattern and structural transformation of industrial carbon dioxide emissions in China
abstract: Abstract Industrial carbon emissions are a critical component of China’s carbon peaking and carbon neutrality strategy, yet their long-term spatial evolution and underlying drivers remain insufficiently understood. Using the China City Greenhouse Gas (CCG) dataset and urban statistical data for 2005–2020, this study integrates ArcGIS spatial analysis, standard deviation ellipse modeling, and multiple linear regression to investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics and driving mechanisms of industrial CO 2 emissions across China. title: Two new and unusual species of the genus Fauveliopsis (Annelida: Fauveliopsidae) and first records in coralline environments from the Alacranes Reef National Park, southern Gulf of Mexico
abstract: Fauveliopsidae are a family of small polychaetes, found across bathyal or abyssal bottoms in low abundance, with their occurrence in shallow waters very uncommon. However, examining polychaetes from dead coralline fragments collected at Alacranes Reef National Park in very shallow waters (0.5–1 m depth), we came upon two unusual fauveliopsids, whose morphological characteristics did not match any described species, while also differing significantly from one another. institutions: Instituto de Ciencias del Mar y Limnología

title: Tracing thermal structure and fluid evolution of the Mariana forearc subduction channel and mantle wedge using in situ serpentine δ18O
abstract: Serpentinization in the Mariana forearc controls redox conditions, volatile production, and the energy landscape for subsurface ecosystems, yet the temperatures remain poorly defined. We present in-situ oxygen isotope (δ 18 O, VSMOW) measurements of serpentine from three serpentinite mud volcanoes across the forearc: South Chamorro, Pacman, and the newly discovered trench-proximal Haga’ I Tasi. title: Climate frameworks must better account for river ecosystem responses and feedbacks
abstract: River ecosystems worldwide are increasingly affected by hydroclimatic extremes, global warming, and multiple anthropogenic disturbances. Yet, climate assessment frameworks insufficiently account for changes in river ecosystem functioning, the resulting ecosystem responses, and the associated climate feedbacks. Here, we propose that integrating these processes into climate assessment and mitigation frameworks is essential for reducing carbon budget uncertainties, supporting timely river rejuvenation, and guiding river-inclusive climate action.
institutions: Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology

title: Evaluating short and long-term behavior of two bottlenose dolphins returned to the wild after two years in managed care
abstract: Reintroductions and experimental releases of cetaceans to the wild have had very limited success. While dedicated post-release monitoring was sometimes implemented during the critical first few months or years to determine success or failure, opportunistic long-term monitoring including the use of regional photo-identification catalogs has been rare. title: Methane emissions from penguin colonies reshape the natural greenhouse gas budget
abstract: Natural methane (CH 4 ) emissions remain poorly constrained in polar regions, where biogeochemical driven sources are largely unresolved. Here, we quantified CH 4 emissions from Antarctic chinstrap penguin colonies using spatially resolved chamber measurements combined with UAV-derived mapping of guano patches and colony footprints. Area-weighted fluxes revealed intense emissions from guano-enriched ornithogenic soils and negligible release from surrounding non-guano soils. title: Typifying tiny teeth: A standardized coding system to quantify morphological variation in fish teeth for comparative ecological, evolutionary, and functional morphological studies
abstract: Abstract Teeth play a crucial role in vertebrate ecology as one of the main interfaces between predators and their prey. As the most diverse vertebrates on the planet, and the dominant vertebrate consumers in nearly all aquatic ecosystems, fishes – and their teeth – thus play an important role in evolutionary and ecological dynamics of aquatic systems. Most studies of fish tooth morphology, both extinct and extant, have focused on single or a few closely related taxa, rather than attempting to place those teeth in a wider, cross-taxa morphological framework. title: Using the Vaquita's Acoustic Behavior to Strengthen Priority Conservation Areas
abstract: ABSTRACT The vaquita ( Phocoena sinus ) is an endemic porpoise restricted to the upper Gulf of California, Mexico, with a total range of 4048 km 2 . Using expert elicitation, the number of vaquitas detected in and near the Zero Tolerance Area—a 288 km 2 area within the Vaquita Refuge (1263 km 2 )—was estimated at 7 to 10 individuals in 2025 with 67% probability. This estimate reflects the number of distinct individuals observed and should not be interpreted as the total population size. title: How does thermal stratification restructure zooplankton ecological functions in reservoirs: a hypothesis based on self-organised criticality theory
abstract: To clarify the mechanism by which reservoir thermal stratification influences the succession of zooplankton functional groups, this paper systematically reviews the national and international research progress and future development trends concerning both reservoir thermal stratification and zooplankton functional groups. title: Pb and Cd Accumulation of Avicennia marina Leaves and Roots in the Angke Kapuk Mangrove Protected Forest, Jakarta, Indonesia
abstract: The Angke Kapuk Mangrove Protection Forest (AKMPF) in Jakarta is an urban mangrove area affected by ongoing human-caused pollution. There is little information on how much Pb and Cd accumulate in Avicennia marina tissue, the dominant species there. This study measures Pb and Cd concentrations in the leaves and roots of Avicennia marina and examines whether distance from the shoreline affects metal accumulation. Sampling was conducted from June to August 2022 using three transect plots (20 × 140 m) in two distance zones: within 100 meters of the shoreline and beyond 100 meters of the shoreline.

title: From local hubs to regional impact: harnessing the social and solidarity economy in small-scale fisheries
abstract: Abstract The global 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development calls for more equitable and sustainable pathways by integrating traditional communities into development efforts. Despite these ambitions, challenges persist, as many initiatives, including Social and Solidarity Economy (SSE) businesses, often operate in regional silos with broader transformative potential. Small-scale fisheries (SSF), particularly in the Global South, remain as one of the most affected sectors by economic imbalances and social injustices. title: Transitioning to Renewable Energy in Small Island Developing States: Current Status, Opportunities, Challenges, and Policy Pathways for a Sustainable Future
abstract: Small Island Developing States (SIDS) face disproportionately high energy costs due to heavy reliance on imported fossil fuels for energy and transportation. This dependency exacerbates economic instability, undermines environmental sustainability, and heightens vulnerability to climate change impacts. However, SIDS’ geographic isolation and abundant natural resources including solar, wind, and geothermal energy, position them to leverage renewables for energy security. title: High Strength Steel Fatigue Crack Growth Database for Offshore Renewable Energy Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT High strength steels can reduce costs and carbon emissions in offshore renewable energy, but their effect on structural integrity remains unclear. In welded structures, such as support structures for offshore wind and tidal turbines, fatigue life is dominated by crack growth from flaws at weld toes. Although some fatigue crack growth data for modern high strength steels exist, they are sparse compared to the widely used S355 grade. title: Chain architecture-dependent liquid-like PDMS interfaces for multifunctional antifouling surfaces
abstract: In this work, liquid-like PDMS interfaces with systematically tailored chain architectures were developed to investigate how grafted polymer topology and molecular weight regulate interfacial organization and antifouling performance. By varying chain length, grafting topology, and substrate geometry, we establish correlations among molecular architecture, interfacial homogeneity, surface mobility, and fouling resistance. title: First genomic analysis of Platycopioida and phylogenomics across six copepod orders
abstract: Recent advances in bioinformatics have significantly expanded our understanding of the genetic properties of organisms and have provided valuable insights into their phylogenetic relationships and evolutionary histories. However, molecular phylogenetic studies of the class Copepoda remain limited, and the focus has been mainly on the major taxa, namely Calanoida, Cyclopoida, Harpacticoida and Siphonostomatoida. title: Genomic evidence of mainland-driven invasion without local establishment of pink salmon in Svalbard, Norway
abstract: Abstract Pink salmon ( Oncorhynchus gorbuscha ) has rapidly expanded throughout northern Europe, raising concern that continued warming may enable establishment even in high Arctic ecosystems. Svalbard has experienced increasing occurrences of pink salmon in recent years, yet it remains unclear whether these individuals reflect successful local reproduction or straying from mainland populations. We combined field surveys and population genomics to assess the origin and establishment potential of pink salmon on Svalbard. title: Elucidating the In Vitro Adverse Effect of Functionalized Single‐Walled Carbon Nanotubes Against Breast Cancer Cells at the Proteomics Level
abstract: The tremendous therapeutic potential of carbon-based nanomaterials (CNMs) has been limited by inconsistent data regarding the nanotoxicity assessment. Although a bulk of studies have been performed to assess the in vitro cytotoxicity mechanism of CNMs, the exact factors responsible for the cytotoxicity of CNMs have not been fully understood. title: Testing antimitotic agents to induce diploid gametophytes for the production of sterile triploid sporophytes in sugar kelp (Saccharina latissima)
abstract: Abstract The development of non-reproductive seaweeds could alleviate environmental concerns associated with the upscaling of seaweed aquaculture and the deployment of genetically improved cultivars containing non-local genetic material. However, current means to produce triploids rely on diploid gametophytes retrieved via apospory, a rare and poorly controlled process that may yield gametophytes with unclear sex differentiation. title: Ten rules to increase the usability of earth observation mission datasets
abstract: Abstract Publicly-funded Earth Observation (EO) missions present unprecedented challenges and opportunities for observing our changing planet and applying the knowledge gained to benefit society. As EO mission data continue to grow in volume and complexity, a paradigm shift in how we make that data available and engage data users is required to maximize scientific return and societal benefits through decision making, research support, public safety, and resource management. title: Influence of physicochemical properties on natural radionuclides, heavy metal, and magnetic susceptibility in the sediment of Kerala Coast with statistical approach
abstract: The Kerala coast, notably areas such as Kollam and Chavara, is renowned for its high background radiation levels (HBRAs) due to the presence of monazite-rich black sands. This study presents a comprehensive geochemical, magnetic and radiological evaluation of beach sediments collected from Vellanathuruthu Beach in Kollam district to Thumpoly Beach in Alappuzha district along the Kerala coast, focusing on the impact of physico-chemical parameters for sediment characteristics. title: Evaluating the impact of digestion pre-treatments on microplastics using NIR spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics represent the biggest proportion of plastic residues found in the environment. Their monitoring often requires the elimination of organic matrices through digestion treatments, as these matrices hinder their detection and identification. NIR spectroscopy is a rapid technique for microplastic analysis, however its application to chemically digested particles remain underexplored. title: A sunken ship cargo of 500 bipyramidal bars? Implications for La Tène period iron production and trade along the Danube
abstract: Water is not kind to iron, as demonstrated by the ‘rusty treasure’ uncovered at Deinham in Upper Austria, now revealed as the largest assemblage of bipyramidal iron bars yet found in Europe. While similar bars are generally attributed to the Early Iron Age (eighth–fifth centuries BC), the authors here argue that the Deinham bars are a new variant, radiocarbon dated to the Late Iron Age (fourth–first centuries BC). Discovered in a silted-up branch of the Danube River, the bars were likely lost in a shipwreck, permitting speculation as to the purpose and exchange value of this weighty cargo.

title: The complexity of fish as food and a natural resource in the U.S. Great Lakes region
abstract: The Great Lakes region contains more than 20% of the world’s surface freshwater and supports a culturally, economically, and ecologically significant seafood sector. Yet the dual identity of fisheries—as both food and a managed natural resource—creates a complex landscape for understanding how seafood moves from water to consumer. This study represents one of the first coordinated efforts to map the United States’ Great Lakes seafood value and supply chains. title: Resolving the taxonomic identity of commercially cultivated Korean Pyropia dentata (Bangiophyceae, Rhodophyta): genomic, molecular, morphological, and biogeographic evidence for Pyropia eudentata sp. nov.
abstract: Pyropia dentata is one of the most economically important seaweed species widely cultivated in East Asia, particularly in Korea, known as ‘Gob-Chang Gim.’ Its taxonomic identity has long been obscured by heavy reliance on morphological characters, leading to frequent misidentification. Recently, a study focusing on Japanese populations identified two clades within the Py. dentata complex; however, they were treated as a single species based on the rbcL sequences. title: Stable Isotope Analysis (δ 13 C, δ 15 N and δ 18 O) of Killer Whale Dentine: Evaluating Treatment Methods and Establishing Best Practices
abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale Stable isotope measurements in odontocete teeth can be used to reconstruct lifetime ecology, but some pre‐treatments may introduce bias. Isolating dentine collagen with HCl decalcification, removing the organic matrix or drying dentine prior to the analysis of structural carbonates can introduce unintended variability, limiting comparability among studies and populations. title: Effects of cyclic hydrostatic pressure on the water absorption of polymer matrix solid buoyancy material
abstract: From the perspective of service, the effects of cyclic hydrostatic pressure on the water absorption of polymer-matrix solid buoyancy material (PSBM) are critical for the submarine safety. However, the underlying mechanism has not been fully clarified to date. This work is focused on the performance aging and underlying mechanisms of PSBM under cyclic hydrostatic pressure. title: Challenge from nomenclature changes: the case of ascidian biodiversity
abstract: The stability of biological nomenclature is essential for estimating biodiversity and is ensured by the International Codes for Nomenclature. However, species names change over time due to advances in scientific knowledge and new technologies, such as DNA barcoding. While barcoding has significantly improved species identification, it has also revealed complexes of cryptic species that can only be distinguished using molecular methodologies. title: Fósseis Marinhos do Quaternário do Rio Grande do Sul: Invertebrados
abstract: A Planície Costeira do Rio Grande do Sul (PCRS) possui um rico registro fóssil do Quaternário tardio, que reflete as oscilações climáticas e eustáticas ocorridas nesse período. Fósseis de moluscos (gastrópodes e bivalves), vertebrados e invertebrados marinhos ocorrem em acumulações biodetríticas, conhecidas como “concheiros”, em afloramentos, como o do Arroio Chuí, e em lagoas costeiras. A costa gaúcha apresenta uma configuração única formada por quatro sistemas Laguna-Barreira e por leques aluviais. title: Understanding Community-Level Blocklists in Decentralized Social Media
abstract: Community-level blocklists are key to content moderation practices in decentralized social media. These blocklists enable moderators to prevent other communities, such as those acting in bad faith, from interacting with their own—and, if shared publicly, warn others about communities worth blocking. Prior work has examined blocklists in centralized social media, noting their potential for collective moderation outcomes, but has focused on blocklists as individual-level tools. title: Reliability assessment for an offshore green hydrogen production platform
abstract: For the decarbonization of the current energy supply offshore renewable energy sources are gaining increasing significance. One of the challenges is to transport the produced energy onshore. Because of the increasing capacities of offshore wind farms and their distance to the shore, the losses arising from transporting electricity also increase. Offshore hydrogen production addresses this issue and can serve as a technology to overcome this challenge. Producing hydrogen offshore requires a production platform. title: Why Should Surface Runoff Analysis Become a Permanent Part of the Climate Change Adaptation Strategy for Medium-Sized Cities?
abstract: Climate fluctuations can result in long periods of drought interspersed with short but rapid and intense rainfall events. This feasibility study includes verification of the planning documents for a medium-sized city of Katrineholm (including historical and problematic sites) and Land-use land-cover modeling (LULC). Aim was to identify the best Nature-based Solution (NBS) that could be incorporated into the local adaptation plan for reducing surface runoff and improving retention. title: Assessing the positioning accuracy of channel extracted from DEM: a test of channel offset
abstract: River network extraction from DEMs is crucial for hydrological analysis. While the accuracy of watershed area and river length have been widely tested, spatial positioning accuracy lacks attention. This study develops the Test of Channel Offset (TCO) to assess the positioning errors of extracted river networks. Using Landsat TM interpreted data as reference, TCO was applied to evaluated the accuracy of networks extracted from ASTER DEM (30 m) and SRTM DEM (90 m) in the Hanjiang River Basin. title: Contributions of aquatic organisms to understanding the vertebrate ocular lens
abstract: Aquatic species have played a vital role over the past 200 years in detailing the structure, physiology, development, and evolution of the ocular lens. As a living piece of biological “glass”, the lens must balance the optical demands of transparency and refractive power with the requirements of a metabolically active tissue. title: How Hydromorphological Pressures Co-govern Lake Water Quality in a Mediterranean Environment. A Study for Greek Natural Lakes and Reservoirs
abstract: Hydromorphological (HyMo) conditions are increasingly recognized as key drivers of ecological quality in lakes and reservoirs, yet their role in Mediterranean systems remains poorly understood. We hypothesize that the relations between HyMo (natural or anthropogenic) metrics and quality elements (biological and physicochemical; QEs) could be quantified to benefit lake functioning and ecological quality. abstract: Ammonification is a critical step in nitrogen cycling framework, but the role of molecular heterogeneity within dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) remains elusive. title: From pixels to people: The social footprint of satellite Earth observation in Aotearoa New Zealand and Australia
abstract: Satellite Earth observations from space are transforming the way governments, civil society, and industry respond to planetary sustainability challenges. Yet, these technologies also generate new governance challenges, in space and on Earth. Viewing satellite infrastructure as a relational data assemblage involving a politics of resource use and material impacts, we draw on social impact assessment scholarship and practice to map the social footprint of Earth observation in Aotearoa New Zealand and Australia. title: Occurrence, source identification, and human health risk assessment of potentially toxic elements in freshwater sources used for aquaculture in the Senegal, Gambia, and Casamance river basins
abstract: Freshwater resources in Senegal play a crucial role in drinking water (DW) supply, agriculture, and the rapidly expanding aquaculture sector promoted under the National Sustainable Aquaculture Development Strategy. However, no nationwide assessment has previously investigated potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in freshwater resources supporting aquaculture. title: Climate Risk and Firms' Shadow Relocation: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT Using recruitment big data matched to Chinese listed firms and their subsidiaries, covering 26,439 firm‐year observations from 2014 to 2023, we find that parent firms exposed to higher climate risk rarely relocate their registered locations. Instead, they reallocate employment toward subsidiaries located in lower‐risk regions. We term this adaptive strategy shadow relocation. title: Diflubenzuron persists and impairs behavioral and biochemical responses in the giant freshwater prawn (Macrobrachium rosenbergii)
abstract: The intensive use of insecticides such as diflubenzuron (DFB), although effective for controlling ectoparasites in aquaculture, raises concerns regarding its environmental persistence and sublethal effects on non-target organisms. This study investigated the bioaccumulation, depletion, and sublethal effects of DFB in the freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii , integrating kinetic, biochemical, and behavioral responses. title: Storage treatment and diluent cause inconsistencies in commonly used fluorometric microplate enzyme assays conducted with saltmarsh soils
abstract: Abstract Fluorometric enzyme assays are a tool for determining potential enzyme activity in soils. A wide array of methodological approaches is adopted by different studies, making comparisons difficult. An important consideration is whether assay conditions replicate the environment of the samples or optimize potential enzyme activity. Related is whether buffer or distilled water is used as a diluent when creating the soil slurry used in the assay. title: A review of autonomous and low cost sensor systems for surface water quality monitoring with implications for local decision making
abstract: Preserving water quality has become a critical priority due to the increasing pressure on water resources from population growth, production activities and climate change. This article reviews recent studies on water quality monitoring in lakes, rivers and reservoirs, with a focus on lessons relevant to local decision-making. Using a structured literature review approach, we synthesised and interpreted research on water quality monitoring systems used in aquatic ecosystems affected by eutrophication and turbidity. title: Plastisphere microbial succession and predicted functional responses: a 60-day temporal study in wastewater effluent
abstract: Abstract Although wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) achieve high microplastic removal efficiency, substantial quantities are still discharged, and the long-term dynamics of plastisphere microorganisms on their surfaces and potential impacts on receiving waters remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted a 7-15-30-60-day in situ incubation of microbial communities on five polymers (PVC, PE, PP, PET, PLA) and two natural particles (sawdust, gravel) at a WWTP outfall, integrating absolute quantitative 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, biofilm characterization, and multi-dimensional ecological anal

title: Silence in climate policy: fisheries, policy incentives, and the missing low-carbon transition in Brazil
abstract: Greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation has become a central priority as countries align production systems with climate targets. Because emission reductions depend on regulatory frameworks that translate international commitments into operational measures, legal and policy architecture is decisive for low-carbon transitions. Fisheries, as a fuel-dependent food-producing and income-generating sector, are part of this governance chain, yet remain an overlooked arena for climate policy. title: Thermoeconomic optimization of an ORC system utilizing main engine and cargo oil pump turbine heat
abstract: This study presents a thermoeconomic analysis and a genetic algorithm (GA)-based optimization of a dual-mode Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) system employing R1233zd(E) as the working fluid, designed for waste heat recovery aboard a 116,000 deadweight tonnage (DWT) tanker vessel. The system harnesses waste heat from two distinct operational phases: the main engine during navigation and the cargo oil pump turbines (COPTs) during cargo discharge, a configuration rarely explored in the existing literature. title: Scenario-based evaluation of nutrient pollution control in agricultural drainage ditch–pond systems using the QUAL2K model
abstract: Agricultural drainage ditches are vital for farmland water management but often contribute to nutrient enrichment and downstream eutrophication. In this study, the QUAL2K model was calibrated with 2022 field data and validated using 2023 monitoring results to simulate nitrogen and phosphorus transport under steady-state conditions. title: Analysis of the Implication of Climate Change Policies on Urban Planning and Development in Calabar Metropolis
abstract: All aspects of Nigeria’s development are vulnerable to climate-related stressors. Its natural capital (including land, forests, landscapes, water, and fisheries) and physical capital (including cities, infrastructure, and other kinds of produced capital), as well as its human capital, are highly susceptible to the impact of climate change. Nigeria’s economy and other sectors of development are equally very vulnerable to climate change. title: InaRisk Personal for Critical Thinking and Disaster Resilience in Social Studies Education
abstract: This research investigated the contribution of InaRisk Personal, a location-sensitive disaster-risk application, to senior high school students' critical thinking in social studies-oriented disaster education. The study employed a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control-group design involving 72 Grade XI students at State Senior High School 11 Semarang. title: Lake sediment trace-element and strontium isotope data reveals spatiotemporal changes and anthropogenic influence: Implications for archaeological provenance studies
abstract: Surface waters, non-migrating rodents, plants, and soils are the most common proxies used for the establishment of strontium isotope isoscapes for archaeological investigations. Recent studies have cast doubt about the accuracy of these methods, notably regarding possible agricultural liming contamination on the 87 Sr/ 86 Sr ratio. abstract: Woody taxa encroachment in the Arctic has been widely observed. However, it remains uncertain how plant interactions are affected by such encroachment due to the lack of long-term observational data. Here, we reconstruct plant composition and functional trait turnover during post-glacial woody encroachment using sedimentary ancient DNA from nine lakes in the Siberia-Alaska region. abstract: Abstract Bisphenol A is a chemical widely used in industry and production of various products and has been often detected in surface waters worldwide. There have been few environmental surveys on BPA in surface waters in Iran. This study was conducted to determine BPA concentration in water resources and wastewater treatment plants of eight cities of Khuzestan province during wet and dry seasons and to estimation of potential health risks in terms of non-carcinogenic risks by hazard quotient (HQ) and hazard index (HI). title: Past flow intermittence duration influences microbial and invertebrate community structure and ecological processes after flow resumption
abstract: Intermittent streams represent over half of the global river network and are becoming increasingly prevalent due to climate change and water abstraction. Despite their importance, knowledge of their functioning remains limited, especially in temperate regions. Here, we assessed the effects of past flow intermittence duration on functional processes during the flowing period in two temperate streams of northeastern France, using functional indicators (i.e., organic matter decomposition and primary production) and monitoring aquatic fungal and invertebrate communities. title: Establishing a reference cultivation protocol for systematic characterisation of the Halomonas genus
abstract: Introduction Halomonas species are increasingly recognised as promising next‐generation industrial biotechnology chassis due to their capacity to grow under high-salt, non-sterile conditions, reducing contamination risk and eliminating the need for resource‐intensive sterilisation. Despite this potential, most Halomonas species remain poorly characterised beyond initial isolation, limiting their adoption. title: Microbial communities and ecological functions shift with glacier retreat in the Canadian High Arctic
abstract: Abstract Glaciers are rapidly retreating under climate warming, raising concerns about the loss of unique microbial ecosystems in both glacier ice and forelands. However, the changes in microbial diversity, community structure, and functional traits across the glacier ice-foreland transition remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how glacier retreat shapes bacterial and fungal communities along an ice-foreland chronosequence at the Arklio Glacier on Ellesmere Island, Nunavut, in the High Arctic of Canada. title: Environmental availability and human health risks of Zn and Mn in battery waste assessed by sequential extraction
abstract: Abstract In Brazil, a considerable portion of electronic waste, such as batteries and accumulators, is still discarded with household trash and sent to landfills without sanitary or environmental control. Improper disposal can lead to the accumulation of potentially toxic metals, posing risks to ecosystems and human health. This study evaluated the performance of a modified Bureau Community of Reference sequential extraction protocol applied to battery waste, focusing on the environmental availability of Zn and Mn. title: JuRa: The Juventas Radar on Hera Mission to Probe Internal Structure of Didymos and Dimorphos Asteroids
abstract: JuRa, the Juventas Radar, is the sounding radar of the Hera/ESA mission on cruise to the asteroid Didymos and its moon, Dimorphos. In 2027, it will, for the first time, do direct observation of the internal structure of an asteroid for the benefit of both science and planetary defense. The instrument is a 60 MHz monostatic radar with a 20 MHz bandwidth, operating in full linear polarization, onboard Juventas, a CubeSat that will operate from end of January to end of March 2027, in a sun-synchronous orbit with a radius ranging from 3.3 to 2 km. title: Stable isotopes reveal tissue-specific nutrient assimilation and energy allocation during ovarian maturation in the pink shrimp Farfantepenaeus brasiliensis
abstract: Abstract Stable isotope analysis provides an effective approach for investigating patterns of nutrient assimilation and resource use in aquatic organisms. Dietary assimilation in the pink shrimp Farfantepenaeus brasiliensis was assessed across four ovarian maturation stages using δ 13 C and δ 15 N. Muscle and ovarian tissues from 121 individuals were analysed to estimate the relative contributions of seven dietary source groups—algae, zooplankton, molluscs, crustaceans, fish, bivalves, and polychaetes—using the Bayesian mixing model MixSIAR. title: Occurrence and risk assessment of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in fish from urban rivers in an Asian megacity: Evidence from Dhaka, Bangladesh
abstract: This study presents the first comprehensive assessment of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in frequently consumed freshwater fish from three major urban rivers (Buriganga, Turag, Shitalakkha) surrounding Dhaka, Bangladesh. We analyzed 15 target PFAS using HPLC‑MS/MS in the muscle tissue of 54 samples from three species: Channa punctatus, Heteropneustes fossilis , and Trichogaster fasciata . title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Sclerophytum querciforme Pratt 1903 (Anthozoa: Octocorallia: Sarcophytidae)
abstract: Historically, the taxonomic classification and phylogenetic position of Sclerophytum querciforme, which is primarily delineated by morphological characteristics, have long remained controversial and undergone repeated revisions. In this study, we sequenced and systematically analyzed the complete mitochondrial genome of S. querciforme. The genome is 18,743 bp in length, containing 14 protein-coding genes, two ribosomal RNA genes, and one transfer RNA gene, with the same gene content and order as other species in the genus. title: Zooplankton assemblages, water quality dynamics and molecular characterization of key crustacean taxa in human-impacted selected freshwater lakes of the Gangetic Plain, West Bengal, India
abstract: Freshwater lakes in the Gangetic plain of West Bengal encounter immense pressure due to high population density and intensive human activities, resulting in deterioration of water quality and aquatic biodiversity. Such information is essential for their sustainable management. The present study aimed to evaluate the physicochemical characteristics, crustacean zooplankton community, and molecular characterisation of key taxa from selected freshwater lakes over a period of one year. title: When the impact is not the same everywhere: The need for regionalized characterization factors in the LCA of plastics
abstract: LCA presents important methodological gaps in the impact assessment phase, especially regarding the characterization factors (CF) applied for plastics. The purpose of this article is to identify methodological barriers and opportunities for improvement in the CFs proposed for plastics-related impacts. It discusses the need to advance toward regionalized characterization factors that better reflect the specific environmental, social, and technological conditions of different geographical contexts. abstract: Abstract Transporting hydrogen using pipelines is becoming increasingly relevant in the energy system, yet current cost estimates typically rely on simplistic approaches that overlook region-specific characteristics, leading to potential miscalculation of costs. Here we examine hydrogen pipeline costs by incorporating regional geographical factors, such as land use, topography and existing infrastructure, together with political-economic factors represented through country-specific weighted average costs of capital. title: Assessing the economic viability of mussel on-bottom culture: a comparative analysis of wild and aquaculture seeds in Denmark
abstract: Mussel on-bottom culture, involving the relocation and transplantation of mussel seed to designated seabed areas, is a relatively recent practice in Denmark and has been proposed as a management approach to address pressures such as overfishing and eutrophication. While ecological and biological benefits are well documented, the economic feasibility of this practice remains largely unexplored. This study provides the first economic evaluation of mussel on-bottom culture under alternative seed-sourcing and organizational arrangements, using primary data from Limfjorden, Denmark. title: Dual northward overseas radiation from Japanese islands shaped the phylogeography of North-East Asian tree frog
abstract: The tree frog Dryophytes japonicus has a broad geographic distribution in northeastern Asia, comprising two major genetically divergent clades whose geographic boundary is located within the Japanese mainland. However, the evolutionary and adaptive mechanisms underlying this wide overseas distribution remain unclear. To uncover the phylogeographic history of the species, we conducted comprehensive genetic and reproductive analyses. title: Multiscale dynamics and nonlinear associations of ecological quality in the Hangzhou Bay urban agglomeration, China
abstract: Ecological quality change in rapidly urbanizing regions is spatially heterogeneous, but assessments based on a single analytical scale may obscure local changes and alter the apparent factor importance. This study constructed a 2000–2024 Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) series for the Hangzhou Bay Urban Agglomeration using Google Earth Engine and Landsat imagery. title: Economics of Wind Energy: Markets, Policy, and Investment Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Wind energy is central to energy transitions, but research on its economics remains fragmented across markets, policy, finance, lifecycle costs, and system integration. This review consolidates the field by applying co‐word analysis, Louvain clustering, and tech‐mining emergence metrics to 2448 publications from 2015 to 2025. abstract: The foundational Balinese Hindu philosophy Tri Hita Karana, which emphasizes harmonious relations among the divine (Parahyangan), humanity (Pawongan), and the environment (Palemahan), has long governed Balinese socio-cultural practices, spatial planning, and customary law. However, how this philosophical framework is formalized and translated into the painterly strategies of contemporary fine art remains insufficiently explored. title: Assessing the Stress Responses and Aquaculture Potential of Silver Barb (Barbonymus gonionotus) Under Saline Exposure
abstract: This study evaluated the salinity adaptation capability of silver barb (Barbonymus gonionotus) by examining its physiological and behavioral stress responses under varying saline conditions. abstract: The widespread use of agrochemicals, including pesticides, fertilizers, and plant growth regulators, has substantially increased agricultural productivity, but their indiscriminate application carries serious ecological risks. This review examines the classification, dispersal pathways, and ecological consequences of agrochemical wastes, with a regional focus on Bijnor District, Uttar Pradesh, India. title: Flash floods in traditionally less flood prone areas of southeastern Bangladesh
abstract: The growing threat of climate-driven urban flash floods signifies the need for rapid damage assessment tools. Understanding the impacts of sudden floods on populations and croplands in historically less flood-prone regions is essential for effective risk management. This study highlights the significant impact of the flood event that began on August 20, 2024, affecting three southeastern districts of Bangladesh Noakhali, Feni, and Cumilla that had experienced minimal flooding in the past three decades. title: Incentive-Based Riparian Restoration as A Scalable Model for Agricultural Watershed Compliance
abstract: Riparian buffers, vegetated waterways, streambank stabilization practices, and floodplain reconnection projects collectively constitute the riparian restoration toolkit through which agricultural watershed compliance programs address nonpoint source nitrogen, phosphorus, sediment, and pathogen loadings from cropland and pasture. abstract: Abstract Throughout the Pleistocene, the Levant served as a key land bridge between continents and witnessed repeated hominin dispersals, including the major expansion of modern humans out of Africa. Yet despite this strategic role, the local ecological conditions encountered by hominin populations along the central Levant remain poorly understood. title: Global solidarity? Philanthropic legitimacy, environmental justice, and vulnerabilities in Japanese foundations
abstract: This article examines how Japanese philanthropic foundations define and implement environmental solidarity through a comparative qualitative analysis of the Nippon Foundation, the Sasakawa Peace Foundation, and the Toyota Foundation. Based on institutional documents, interviews, and participant observation, it conceptualizes solidarity as a mode of governance rather than a normative ideal. title: Enhanced nocturnal N 2 O 5 -ClNO 2 chemistry in Delhi under reduced NO conditions
abstract: Nitryl chloride (ClNO 2 ) is an important Cl⚫ precursor, originating from the heterogeneous reactions of dinitrogen pentoxide (N 2 O 5 ) on chloride-containing particles. This N 2 O 5 -ClNO 2 chemical process plays critical roles in chloride activation, nitrate formation, and thus air pollution. Here we present field measurements made in the early springtime of 2023 in Delhi and compare with a previous study conducted during the winter of 2019. title: Differential regulation of ribogenesis genes throughout oogenesis in thicklip grey mullets, Chelon labrosus, preparing the maternal contribution to embryo development
abstract: Oocytes in teleosts undergo complex changes during oogenesis, including the accumulation of ribosomal RNAs and tRNAs needed to support protein synthesis during early embryogenesis. Previous studies show that high levels of 5S rRNA and tRNAs in perinucleolar previtellogenic (PV) oocytes, and the easily calculated 5S rRNA/18S rRNA index, reliably distinguish testes from ovaries, especially when ovaries are in PV. title: Regional signaling controls stem cell-mediated regeneration in an invertebrate chordate
abstract: Many tissues harbor quiescent stem cells that activate after injury, yet how local signals regulate this transition is not well understood. The solitary ascidian Ciona robusta provides a unique model, as bottom body fragments regenerate while upper fragments fail to do so. By comparing these regenerative and non-regenerative contexts, we reveal striking differences in transcriptional dynamics and signaling environments. title: Effect of Microplastics on Water Quality and Oreochromis Niloticus (Nile Tilapia) In Jakara River, Kano State, Nigeria
abstract: Microplastic contamination has emerged as a significant threat to freshwater ecosystems globally, yet data from African water bodies remain critically limited. This study assessed the occurrence of microplastics and their effects on water quality and oxidative stress responses in Oreochromis niloticus from Jakara Reservoir, Kano State, Nigeria. title: A novel multiplex PCR method for the identification of red snapper (Lutjanus purpureus) and detection of multi-species fraud
abstract: Abstract The red snapper ( Lutjanus purpureus ) is a highly valued commercial fish species subject to intense global trade and high rates of economic fraud through species substitution. Traditional DNA barcode approaches, while accurate, are costly and time-consuming for routine regulatory enforcement and industrial food control. To address this methodological limitation, we developed and validated a novel, low-cost forensic multiplex PCR screening assay based on the mitochondrial Cytochrome B (Cytb) gene. title: Quantifying the Spatio-Ecological Context of Urban Nature-Based Solutions Across European Cities
abstract: Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) are increasingly implemented to address urban environmental challenges, yet the surrounding spatial context in which they are embedded may influence the conditions supporting their ecological functioning. This study applied an integrated remote sensing-based spatial diagnostic framework combining Sentinel-2 spectral indices and land-cover composition metrics to characterize and compare the surrounding environments of five NBS sites in Oslo, Riga, Milan, St. Gallen, and Lublin. title: Ecotoxicological Effects of Polyvinyl Chloride Microplastics on Limnodrilus hoffmeisteri Influenced by Key Environmental Parameters
abstract: ABSTRACT The toxicological effects of polyvinyl chloride microplastics (PVC MPs) on Limnodrilus hoffmeisteri have not been reported previously. Thus, in this study, the toxic effects of PVC MPs on L. hoffmeisteri and associated toxicological mechanisms were determined in indoor simulations during exposure for 21 days. title: Tourism Governance and Regional Security in Sebatik–Tawau Border Integration
abstract: Background: The Sebatik–Tawau borderland presents an integration paradox in which intensive social and economic interactions coexist with underdeveloped tourism governance and legal mobility facilitation. Objective: This study examines how tourism governance and regional security shape border integration and formulates an applicable governance framework for the Sebatik–Tawau borderland. Methods: An embedded qualitative case-study design was employed, covering five Indonesian subdistricts on Sebatik Island and Tawau District, Malaysia. title: Ex-situ replication of concrete pore solution: alkali-activated concrete
abstract: This study presents a reliable methodology for simulating the evolving pore chemistry of alkali activated materials. Using ex situ leaching, binder alkali profiles were established, and concrete specimens were characterized over one year under air and water exposures via porosity, ion chromatography, and pH analysis. title: Assessing Current Patterns and Impacts of Climate Change on Water Resources in Leh-Ladakh
abstract: Climate change and global warming have significantly impacted the water cycle and water resources in the Himalayan region. This study focused on the effects of climate change and human intervention on water resources in the Ladakh region over the past decades. Changes in snowfall and glacial patterns, rapid runoff, and erratic rainfall due to changes in the snow season and an increase in temperature have resulted in water scarcity in this area. title: Seasonal variation in microplastic abundance, morphology, polymers, and adsorbed contaminants in wastewater treatment sludges and biosolids
abstract: This study investigated the seasonal impact on microplastic (MP) characteristics and concentration in the sludge streams (primary, secondary (waste activated) and digested) at a municipal wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) in Ontario. MPs were recovered after digestion and density separation of primary, secondary and digested sludge samples and were quantified and characterized (shape, colour, polymer type, and chemical contaminants) using microscopy and FTIR. title: Determinants of behavioral intentions to reduce single-use plastic among Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh using an extended theory of planned behavior model
abstract: Despite the growing recognition of single-use plastic (SUP) pollution as a substantial environmental challenge, there is limited understanding of the behavioral and socio-demographic factors influencing individuals’ intentions to reduce SUP usage, particularly in refugee populations. This study investigated the determinants of behavioral intentions (BI) to reduce SUP usage among the Rohingya refugee population in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, using an extended Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) model. title: The earth above: participatory immersion, transdisciplinarity, and the planetarium as research space
abstract: This article examines experimentation as a defining force in Australian screen production education and research through a practice-led analysis of The Earth Above: A Deep Time View of Australia's Epic History. Emerging from the ARC Centre of Excellence for Australian Biodiversity and Heritage (CABAH) and developed in collaboration with First Nations communities, archaeologists, artists, and technologists, The Earth Above is a fulldome planetarium work that entangles Indigenous knowledge systems with emerging research to narrate Australia's deep time histories. title: Review on the Permian–Triassic Boundary (PTB) in Abadeh (Iran), a Traveling Boundary
abstract: The Permian–Triassic transition along the South Cimmerian margin of the Neotethys in Abadeh (Iran) is built by four successive lithologies/events with apparently no gaps: (1) the stop of the skeletal carbonate factory of the Paratirolites limestone caused by the end-Permian mass extinction event (EPME); (2) replacement of carbonate deposits by the up to 0.3 m thick boundary clay, defining the base of the Elikah Formation; (3) sudden emergence of a sponge-microbial carbonate factory with buildups of ca. 1.6 m, called the microbial unit; (4) a thick succession of platy lime mudstone. title: Taxonomic and Cytogenetic Complexity Complicate Forecasts of Climate-Driven Habitat Change in Rhexia (Melastomataceae)
abstract: Abstract Rhexia (Melastomataceae), a temperate genus composed of 13 species in eastern North America, provides a useful system for evaluating how taxonomic and cytogenetic complexity influence projections of climate-driven habitat change. Ecological niche models (ENMs) incorporating climatic and edaphic variables were used to estimate current and future habitat suitability for diploid, polyploid, and mixed-cytotype species. title: Flight energetics of barn swallows across speeds: high aerodynamic efficiency, but low energy conversion efficiency
abstract: Bird flight conversion efficiency (η) determines the amount of metabolic power (Pmet) transformed into mechanical power (Pmech) to remain aloft, and it is central to understanding animal flight energetics, yet it remains difficult to quantify. Using 13C-labelled sodium bicarbonate (NaBi) and particle image velocimetry (PIV), we measured Pmet and Pmech, respectively, in un-instrumented barn swallows (Hirundo rustica) flying across 7.8 to 13.6 m s-1 in a wind tunnel.
