abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate streamflow measurements are essential for hydrologic monitoring, flood forecasting, and water resource management. Traditional in situ methods, although reliable, are often impractical or unsafe during flood conditions or at inaccessible locations. Image velocimetry techniques offer a potential non‐contact alternative, yet operational adoption has been hindered by the lack of standardized, open‐source tools, particularly for Space–Time Image Velocimetry (STIV). abstract: Most small vessels have been constructed using wood or fiberglass-/carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composite materials. Increasingly, low-pressure polyethylene, or high-density polyethylene (HDPE), has been adopted as an alternative material. It combines enhanced resistance to marine environments with full recyclability, as well as a low density and competitive price. abstract: Although the three anxiety-related items of the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS-3A) are widely used to flag anxiety-related distress, their psychometric performance across perinatal phases remains insufficiently established. We evaluated factor structure, measurement invariance, differential item functioning (DIF), score precision and convergence with Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) thresholds in a nationwide Italian sample of 10,100 individuals (4,410 pregnant; 5,690 postpartum). abstract: Background: Sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEA/SH) constitute serious violations of professional ethics, patient safety, and human rights. abstract: Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare Mill.) is one of the economically important seed spices grown across arid and semi-arid India, and Rajasthan remains its leading producer. title: Aflatoxin contamination in dried fish: Sources, health impacts, Detection, Detoxification, and Control strategies in developing countries
abstract: Aflatoxin contamination in dried fish is a growing food safety concern with significant implications for human and animal health. This review highlights the key factors contributing to aflatoxin contamination in dried fish, including its sources, influencing factors, health impacts, detection methods, and prevention and mitigation strategies. To reduce this uncertainty, we incorporated a fully coupled wetland-hydrology and wetland-methane module into the ICON-XPP Earth-system model and performed a suite of coupled model experiments with prescribed sea surface temperatures spanning 1855–2014. abstract: Abstract This article revisits the debate on the relationship between capitalism and abolition from the perspective of South Asia. abstract: Abstract Microplastic (MP) pollution is an emerging environmental concern that affects aquatic ecosystems worldwide, with rivers acting as important pathways for the transport of plastic debris. This study investigated the concentration and characteristics of MPs in the two main urban rivers of Rasht City, northern Iran: the Zarjub and Goharrood rivers. title: Beyond deception: fighting scams in an age of digital inauthenticity
abstract: Scams are not isolated criminal events but the most damaging expressions of the “Age of Inauthenticity,” in which generative AI, synthetic media, and platformed deception have made fabricating identity, evidence, and trust trivially cheap. We argue that fighting scams requires moving beyond a narrow fraud-detection frame to an interdisciplinary account of how inauthenticity is engineered, why targets comply, what ecosystems sustain the perpetrators, and which interventions can scale. title: Seasonal drivers and infrastructure impacts on dissolved oxygen dynamics in complex environmental systems
abstract: Urban streams are increasingly regulated by the interaction of climate-driven thermal stress and episodic infrastructure disturbances, yet their combined influence on dissolved oxygen (DO) dynamics remains insufficiently resolved across temporal scales. This study quantified the combined effects of temperature, hydrology, and combined sewer overflow (CSO) activity on DO across four urban watersheds in Philadelphia, USA, using 12 years of high-frequency monitoring integrated with precipitation, streamflow, and modeled CSO data. title: From SCADA Pressure to Actionable Alarms: Calibration-Aware Monitoring of Kaplan Turbine Runner-Blade Actuation Friction
abstract: Runner-blade friction and lubrication wear in a Kaplan turbine stay hard to observe directly between costly hub inspections. We introduce KFM-Cal, a unit-adaptive pressure-to-alarm algorithm that converts installed one-minute close/open servo-pressure SCADA into persistent friction and lubrication-risk alarms. title: Health Risk Measurement of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (Pahs) In Barbecue Food “Nile Tilapia” (Oreochromis Niloticus)
abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are harmful compounds produced during the incomplete combustion of fats, particularly when fish is barbecued or grilled. When fat drips onto hot coals, flames, or electric burners, flare-ups occur, leading to PAH formation that can contaminate food and enter the human body through dietary intake. In this study conducted in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. title: Process-dependent wetland degradation and ecological resilience in Northeast China revealed by a zone-weighted regional wetland composite index
abstract: In Northeast China, wetland degradation has intensified under climate change and human activities, disturbing the stability of the system. However, due to the spatial heterogeneity in dominant degradation processes, the applicability of conventional indicators and fixed weighting schemes appears to be limited. title: A source–medium–receiver framework for modeling wind-driven vegetation cooling in urban landscapes
abstract: Vegetation cooling in cities is often represented as a local, isotropic effect, although atmospheric processes can redistribute cooling beyond individual vegetation patches. This simplification may overlook the nonlocal and directionally structured nature of cooling propagation. We developed a physics-guided source–medium–receiver (SMR) framework for the Greater Bay Area of China to compare multi-source isotropic connectivity with prevailing-wind-conditioned connectivity. title: Elliptical trajectories and uncertainty principles in a geometric theory of generalized signal analysis
abstract: Abstract Bivariate signals, representing vector motions in 2D spaces (e.g., oceanography and radar systems), require specialized uncertainty analysis beyond traditional complex signals. This paper introduces the novel uncertainty principles for bivariate signals via quaternion Fourier transform and Hilbert transforms. title: Strong trophic specialization on guanaco within the native prey community -DNA metabarcoding of puma diet in Torres del Paine, Patagonia
abstract: Understanding dietary composition and prey-use patterns of apex predators is fundamental for interpreting predator–prey dynamics and ecosystem functioning. In Patagonia, the diet of the puma ( Puma concolor ) has been described primarily using conventional scat analyses, while molecular approaches offer additional taxonomic resolution for detecting low-frequency prey taxa. Here, we used vertebrate DNA metabarcoding to characterize the native vertebrate component of puma diet in the Cerro Guido–Torres del Paine landscape of southern Chile. title: Integrated Structural Risk Assessment of University Lecture Theatres in Developing Countries: A Case Study of Taraba State University, Nigeria
abstract: This study applies the Integrated Structural Risk Assessment Framework (ISRAF) to all 12 reinforced concrete lecture theatres on the main campus of Taraba State University (TSU), Jalingo, Nigeria. ISRAF is presented as a comprehensive integrated framework adapted to the data constraints of resource-limited university environments in sub-Saharan Africa. title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Forensic Accounting In Reducing Financial Fraud in Nigeria Banking Sector
abstract: This study assesses the effectiveness of forensic accounting in reducing financial fraud in Nigeria’s banking sector. Specifically, it investigates the impact of forensic accounting techniques, tools, and professional expertise on the prevention and detection of financial fraud. The study employed a quantitative research design, using structured questionnaires administered to 81respondents. title: Global research trends on seaweed-based amendments for soil health and crop productivity
abstract: Seaweeds have emerged as pivotal bioresources in sustainable agriculture, bridging the soil–crop–nutrient continuum through their multifaceted roles in enhancing soil fertility, nutrient cycling, and crop productivity. These bioactive compounds-including phytohormones (auxins, cytokinins, gibberellins), polysaccharides (alginates, laminarin, fucoidan, carrageenan), phenolic antioxidants, and betaines-modulate plant physiological processes such as photosynthetic efficiency, nutrient transporter expression, and stress-responsive gene regulation, while simultaneously improving soil organic matter

abstract: With the construction of the new power system, the penetration rate of distributed renewable energy in power distribution networks has gradually increased, bringing new characteristics to the new power system, including bidirectional power flow in equipment operation and frequent operating condition fluctuations. abstract: In this study, the effects of postharvest applications of different doses of gibberellic acid (GA₃) on quality attributes, bioactive compounds, and lipid peroxidation in 'Çakıl' cherry tomato fruits were investigated. The fruits were immersed in 0.1 and 0.3 mM GA3 solutions for 10 min, while the control group was immersed in a solvent-matched solution containing 0.1% (v/v) ethanol without GA3. title: SPAMS10: an InSAR-derived soil motion parameter dataset to model relative peat surface elevation changes
abstract: Peat subsidence poses a significant challenge to long-term land and environmental stability by increasing flood risk and producing greenhouse gas emissions. Field monitoring with extensometers reveals variability in relative surface elevation changes, which are then modeled using simple parameterization for the motion of soils (SPAMS). title: Youth Awareness on Climate Change and Environmental Issues, Case for Qardho, Karkaar Region, Puntland, Somalia
abstract: The study's goal was to find out how young students' awareness of the effects of climate change and core mitigation strategies is in the Qardho district of Puntland, Somalia. The research population for this study consisted of younger respondents from various school/academic years and stages. title: An AI-based algorithm for retrieving aerosol optical depth and single scattering albedo using All-Sky Imager observations
abstract: Accurate measurement of aerosol optical properties is critical for understanding their radiative and environmental impacts. Currently, the most accurate retrieval of aerosol properties comes from the multi-channel surface sun photometer, but with relatively high cost and deployment/maintenance requirements. Here we develop a novel AI-based method for retrieving daytime aerosol optical parameters, namely aerosol optical depth (AOD) and single scattering albedo (SSA) using images acquired by All-Sky Imagers (ASI). title: Immigration detention centers as torturing environments: Ethical reckonings, radical refusals, and implications for a psychology of resistance
abstract: This paper examines psychologists' ethical dilemmas in immigration detention centers. Using critical psychology, border, and detention scholarship, it highlights psychologists' historical complicity in state violence, from the U.S. Enhanced Interrogation Program to current border regimes. We argue that the structural conditions of migrant detention, characterized by profound dehumanization and harm, make ethical psychological practice in these torturing environments impossible. title: Exploring household livelihood resilience and natural resource dependence in urban-oriented resettlement in rural China
abstract: Urban-oriented resettlement is a key policy instrument for alleviating resource-driven livelihood constraints and fostering rural transformation and sustainable development in ecologically fragile regions. However, relocation not only changes residential locations but also alters households’ access to natural resources, livelihood capital structure, social networks, and livelihood strategy choices, leading to heterogeneous post-resettlement livelihood outcomes. title: Optimization method of internal financial budget execution and control based on SVM and clustering algorithm
abstract: With the rapid growth of enterprise financial data, traditional budget execution management methods that rely on manual analysis are unable to identify complex financial risks in a timely manner. Moreover, existing intelligent financial analysis methods mainly focus on data mining and lack comprehensive evaluation capabilities for departmental budget execution quality. title: GUYANA’S WATER GOVERNANCE, PUBLIC HEALTH, AND INDIGENOUS EQUITY: A REVIEW OF LEGAL AND POLICY FRAMEWORKS AFFECTING AMERINDIAN COMMUNITIES
abstract: Access to safe drinking water is recognised worldwide as a fundamental human right and a primary determinant of public health; however, inequities persist among Indigenous (Amerindian) communities in Guyana. This review analyses the legal, institutional, and governance frameworks that shape water quality and access. title: Synergistic Optimization of Hot Molding Process and Lay‐Up Design of CFRP ‐Steel Composite Load Wheel
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermoplastic CFRP composites offer great potential for lightweight rail vehicle wheels due to high specific strength and fatigue resistance. title: Improved seeds and rice productivity in Tanzania: policy insights from national sample census data
abstract: Improving rice productivity is central to Tanzania’s efforts to strengthen food security, reduce rural poverty, and advance agricultural transformation. Although improved seed technologies have been widely promoted, robust national-scale evidence on their performance under real-world smallholder conditions remains limited. This study aims to assess how improved seed adoption influences rice productivity across agroecological zones (AEZs) in Tanzania, addressing a key empirical gap in the existing National Sample Census of Agriculture (NSCA) literature. title: Climate and Human Impacts on Semi-Arid River Water Quality
abstract: Water quality degradation in river ecosystems is a growing global challenge, driven by both anthropogenic activities and climate change. This study examined program management and satisfaction at a PKBM in Situbondo, Indonesia, using a quantitative correlational design. title: From Normalization to Geopolitical Stress Test: The Abraham Accords After Five Years
abstract: This article examines the Abraham Accords (AA) 5 years after their signing, reconceptualizing them as a stress-tested security framework rather than a linear normalization project. Drawing on regional security developments—including the Hamas–Israel war, Houthi maritime attacks, the collapse of the Assad regime, and Iran–Israel confrontations—the article evaluates how conflict both constrains and reinforces normalization. abstract: In the context of escalating global trade uncertainty driven by geopolitical tensions and protectionist policies, and unforeseen systemic shocks, supply chain resilience has become a critical strategic priority for enterprises operating in open economies. abstract: With the proliferation of dynamic network environments such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks, challenges related to data localization and privacy leakage have become increasingly prominent. This randomized controlled trial included 158 children aged 8–9 years who completed 30 training sessions over 10 weeks. abstract: Abstract Benthic diatoms are widely used as bioindicators in freshwater assessment, and diatom-based biomonitoring tools have been applied in China for several decades. However, existing knowledge in China remains fragmented across Chinese and English literature, geographical regions, ecosystem types, and methodological traditions. abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are chronic, complex wounds that pose a significant global health care burden, particularly for individuals with poor control of their glycemic index. abstract: Soil-transmitted helminths (STHs) pose significant challenges to public health in endemic areas, necessitating reliable methods for their detection. abstract: The increasing consumption of canned tuna fish globally necessitates regular assessment of its safety, particularly with respect to heavy metal contamination. This study evaluates the concentrations of selected heavy metals—namely lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd), mercury (Hg), and arsenic (As)—in two popular varieties of canned tuna fish commonly found in local markets. abstract: This study examines how organizational performance and quality improvement influence competitive advantage through employee well-being in higher education institutions. abstract: Soil salinity is an issue in agriculture. Traditional methods of managing and treating soil cannot be used in saline and mineral-deficient conditions. abstract: The quality of Islamic school education is closely associated with the effectiveness of human resource management (HRM), particularly in developing teachers who possess professional competence while maintaining strong Islamic values. abstract: The Biodiversity Genomics Europe plus (BGE+) Project builds on a pan-European collaboration to scale up the production and uptake of genomic evidence for taxonomy, monitoring, and policy. abstract: Critical thinking is a core ability for application-oriented graduate students to tackle complex engineering problems and grow into high-level innovative practitioners. abstract: Manufacturing plants impose stringent requirements on the quality, efficiency and flexibility of batch production processes. Industrial robots, characterized by high flexibility, precision and reliability, have emerged as pivotal processing equipment in modern factories – particularly in the scenario of clustered flexible processing involving dozens or even hundreds of industrial robots. abstract: African leafy vegetables are important sources of dietary nutrients, including amino acids, but agronomic factors can influence their nutritional composition. abstract: Abstract Corrosion of carbon steel in hydrochloric acid is a significant industrial concern, particularly during acidizing and other acidic processes. abstract: Abstract Perveen Shakir (1952–1994) is celebrated as one of Pakistan’s pathbreaking Urdu poets. abstract: Ensuring access to safe drinking water remains a major challenge in developing regions, where traditional water quality monitoring methods are often manual, time-consuming, and unable to provide real-time insights. abstract: Abstract Well-log lithology classification supports reservoir identification and sedimentary facies mapping in exploration wells where core data are unavailable. We evaluate this deployment mismatch on a public 118-well Norwegian Continental Shelf dataset while controlling the target mapping, leakage protocol, missing-curve handling, and evaluation metric. Row-level validation substantially overstates unseen-well reliability: pooled F1-macro is 0.81–0.

title: Sero-catalytic and spatial modeling of dengue virus force of infection in Timor-Leste
abstract: Abstract Dengue virus (DENV) infection causes significant morbidity and mortality across tropical and sub-tropical regions, including in Timor-Leste. In this study we present the results of a national, population-representative serological survey, used to determine the drivers of observed variations in DENV force-of-infection (FOI, i.e. the average annual per-capita risk of infection for a susceptible person) at high spatial resolution. Households were randomly selected from census data and occupants aged above one year were tested using the Panbio Indirect dengue IgG enzyme-linked immunosorbe
institutions: National Centre for Immunisation Research & Surveillance

title: European blackflies: accepted and questionable species (Diptera, Simuliidae)
abstract: Primary and secondary published sources on European blackflies were systematically examined, and relevant data were extracted and compiled into a comprehensive inventory of extant species. All non-synonymised species-level taxa reported from Europe were incorporated into a raw data pool, comprising 268 taxa. A basic core set of species, containing 261 taxa, was derived from the raw data pool by excluding formally unnamed taxa—specifically two morphoforms and five cytoforms (including one hypothetical species)—and two nomina nuda . This also included the reassessment of Simulium aff. tuberosum

title: Fortifying the frontier, building the state: The ribat system and the consolidation of the Adamawa Emirate, 1809–1901
abstract: This paper examines the ribat as the central institution through which the Adamawa Emirate achieved both security and statehood between 1809 and 1901. Existing scholarship on the Sokoto Caliphate has generally treated the ribat as a fortified military outpost, a defensive structure erected at the margins of settled territory to repel external raids and to ensure the security of the people living in the ribats . journal: Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal

title: Comparative genomics of Sympodiorosea identifies genome evolution mediated through selective pressure on the metabolic gene repertoire
abstract: Abstract Biological interactions involving host-associated fungi are driven by chemistry shaped over evolutionary time. For antagonistic fungi, specialization often involves acquiring genes for novel secretions—including proteins and specialized metabolites—that mediate nutrient acquisition and host defense interactions. Here, we conducted a phylogenomic investigation of Sympodiorosea, ascomycetes commonly found in basal fungus-growing ant gardens. title: Conditioning-controlled retrieval of broadband land surface temperature and emissivity from paired ground-based longwave irradiance measurements
abstract: Accurate retrieval of land surface temperature ( T s ) from broadband longwave radiometric measurements is limited by the nonlinear coupling between surface emissivity ( ϵ ) and temperature, particularly when the available radiative contrast provides insufficient information to distinguish their contributions. title: The History and Legacy of British Colonial Looting
abstract: Abstract This historiographical review surveys the scholarship on British colonial spoils of war, outlining and critically analysing the main arguments and approaches as well as the new directions taken by recent authors. Moreover, it seizes the opportunity to take stock of what we know to address one of the field’s main issues – its disjointed nature. Scholars have mostly focused on a particular object, collection, or war, and so our understanding has developed piecemeal. title: From lab to market: A system integration perspective on flexible smart sensors
abstract: Flexible smart sensors are designed to conform to irregular or compliant surfaces. Operating at the interface of materials, structures, sensing, electronics, and system integration, these sensors have advanced rapidly at the device level, yet their transition into commercial sensor systems is lagging. journal: Journal of Intelligent Material Systems and Structures

title: Geology and Petrology of Buji Younger Granite Complex of North Central Nigeria
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive petrographic, and mineralogical evaluation of the Buji Younger Granite Complex in North-Central Nigeria, the Buji Younger Granite complex, five (5) major rock units were identified. Namely, Syenite, Nepheline Syenite, Biotite Granites, late and early rhyolites and fine and medium grained biotite granites. title: Electromethanogenesis underpins the methane production in a Tibetan wetland
abstract: Wetlands are a significant source of methane, a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming. Acetate and H2/CO2 are generally considered the dominant precursors for methane formation, while H2, generally considered as the electron donor, is considerably lower in wetlands. This work investigated alternative reductive mechanisms of methanogenesis in the soil microcosms of Zoige wetland on Tibetan Plateau. title: Integrated hydrochemical and microbiological assessment of groundwater quality for early contamination detection and preventive management
abstract: Abstract Groundwater is a critical source of drinking water in many rural areas and peri-urban communities; however, both geochemical and microbiological factors increasingly influence its suitability. This study presents an integrated assessment of groundwater quality in mining and agriculture-influenced communities of Ghana (Segyemase, Juaso and Nsuapemso) using hydrochemical characterization, water quality indices, microbiological indicators and risk-based interpretation. title: Transcriptomic adaptation of Litopenaeus vannamei to biofloc conditions in an indoor aquaculture system
abstract: Shrimp aquaculture is a crucial sector in global seafood production, yet environmental stressors adversely affect shrimp metabolism and immunity. Biofloc technology (BFT) addresses these challenges through the formation of microbial aggregates in floc, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This exploratory study evaluated transcriptomic alterations in the midgut of Litopenaeus vannamei cultured in an Indoor Multi-Trophic Aquaculture System (IMTAS). title: Rethinking Secularization: The Religion-Secular Binary, Christianity, and the Politics of Exclusion
abstract: Recent philosophers of secularization have given religion a more central place in their thinking about secular modernity and liberal democracy. This article argues that such theories have overlooked an important dimension of the contemporary social and political landscape, namely how the framework of separating ‘religious’ and ‘secular’ spheres can paradoxically affirm the hegemonic position of Christianity and marginalize non-Christian minorities. title: Harnessing agro-waste to combat microplastic pollution: Investigating the potential of low-temperature biochar from carrot and beetroot petioles
abstract: The growing concern over microplastic (MP) contamination in aquatic environments necessitates the development of effective, sustainable adsorbents for environmental remediation. This study evaluates the effectiveness of low-temperature biochar (LBC, partially carbonized) produced from carrot petiole (DCP) and beetroot petiole (BVP) waste through low-temperature pyrolysis at 200°C for removing microplastics. title: Preschool teachers’ competency in inclusive education: construction of a five-dimensional framework and empirical evidence from Chongqing, China
abstract: Against the backdrop of the continuous advancement of inclusive education, kindergarten teachers have become crucial to determining whether the quality of preschool inclusive education can be effectively realized. However, existing studies have tended to examine teachers' attitudes, knowledge, or skills separately, with limited structural explanation of how deep-seated qualities, intrinsic motivation, and explicit practices jointly constitute teacher competency in preschool inclusive settings. This study integrated the Iceberg Model and the Onion Model to construct a five-dimensional framework
institutions: Henan Institute of Science and Technology

title: Abraham Benaroya and the Transformation of Otherness: The Dialectics of Socialist Inclusion in the Greek Left-Wing Press (1918–1924)
abstract: Abstract Studies of anti-Jewish representations in the Greek press of the 1910s–1930s have focused on right-wing dailies, assuming that class-based universalism precluded similar attitudes within the labor press. This article argues that socialist universalism did not eliminate the production of Jewish Otherness but relocated it. title: The Impulsive Buying in Southeast Asian E-commerce Platforms: A Comparative Analysis Focused on Consumers’ Construal Levels
abstract: This study investigates the key factors and decision-making processes influencing impulse buying behaviour among Southeast Asian consumers, focusing on digital consumption patterns, sociocultural influences, psychological drivers and technological enablers. Data were collected from 279 adult consumers in Malaysia with active e-commerce experience. Structural equation modelling (SEM) and multi-group analysis were employed to test hypothesized relationships and moderating effects. title: İşgalci Tür Dreissena polymorpha (Pallas, 1771)’nın (Bivalvia) Trakya’daki Lentik Ekosistemlerdeki Dağılımı ve Çevresel Faktörlerin Etkisi
abstract: Ponto-Caspian kökenli bir bivalv türü olan Dreissena polymorpha (Pallas, 1771), monospesifik kolonileşmeleri sayesinde içsulardaki en önemli işgalci türlerden biri olup, birçok ekolojik ve ekonomik problemlere neden olduğu bildirilmektedir. abstract: Background: In 2026, the CFQ/CRQ System turns 70 (Law No. 2,800/1956), overseeing a sector responsible for ~11% of industrial GDP, but it lacked a chronological reconstruction based on its own official primary records. Aim: To reconstruct the System's legal genesis, establish a documented official chronology of its presidencies, and discuss current regulatory challenges. title: Prevalence of Dietary Supplement Use and Potential Medication Interactions Among Adults with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize the prevalence and correlates of dietary supplement use, identify commonly used supplements, and evaluate potential supplement-medication interactions among adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from 451 adults in the Approaches to Positive, Patient-centered Experiences of Aging with Lupus (APPEAL) study, an ancillary study of the population-based Georgians Organized Against Lupus cohort. title: Multi-omics insights into bacterial and fungal bioremediation of Potentially Toxic Elements (PTEs): a critical overview of their applications
abstract: Potentially toxic elements (PTEs) are persistent contaminants of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems and heavy metals and metalloids represent a major environmental and health concern. Microbial bioremediation exploits the ability of bacteria, fungi, and microbial communities to modulate PTE fate through processes including biosorption, bioaccumulation, redox transformation, biomineralization, precipitation, chelation, and extracellular sequestration. journal: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology

title: New records and invasion risk of Stenochrus portoricensis Chamberlin, 1922 (Schizomida: Hubbardiidae) in Brazil
abstract: Stenochrus portoricensis Chamberlin, 1922 is a schizomid native to the Caribbean and Central America and is notable for facultative parthenogenesis and a broad synanthropic distribution. It is widely reported as an exotic species in several regions worldwide, with recognized invasive potential. Here, we expand its known distribution in Brazil by documenting the first records from the state of Mato Grosso and new occurrences in tourist caves in Bahia. title: Accuracy assessment of terrestrial laser scanning for estimating tree height, diameter at breast height, crown dimensions, and aboveground biomass
abstract: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) provides dense three-dimensional observations of forest structure and has the potential to complement or replace labor-intensive conventional measurements for selected tree attributes. This study establishes an accuracy-assessment framework for estimating tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), crown dimensions, and aboveground biomass (AGB) from TLS point clouds. title: Salt-Assisted High-Hydrostatic-Pressure Strategy to Achieve High-Efficiency Nondestructive Bacterial Inactivation for Liquid Collagen
abstract: Abstract Collagen and its derivatives stand out as valuable biomaterials for applications in foods, cosmetics, healthcare products, medical equipment, and drug delivery carriers due to their high biocompatibility, biodegradability, and lack of toxicity and immunogenicity. However, the problem of microbial contamination in collagen is too important to ignore, which limits its further application in various fields. Traditional bacterial inactivation methods such as heating and irradiation can effectively kill microorganisms in solid collagen, yet struggle to eliminate microbes in liquid collagen

title: The 1956 Suez crisis: Britain’s relative decline and the geoeconomics of British power
abstract: The Suez Crisis of 1956 is conventionally seen as a turning point in Britain’s decline as a world power. This article argues instead that the Suez Crisis exposed the consequences of a much longer process of relative economic decline. By 1956, slower productivity growth and declining international competitiveness had weakened Britain’s economic position, while the need to defend sterling left it increasingly dependent on American financial support. title: Synergistic configurations of livelihood capital drive pastoralist well-being: evidence from Tibetan Plateau, China
abstract: Grassland governance has shifted from a primary focus on ecological restoration toward greater attention to pastoralists’ well-being. Against this background, subjective well-being (SWB) has become a core indicator for assessing livelihood outcomes in pastoral regions. Using survey data from 163 pastoral households in Sunan Yugur Autonomous County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau, this study applies fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to identify multiple pathways through which livelihood capital configurations generate high SWB. title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the Endangered scaly-sided merganser Mergus squamatus with insight into its demographic history
abstract: The scaly-sided merganser, Mergus squamatus, is an Endangered piscivorous duck which has been declining since the late 1900s due to habitat loss, over-hunting, and climate change. Despite being a species of global conservation concern and subject to ex- and in-situ conservation efforts, genomic research has been limited, hindering our understanding of its population genetic status and evolutionary history. title: India, China and the China+1 Strategy: Trade, Investment and Policymaking in a Fragmented World
abstract: ABSTRACT COVID‐19 and geopolitical tensions have compelled global firms to diversify parts of their operations to other countries. Although India looks primed to gain from this ‘China+1’, the authors' research, including interviews with 50 executives, officials and experts across India, America, Europe and Singapore, paints a more cautious picture. abstract: Manufacturing has historically aided as a first driver of economic development in advanced economies, contributing meaningfully to structural transformation, employment creation, and technological progress. title: Breaking the biofilm barrier: herbomineral nanocomposites to control Staphylococcus epidermidis through oxidative response and biofilm disruption
abstract: The growing prevalence of antibiotic resistance and biofilm-forming dental pathogens necessitates the development of alternative antimicrobial strategies. Staphylococcus epidermidis is an opportunistic pathogen associated with dental biofilms, oral microbial colonization, and implant-related infections, contributing to persistent infections and treatment challenges. abstract: This study evaluated the effects of different pretreatment methods on the phytochemical composition and amino acid profile of “Nyama Asabo” (Diplazium esculentum) to determine the most effective processing method for preserving its nutritional quality in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. title: From Energy Poverty to off-grid Smart Energy: Measured Household Air Quality and Willingness to Pay in Skardu, Gilgit-Baltistan
abstract: Gilgit-Baltistan lies at the periphery of Pakistan's electricity network, and in Skardu the consequences are acute. The town sits at 2,228 m, receives no piped natural gas, and endures a heating season of four to five months in which night temperatures fall between −10 and −20 °C. More than 80% of households therefore burn wood, dung cakes, crop residue, kerosene, coal, or plastic waste for warmth and cooking. abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated petrophysical-rock physics-geomechanical workflow that combines petrophysical analysis, Gassmann fluid-substitution modelling, elastic-property evaluation, and sand-production assessment to investigate reservoir responses to increasing gas saturation (Sg) during gas-based enhanced recovery in the Niger Delta. title: New Orleans and the Illegal Transatlantic Slave Trade, 1857–1861
abstract: This study explores the role of New Orleans in the illegal transatlantic slave trade between 1857 and 1861. It argues that the city’s growing involvement in this trade was connected to broader debates and attempts to reopen the transatlantic slave trade in Louisiana, which had been prohibited since 1808. title: Roasting-induced changes in the metabolite profile of laver (Neopyropia yezoensis): Focus on mycosporine-like amino acids and antioxidant activity
abstract: This study investigated non-volatile metabolites in laver ( Neopyropia yezoensis ) roasted under different temperature/time conditions. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry-based metabolomics identified 69 metabolites, including mycosporine-like amino acids (MAAs) and their dehydrated derivatives. abstract: Abstract Synonymous codons occur at unequal rates in the coding genome, with those represented least often termed ‘rare.’ Rare codon-enriched genes typically exhibit poor expression due to reduced transcription, mRNA stability, export, and translation. However, there are an increasing number of examples whereby rare codon-enriched genes are paradoxically highly expressed, suggestive of mechanisms to overcome the poor expression imposed by rare codons. title: Determination of Some Heavy Metals in Boswellia odorata, Thaumatococcus daniellii, Anogeissus leiocarpus, Erythrina senegalensis and Cochlospermum tinctorium Leaf
abstract: The assessment of heavy metals in plant species is crucial for understanding environmental health and potential risks to human health. This study focuses on the determination of heavy metals specifically lead, chromium, nickel, and manganese in the leaves of five selected plant species: Boswellia odorata, Thaumatococcus daniellii, Anogeissus leiocarpus, Erythrina senegalensis, and Cochlospermum tinctorium. abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have undergone an unprecedented expansion of host range since 2021, moving from wild birds and poultry into dairy cattle, domestic cats, and other mammals, with sporadic human infections in Europe and North America ( Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a ; Rolfes et al., 2025 ). title: A novel multi-sensor fault diagnosis framework based on PPS feature selection and Kmeans initialized particle swarm classifier using MiniRocket feature extraction
abstract: Abstract Acoustic sensors and microphone array technologies are widely used in industrial condition monitoring and fault diagnosis, and their reliability directly affects monitoring stability and equipment safety. However, existing acoustic sensor fault diagnosis methods under complex operating conditions still face limitations, including insufficient feature representation, reliance on handcrafted features, high computational cost, and difficulty in real-time deployment. title: Computational Design of a Phytochemical Drug Candidate Targeting Monkeypox Virus D8l and D4r/A20r Complex: An in Silico Study of Pharmacophoreand Molecular Prediction
abstract: Due to its rapid spread and the absence of approved antiviral treatments, Monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been declared as a global health emergency. This study aimed to identify possible drug candidates targeting MPXV vaccinia proteins D8L which is involved in host cell entry, and D4R/A20R Complex responsible for viral DNA replication and host cell entry. title: Modernized cosmogony: enduring hierarchies and the co-optation of public administration reform in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the persistent barriers to democratic accountability within Indonesian public administration by elucidating the evolving cultural logic termed modernized cosmogony. Drawing on historical institutionalism and critical realism-informed research, the research reveals how inherited sacred hierarchies, rooted in pre-colonial cosmologies, have dynamically adapted to withstand colonial, authoritarian, and democratic reforms. title: Assessing the limits of climate-driven and memory-enhanced streamflow forecasting in the regulated euphrates river under CMIP6 scenarios
abstract: Previous Euphrates and regulated-river forecasting studies have often compared algorithms without quantifying how far prediction can proceed when reservoir releases, storage, withdrawals, and allocation rules are unavailable. This study tested that information limit for monthly discharge at Haditha, Abbasiya, Kufa, and Nasiriyah using station-specific discharge records within 1980–2023 and observed rainfall/temperature from Iraqi meteorological sources. abstract: This research paper reviews issues associated with identifying the impact of electromagnetic interference (EI) sources within an environment where integrated electronic security systems (IESS) are operated. IESS are operated under diverse environmental conditions. They are exposed to internal and external EIs both natural and artificial. The authors conducted experiments within a natural environment. title: Audit Quality and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Insurance Companies in Nigeria
abstract: The integrity of audit opinions regarding financial reports has been a matter of concern since the Enron accounting scandal in 2001 and the subsequent financial crisis that affected numerous organizations, despite the issuance of clean audit opinions by auditors over the years. Consequently, this study investigated the effects of audit quality on the financial reporting quality of listed insurance companies in Nigeria from 2014 to 2023. title: The National CORS Network and Surveying Productivity in Vietnam: A Techno-Economic Assessment of VNGEONET
abstract: Vietnam completed its national satellite positioning network, VNGEONET, at the end of 2019, and in September 2024 moved the service from free trial access to a priced public utility. Both steps were justified on productivity grounds, yet no published study has quantified how much surveying productivity the network can plausibly deliver, or under what conditions the new access charges leave users better off. abstract: This paper asks whether the rapid expansion of digital payment platforms such as Alipay and WeChat Pay is linked to provincial economic growth in China, and if so, through what channel. It builds a panel of all 31 provincial-level regions from 2011 to 2023 (n = 403), combining the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion (DFI) Index with official provincial data on GDP, urbanization, patents, foreign direct investment, higher-education enrollment, and industrial structure. title: European ash pangenome reveals widespread structural variation and genetic basis of low ash dieback susceptibility
abstract: European Ash (Fraxinus excelsior) is a keystone tree species, whose populations are being decimated by ash dieback disease (ADB) - better characterisation of genetic variants associated with low susceptibility to the disease is needed. abstract: Abstract The article revisits Schneider and Schröder’s (2021) assessment of Namibian English (NamE) as a ‘non‑postcolonial’ variety that has moved from a phase of diffuse normative input into a yet uncompleted Phase 3 (‘nativization’) and that – due to ‘ethnic variation’ – remains well short of displaying the ‘homogeneity’ expected of Phase 4 (‘endonormative stabilization’). The article examines the historical record and draws on both perceptual and linguistic datasets collected across Namibian ethnolinguistic groups. title: Bacterial extracellular vesicles as central mediators of microbiota–host communication
abstract: Bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are nanoscale, lipid bilayer–enclosed structures released by both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria that act as active mediators of microbial and host–microbe communication rather than simple byproducts of membrane turnover. By packaging proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and metabolites, BEVs participate in quorum sensing, biofilm regulation, horizontal gene transfer, and immune modulation, with functional outcomes that depend strongly on microbial origin and environmental context: pathogen-derived BEVs frequently promote inflammation and tissue da

title: Pollen on feathers: unlocking the potential to study avian life histories through palynology
abstract: Capsule Bird-associated pollen can be effectively retrieved from single-use gloves worn during ringing to reveal patterns in habitat use and migratory ecology.Aims We compared abundance and richness of bird-associated pollen retrieved from ringers’ gloves, bird bags, feather swabs and feather clippings from Pied Flycatchers Ficedula hypoleuca to establish optimal methods for avian palynological research. We also highlight real-world applicability through proof-of-concept analysis.Methods Thirty females from three sites were handled during routine ringing using new cotton gloves and bird bags.

title: Validation of EarthCARE CPR reflectivity using the ACTRIS cloud radar network
abstract: The Earth Cloud, Aerosol, and Radiation Explorer (EarthCARE) satellite carries a cloud profiling radar (CPR) designed to observe global cloud properties. In this study, we assess the calibration of CPR reflectivity profiles by comparing them with seven calibrated ground-based cloud radars from the European Aerosol, Clouds and Trace Gases Research Infrastructure (ACTRIS). We compare the statistics of ice cloud reflectivities observed from space and from each ground site. title: Bioinspired Surface Enabled by Anisotropic Pyramid Structure Arrays for Directional Liquid Self‐Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Inspired by the phenomenon of directional liquid transport in natural organisms, various bionic surfaces with customized topological structures have been designed and fabricated, contributing to advances in such fields as microfluidics, microreactors, energy harvesting, biomedicine, etc. Despite extensive progress, bionic surfaces with directional liquid self‐transport capabilities still suffer from high technical thresholds, cumbersome fabrication processes, and contamination‐induced failure, limiting their widespread applications. title: Nanoengineered therapeutics for snakebite envenoming: Integrating recombinant antivenoms, targeted nanocarriers, nanobodies, toxin inhibitors, and translational challenges
abstract: Snakebite envenoming remains one of the most devastating neglected tropical diseases, causing an estimated 81,000–138,000 deaths and over 400,000 permanent disabilities annually, predominantly among rural populations in low- and middle-income countries. Despite the life-saving efficacy of conventional plasma-derived antivenoms, their therapeutic effect is often compromised by limited tissue penetration, delayed neutralization kinetics, immunogenicity, batch-to-batch variability, cold-chain dependence, and narrow species specificity. Recent advances in recombinant biologics, nanobody engineerin

title: Iron-refractory iron-deficiency anemia in pregnancy associated with a novel TMPRSS6 missense variant (c.248T>G): A case report from North India
abstract: Iron-deficiency anemia remains the most frequent cause of anemia in pregnancy and is usually amenable to treatment with oral or intravenous iron. Nonetheless, a minority of patients exhibit poor therapeutic response despite adequate dosing and compliance, warranting evaluation for uncommon etiologies such as iron-refractory iron-deficiency anemia (IRIDA). IRIDA is a rare inherited disorder with an autosomal recessive pattern, caused by mutations in the TMPRSS6 gene that lead to inappropriate hepcidin activity and disrupted iron regulation. journal: Journal of Hematology and Allied Sciences

title: Quantitative Occurrence of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons in Heat-Processed Fish and Meat Products in Variable Processing Matrices
abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are carcinogenic contaminants formed endogenously during high-temperature processing of protein-rich foods. This investigation evaluated the occurrence and dietary risk associated with four priority PAHs — benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), chrysene (Chr), benz[a]anthracene (BaA) and benzo[b]fluoranthene (BbF), collectively termed PAH4 — in traditionally processed fish and meat foods sampled from markets across six geopolitical zones of Nigeria. A total of 60 samples comprising smoked catfish, smoked tilapia, smoked mackerel, suya, kilishi and balangu were collected

title: Cost-effective tariff-aware HVAC coordination in Saudi residential buildings using physics-informed deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract When multiple On/Off split air-conditioning units in Saudi residential buildings activate simultaneously, the resulting peak demand spike stresses the electrical grid and inflates monthly bills under the kingdom’s two-tier tariff (0.18 SAR/kWh $$\leq$$ 6,000 kWh; 0.30 SAR/kWh above). journal: Journal of King Saud University - Engineering Sciences

title: Regulating private gardens under planning law: Challenges and opportunities encountered in the Low Countries
abstract: Abstract This article examines how planning law in Flanders (Belgium) and the Netherlands regulates residential gardens as nature‐based solutions, identifying both legal opportunities for and obstacles to activating the ecosystem services of gardens. The comparison and analysis focus on normative conditions, planning permission as a regulatory permission and enforcement. The EU's Nature Restoration Regulation makes this comparison a timely exercise, as it contains specific obligations for urban nature, which will likely lead to an increased focus by planning authorities on private gardens.
journal: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law

title: Citizen science reveals patterns of distributional decline and expansion across 1864 native vascular plant species in Kanagawa, Japan
abstract: Abstract Rapid land-use change and climate change increase the need for quantitative, region-wide assessments of current status across many plant species. Long-term citizen-led distribution surveys help meet this need, and European examples in particular have been widely recognized internationally. In contrast, comparable efforts in non-English-speaking regions remain underrepresented due to language barriers. We present a citizen-science project in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, and analyze presence–absence data from three distribution surveys (1979–1987, 1996–2000, 2013–2017) conducted under th
institutions: Kanagawa Prefectural Museum of Natural History

title: Influence of irrigation regime and microbial consortium application on pharmaceutical uptake in durum wheat irrigated with treated wastewater
abstract: The reuse of treated wastewater (TWW) in agriculture represents a promising strategy to alleviate freshwater scarcity, although the occurrence of pharmaceuticals (PhACs) raises concerns regarding their fate and potential transfer within the soil–plant system. This study investigated the combined effects of irrigation regime and beneficial microbial inoculation on the persistence, transformation, and plant uptake of PhACs in durum wheat cultivated under controlled pot conditions and irrigated with TWW. The experiment evaluated four irrigation levels (I100, I70, I50 and I30 deficit conditions),

title: GRAIN: Mapping the World's Irrigation Canals and Why It Matters for Water, Food, and Climate
abstract: Abstract The engineered channels that carry water from large dams and rivers to agricultural fields, known as irrigation canals, are the link between source (lakes and reservoirs) and sink (farmlands). These canals make cultivation of crops possible across millions of hectares of land. A comprehensive global map of irrigation canals has, until now, been missing. We introduce in this perspectives, a comprehensively prepared and curated geospatial data set called Global Registry of Agricultural Irrigation Network (GRAIN). With GRAIN, which documents nearly 3.8 million km of canal geometry, we be
journal: Perspectives of Earth and Space Scientists

title: A review of mRNA vaccines and host-directed therapeutics for multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens
abstract: Abstract The persistent threat of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens— Enterococcus faecium , Staphylococcus aureus , Klebsiella pneumoniae , Acinetobacter baumannii , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , and Enterobacter species (ESKAPE)—has necessitated messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) strategies beyond conventional antibiotics. title: CMIP6 data usage: lessons learned from more than 200 million downloads
abstract: Earth system simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) are considered the gold standard in terms of representation of the Earth's climate system, its past and present states, and possible future evolution. As CMIP moves into its seventh phase, the increasing complexity of Earth system models (ESMs) means that there is a greater need for infrastructure resources to store, distribute and utilize CMIP simulations. Statistics on the usage of data during CMIP6 has the potential of offering guidance to prepare for CMIP7. Here, we analyse the downloads of CMIP6 data and propos

title: Sustainable soil stabilization: a comprehensive review of green technologies, industrial by-products, and bio-mediated methods
abstract: Abstract Soil stabilization is fundamental to geotechnical engineering, yet traditional cement- and lime-based methods impose significant environmental burdens through high energy consumption and CO 2 emissions. This review systematically analyzes sustainable stabilization technologies, including bio-mediated techniques (microbially induced carbonate precipitation [MICP] and enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation [EICP]), industrial by-product utilization (fly ash, ground granulated blast furnace slag [GGBS], steel slag, and cement kiln dust [CKD]), geopolymer and alkali-activated binders, and

title: Design of a Sanitary Landfill for Solid Waste Disposal in Kaduna North Local Government Area of Kaduna State
abstract: Effective solid waste management is a growing challenge in Kaduna North Local Government, Kaduna State, due to rapid urbanization and increasing waste generation. This study focuses on the design of a sanitary landfill that provides a sustainable and environmentally friendly waste disposal solution for the region. The research involves a comprehensive assessment of current waste generation rates, waste composition, recoverable materials and disposal methods. The landfill design incorporated key engineering parameters such as landfill capacity, liner systems to prevent groundwater contamination
journal: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT

title: Emergent blink rate in early childhood is associated with neural origins of executive function
abstract: Executive function develops rapidly in early childhood and predicts later success in life, yet its neurobiological correlates during this period are not yet well characterised. In adults, executive function is supported by prefrontal–striatal circuits under neuromodulatory control, including dopamine. Here, we show that spontaneous eye-blink rate, a physiological output influenced by neuromodulatory systems, is associated with the developmental trajectory of executive function and prefrontal functional differentiation. We used fNIRS to monitor prefrontal cortex (PFC) activation in 113 children

title: Green biosynthesis of selenium nanoparticles by a novel Monoraphidium sp.: optimization, bioinformatic insights, and nanoparticle characterization
abstract: Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) offer unique biomedical and industrial potentials with reduced toxicity compared to inorganic selenium, yet sustainable and eco-friendly production methods remain underexplored. As a novel approach, this study reports the first biosynthesis of SeNPs using a locally isolated Monoraphidium sp., alongside optimization of cultivation parameters and bioinformatic analysis. title: Synergistic preservation of fresh cut fruits and vegetables through cold chain logistics and antagonistic microorganisms: mechanisms and emerging applications
abstract: Fresh-cut fruits and vegetables are widely popular owing to their pleasant texture, rich nutrients and convenient consumption. Nevertheless, microbial contamination and physiological deterioration frequently emerge during processing and cold chain distribution, triggering quality degradation and shortened shelf life. Conventional single cold storage fails to efficiently suppress psychrotrophic spoilage microorganisms, whereas chemical preservatives carry hidden risks of toxic residues. Current research on antagonistic microorganisms remains fragmented, with inadequate systematic collation of s
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Auxiliary Thrust Jet Engines: Design, Integration, and Performance Analysis
abstract: Fixed-wing surveillance aircraft built around electric or small internal-combustion propulsion offer good endurance but are speed-limited, which restricts their ability to reposition rapidly over long standoff distances or evade emerging threats. This paper presents the design, integration methodology, and performance analysis of an auxiliary thrust micro-turbojet engine intended to supplement the primary propulsion system of a long-range, high-speed intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) aircraft. The proposed architecture retains an efficient primary propulsion system for exten
journal: Global Journal of Engineering and Technology Advances

title: Impact of the GouM transporter on secondary metabolism activation and production yield in Streptomyces noursei strain CK‐15
abstract: Abstract Streptomyces noursei produces various bioactive secondary metabolites with agricultural significance; however, the regulatory mechanisms governing their production and secretion remain largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically characterized the secondary metabolic potential of S . noursei CK‐15 and investigated the role of the transporter gene gouM in regulating gougerotin efflux and global cluster interactions. title: Evaluating Quality of Piles Constructed in Indonesia Through Five Year of Crosshole Sonic Logging Data
abstract: Deep foundation is one of the structural components where ensuring pile integrity is essential to achieve the required strength. Unlike columns, beams, or other structures that can be visually inspected, pile foundations require specialized tools to assess their integrity. One of the tests that can be utilized is the Crosshole Sonic Logging (CSL) test, a method that relies on wave propagation to evaluate the integrity of cast-in-place bored piles. The purpose of this paper is to analyze CSL dataset of piles constructed in Indonesia, identifying patterns and trends within large datasets. This s

title: Biological and Therapeutic Properties of Honey in Wound Healing
abstract: Background. Chronic and infected wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to impaired tissue regeneration, persistent inflammation, bacterial biofilms, and antimicrobial resistance. Aim. This review aimed to assess the biological and therapeutic properties of honey in wound healing, with emphasis on its mechanisms of action, clinical applications, and emerging therapeutic approaches. Material and methods. title: EXPERIMENTAL STUDY OF BEARING CAPACITY OF SOIL STABILIZATION WITH MARBLE DUST
abstract: Soft soils in road subgrades pose considerable engineering challenges; however, stabilization with marble dust offers an environmentally sustainable alternative. In this study, a 100 × 90 × 90 cm tank was employed to assess soils blended with 0%, 3%, 6%, 9%, and 12% marble dust by dry weight at depths of 10, 20, and 30 cm. Then, the soil mixed with marble dust was cured for 7 days before the testing. title: Legacy of non-ferrous metallurgy driving heavy metal-induced geochemical transformation of urban soils
abstract: Introduction Urban soils in long-established mining and metallurgical cities represent persistent reservoirs of potentially toxic elements (PTEs), posing long-term ecological and human health risks. Ust-Kamenogorsk (Oskemen), one of Kazakhstan’s major non-ferrous metallurgical centers, has experienced more than seven decades of intensive ore processing and smelting. Although previous studies reported elevated concentrations of Cd, Pb, Zn, and Cu, a comprehensive assessment integrating contamination status, ecological risk, spatial variability, and environmental controls has remained limited. title: Belowground microbial stewardship underpins sustainable agroecosystem management
abstract: Below every cultivated field lies a civilization of unimaginable complexity. A single gram of productive agricultural soil harbors upwards of a billion bacterial cells, several kilometers of fungal hyphae, and a faunal community spanning nematodes, protozoa, mites and collembolans, all bound together in trophic relationships that have been taking shape for hundreds of millions of years. title: A Low-Power, IP68-Compliant, BLE-Based Multi-Station Smart Irrigation Control Unit for Agricultural Applications
abstract: This study designs, develops, and evaluates the performance of a low-power, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) based, IP68 protection-rated, multi-station smart irrigation control unit for agricultural irrigation applications. The system is built on an STM32F103 microcontroller-based electronic control board and can manage 6 independent irrigation stations. Irrigation is automatically controlled by evaluating environmental data obtained from rain, frost, and wind sensors, and it is designed to be compatible with different types of rain sensors. title: Height-threshold-dependent estimates of forest gap characteristics, spatial patterns, and dynamics: Evidence from multi-temporal UAV–LiDAR
abstract: Forest gaps record disturbance, regeneration, and canopy structural change, yet estimates of gap closure depend strongly on the height threshold used to define when a gap is considered closed. This issue is particularly relevant for three-dimensional LiDAR analyses, where gap structure and dynamics can be quantified across vertical canopy layers. We used multi-temporal UAV–LiDAR data from a temperate forest in northeastern China to test how six fixed height thresholds (2–12 m) influence estimates of gap characteristics, spatial patterns, and dynamics. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Duckweed (Wolffia globosa, Wolffia arrhiza, and Lemna minor) as novel therapeutic food for acute malnutrition and famine alleviation in low- and middle-income countries and humanitarian crisis settings
abstract: Acute malnutrition remains a leading cause of under-five mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly in humanitarian crisis settings where conventional therapeutic food supply chains are frequently disrupted. There is an urgent need for locally cultivable, affordable, and nutritionally adequate alternatives to imported ready-to-use therapeutic foods (RUTFs). In this review, we examine the nutritional composition, food safety, and production scalability of three duckweed species, namely: Wolffia globosa , Wolffia arrhiza , and Lemna minor , as candidate therapeutic foods

title: Distribution and Health-Risk Assessment of Polychlorinated Biphenyl Congeners in Soils from E-Waste and Automobile Dismantling Sites
abstract: The uncontrolled dismantling of electronic waste and end-of-life vehicles in low- and middle income countries has emerged as a significant, yet inadequately quantified, source of persistent organic pollutants to the terrestrial environment. This study characterised the distribution, congener-specific profile and human health-risk implications of nineteen polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB) congeners in topsoils collected from three informal electronic-waste (e-waste) dumpsites and two automobile-dismantling sites in the densely populated metropolis of Lagos, Nigeria. title: Degrowth-oriented entrepreneurial identity in rural agrifood: Evidence from women-led firms in Ireland
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of degrowth-oriented entrepreneurial identity, and theorises how it is formed and enacted in practice by combining degrowth research with rural women entrepreneurship, employing a Feminist Political Ecology (FPE) lens. title: Food Safety Knowledge, Attitude and Practices of Road-Side Vendors of Ready-To-Eat Grilled Catfish in Awka Metropolis, Anambra State, Nigeria
abstract: The study was conducted to determine the food safety knowledge, attitude and practices of road-side vendors of ready to eat grilled catfish in Awka metropolis, Anambra state, Nigeria. Cross-sectional survey was adopted in selecting a sample of vendors. This sample was derived from 20 entities randomly selected from four predetermined towns that were considered to have high concentration of these operators. title: Effects of dietary fucoidan and exercise on the gut microbiome, fecal metabolome, and tumor-related responses in a murine colorectal cancer model
abstract: Dietary fucoidan, a sulfated polysaccharide derived from brown seaweed, has attracted increasing interest for its potential to influence gut microbial and metabolic responses. However, the individual and combined effects of dietary fucoidan and exercise on host–microbiome interactions during colorectal cancer development remain incompletely understood. In this preventive study, mice received fucoidan at 300 mg/kg (F1) or 600 mg/kg (F2), alone or in combination with low-intensity exercise at 12 m/min for 30 min or moderate-intensity exercise at 15 m/min for 40 min, for six weeks before MC38 tum

title: Allanblackia and Soybean Bakery Fat Impact on Baking Performance of Bread
abstract: Physicochemical features of Allanblackia and Soybean bakery fat and the impact of on baking performance of bread in terms of loaf volume, weight, height and oven spring was investigated. Outcome was compared with the commercial equivalent. Results showed that fat and solid fat content was higher in Allanblackia-soybean bakery fat than the control sample whereas water, melting point and salt content were highest in control sample. journal: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF FOOD SCIENCE AND QUALITY CONTROL

title: Spatial prediction of soil organic carbon stocks in Sudanese clay soils using regression kriging
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks are a critical component of terrestrial carbon pools, influencing soil quality, agricultural productivity, and climate change mitigation. This study aimed to map and improve spatial estimation of SOC stocks in Sudan’s Blue Nile clay soils using regression kriging (RK). The model integrated 554 spatially unique soil profiles with nine environmental covariates: precipitation, temperature, relative humidity, normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), land use/cover, bare soil index (BSI), digital elevation model (DEM), LS-factor, and aspect. title: Gut microbiota remodeling and immune gene modulation by Semiliquidambar cathayensis protect Misgurnus anguillicaudatus against Aeromonas hydrophila: integrative transcriptomic and 16S rRNA analysis
abstract: This study aims to explore the regulatory mechanism of Semiliquidambar cathayensis extract on the immune stress induced by Aeromonas hydrophila in Misgurnus anguillicaudatus . Through transcriptomics and 16S rRNA sequencing techniques, the changes in gene expression profiles of M. anguillicaudatus muscle tissues and the structure of the intestinal microbiota were analyzed separately. title: Multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli in selected sachet water and associated public health risk assessment in Ago-Iwoye and Oru, Ogun State, Nigeria
abstract: Safe drinking water remains essential for public health, particularly in developing regions where sachet water is widely consumed. This study assessed the physicochemical properties, bacteriological quality, antibiotic resistance, heavy metal contamination, and potential health risks of 8) selected sachet water samples. Physicochemical parameters were measured using APHA standard methods. Bacterial counts were determined by serial dilution and plate count techniques. title: Environmental drivers of body size plasticity and their consequences for reproductive fitness in Anopheles coluzzii
abstract: Malaria is a life-threatening infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites and transmitted to humans primarily through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. Sub-Saharan Africa bears the greatest global burden of malaria, with members of the Anopheles gambiae complex, including Anopheles coluzzii, serving as important malaria vectors in the region. title: Wasserstein distributional distance and linear programming convergence planning as monitoring network benchmarking tools: cross-continental surface water quality assessment across Brazilian and European river basins
abstract: Abstract Evaluating the performance of long-term water quality monitoring networks against international reference systems requires analytical tools capable of comparing entire empirical distributions — not merely summary statistics — yet distributional benchmarking methods have rarely been applied at the cross-continental scale. title: WATER, DROUGHT AND SOCIETY IN COLONIAL BUNDELKHAND: A HISTORICAL STUDY
abstract: Water, or rather its scarcity, has shaped the history of Bundelkhand more decisively than almost any other single factor. This paper examines the region's long relationship with water as a socio-ecological resource, tracing the shift from the decentralised, community-anchored tank-and-well regime built up over centuries by the Chandela and Bundela rulers to the centralised, revenue-oriented hydraulic interventions of British colonial administration. title: Effect of Graded Dietary Levels of Dried Hermetia illucens Larvae Meal on Biochemical and Hematological Parameters of White Leghorn Laying Hens
abstract: While most previous studies on Hermetia illucens larvae in poultry nutrition have focused mainly on productive performance and the replacement of conventional protein sources, limited information is available on the dose-dependent effects of whole dried larvae on metabolic and blood indices in laying hens. The objective of this research was to examine the effects of graded dietary levels of dried Hermetia illucens larvae (DHIL; 5%, 10%, and 15%) in White Leghorn laying hens on liver enzymes, kidney parameters, lipid profile, and hematological indices. title: A systems-level analysis of global gene expression in resistant and susceptible Biomphalaria glabrata in response to Schistosoma mansoni infection
abstract: Background The freshwater gastropod Biomphalaria glabrata is the major intermediate host of Schistosoma mansoni , the causative agent of human schistosomiasis. Elucidating the molecular basis of snail resistance to schistosomes is essential for understanding invertebrate immunity, host–parasite interactions, and schistosomiasis epidemiology. Methods Two new B. glabrata – S. mansoni interaction models were examined: homozygous lines (HZLs) iBS90_R (resistant) and iM line_S (susceptible), and recombinant inbred lines (RILs) RIL18_R (resistant) and RIL108_S (susceptible). title: Uncovering the Diversity of Mesostoinae (Hymenoptera: Braconidae): A Glimpse Into the Australian Fauna Through a Study of Kangaroo Island
abstract: ABSTRACT The Mesostoinae are a poorly understood braconid subfamily with unresolved morphological challenges and a complex taxonomic history. This study provides insight into the biodiversity of this subfamily on Kangaroo Island (KI), South Australia. Specimens were curated from existing collection material for DNA extraction and sequencing of the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I gene. title: A trainable language model with potential to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms by generating upstream untranslated region sequence libraries
abstract: Tuning protein expression in non-model organisms is often constrained by the lack of validated genetic parts and predictive design tools. Translational tuning through the modulation of upstream untranslated regions (5'-UTRs) offers a potentially organism-agnostic route, but existing methods typically rely on mechanistic assumptions, prior knowledge that may not be available in non-model contexts, or the screening of sequence libraries. title: Metal Contamination and Ecological Risks in the Kasaï and Tshikapa Rivers (DR Congo): Insights from Geochemical Analyses of Sediments and Water
abstract: This study assessed the distribution of trace metals, rare earth elements (REEs), thorium (Th), and uranium (U) in sediments and surface waters of the Tshikapa and Kasai Rivers in Tshikapa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and evaluated the associated contamination and potential ecological risks. Sediment physicochemical properties, grain-size distribution, trace elements, and REEs were determined using analytical techniques.

title: From Yak Dung to Plastics
abstract: This article examines how Zero Waste is interpreted and practised in Naksoknyi, a Tibetan pastoral community in Qinghai Province, China. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork, interviews, focus groups and analysis of NGO publications, it shows that the initiative is not simply adopted as a global environmental model, but translated into local moral, ecological and material concerns. title: Plantago lanceolata and Lolium perenne metabolite profiles, their impact on soil microbial community structures and soil biological nitrification inhibition
abstract: Excess nitrate (NO 3 − ), from fertilizer overuse and intensive agriculture, can pollute water and contribute to greenhouse gas production (nitrous oxide—N 2 O). Plant metabolites from pastural herbs such as Plantago lanceolata (plantain) can inhibit microbial nitrification of ammonium to NO 3 − (biological nitrification inhibition—BNI) and change soil nitrogen cycle dynamics (lower potential nitrification rate—PNR). abstract: Agricultural supply chains are vulnerable to disruptions through linked biophysical and economic systems. We develop a novel AI-powered tool that integrates economic models (GTAP) with biophysical models (APSIM) to analyze supply chain shocks, enabling policymakers and market participants to assess cross-disciplinary impacts through queries and responses written in natural language. title: The impact of heavy metal exposure on drug-induced liver injury in patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis
abstract: Abstract The aim of the study is to clarify the association between heavy metal exposure and drug-induced liver injury (DILI) in patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB), and to provide new epidemiological evidence for the prevention and treatment of DILI. In this study we utilized a 1:2 matched nested case–control study design based on a follow-up cohort of DR-TB patients at Hunan Provincial Chest Hospital from September 2021 to November 2024. abstract: Background: Antimicrobial resistance is a major public health concern, particularly with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA), which are associated with limited treatment options and poor clinical outcomes. This study assessed the antibacterial activity of its ethanolic extract against archived MRSA and CRPA isolates. Methods: This was a laboratory-based experimental study. Using data from 30 major Chinese cities, this study introduces a comprehensive methodology that integrates the XGBoost algorithm with 16 distinct metaheuristic optimization techniques to compare algorithms performance in both regression and classification tasks. abstract: Abstract To date, research on Te isotopic behavior within ores from independent tellurium deposits has yet to be conducted. title: Research on indicator system and comprehensive evaluation of low-altitude airspace use efficiency based on ADS-B data
abstract: This study addresses the growing need for effective low-altitude airspace management driven by the rise of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and urban air mobility (UAM), including e-VTOL aircraft serving the expected UAM concept. The research develops a comprehensive airspace efficiency evaluation system based on ADS-B data, which offers real-time flight information. A TOPSIS-based evaluation model is proposed, incorporating seven core indicators: flight density, total flight time, capacity, traffic flow, specific aircraft flight counts, traffic composition, and altitude utilization. title: A multi-omics integrated analysis reveals the effects of adding Bacillus coagulans BC66 to feed on the intestinal health and immune function of Parabramis pekinensis
abstract: With the widespread adoption of high-density, intensive farming systems, environmental stressors in Parabramis pekinensis farming have become increasingly severe, leading to intestinal dysfunction, reduced digestive and absorptive capacity, and frequent outbreaks of disease. This study aimed to investigate the effects of adding Bacillus coagulans BC66 to feed on the intestinal health and immune function of Parabramis pekinensis , as well as the underlying multi-omic mechanisms. abstract: ABSTRACT The challenges posed by climate change have led to widespread environmental and socio-economic impacts, including rising temperatures, extreme weather events, and polar ice cap melting. These issues, driven by greenhouse gas emissions since the 1980s, have become critical, requiring mitigation strategies rather than reversal. One effective strategy is the circular economy, which promotes waste reduction and resource reuse. title: SLC7A6OS Founder Mutation: A Rare Cause of Progressive Myoclonus Epilepsy Dated to 1100 Years Ago
abstract: BACKGROUND: SLC7A6OS c.191A>G is a rare, autosomal recessive cause of progressive myoclonus epilepsy (PME). The c.191A>G variant, first discovered in two families from Türkiye and Portugal, was recently identified in three additional probands from the USA, all of Puerto Rican ancestry.
