title: A tripartite account of phishing detection: the importance of glucose in supporting the algorithmic mind
abstract: Despite substantial investment in technical safeguards, employees continue to fall for phishing emails at high rates, and the cognitive decision-making processes that drive this susceptibility remain comparatively understudied relative to technical countermeasures. The present research addresses this gap by applying the tripartite model of dual-process theory and prospect theory to examine cognitive responses to phishing and legitimate emails. title: Effects of packaging material and vacuum sealing packaging on TBARS values lipid oxidation in snakehead fish (Channa striata) sausages stored at 10 ± 2 °C
abstract: Lipid oxidation is a major cause of quality deterioration in processed fish products during storage. Snakehead fish (Channa striata) sausages contain unsaturated fatty acids that are susceptible to oxidative degradation. This laboratory experiment evaluated the effects of packaging and vacuum packaging on lipid oxidation in snakehead fish sausage. This experimental study was conducted between March and August 2025 at the Food Laboratory of the Department of Nutrition and Integrated Laboratory of Politeknik Kesehatan Kemenkes Jayapura, Jayapura, Indonesia. abstract: Organic coconut sugar exports depend on claims about origin and process that buyers cannot verify directly, so exporting firms are increasingly required to make their information verifiable. Previous studies have examined traceability systems and business ethics separately and have rarely tested how transparency reaches performance, which constitutes the research gap of this study. abstract: Objective: To critically examine the scientific structure, thematic evolution, and emerging monitoring and mitigation strategies of microbial biodeterioration in diesel, biodiesel, and diesel–biodiesel storage systems. Methods: An integrative review with bibliometric and scientometric analysis used records from the Web of Science Core Collection. title: Authorisation of notary publics on real property transactions in relation to the Turkish land registry system based on “Cadastre 2014 vision”
abstract: The International Federation of Surveyors (FIG) has globally influenced land administration through its Cadastre 2014 vision and subsequent LADM standards. Türkiye has been modernizing its land registry and cadastre system accordingly. The General Directorate of Land Registry and Cadastre (GDLRC) manages approximately 17 million annual transactions, including about 3.4 million conveyancing (long-term averages). title: Faith, form, and the bin: the CT-VR framework for culturally tuned recycling infrastructure in Gulf cities
abstract: Cities in the Gulf Region, such as Doha, are implementing new strategies to manage waste in an environmentally friendly manner. Despite rapid petroleum-based urban development creating unplanned leftover spaces, no systematic research has explored residents' utilization of recycling containers within these areas. This study employs virtual reality (VR) as a pre-deployment tool for testing culturally tuned recycling infrastructure in urban leftover spaces. title: Why are immoral choices more immersive? The effect of moral decision-making on narrative immersion via moral emotions and the moderating role of autonomy — Evidence from Chinese gamers
abstract: Moral choice systems are widely implemented in role-playing games (RPGs) to enhance players' narrative immersion. However, existing research has yielded inconsistent findings regarding whether different types of moral choices (i.e., high-morality vs. low-morality choices) produce different levels of immersion. title: Epidemiology of human RSV in Taiwan, 2018–2024
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants and older adults worldwide. This retrospective study investigated the epidemiology and molecular characteristics of RSV in Taiwan from 2018 to 2024 using data from the National Community Virus Surveillance System, which encompassed the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic period. abstract: Human Resources (HR) to improve service quality at RELOF Clinic Bekasi require systematic and continuous efforts to enhance competence and career progression. This study was conducted with the aim of analyzing the characteristics of HR, mapping the competencies of management and operational staff, evaluating the recruitment and career development system, and assessing the quality of service provided to the community at RELOF Clinic in Bekasi City. title: HSF1-mediated proteostasis decline links aging and sleep disruption
abstract: Sleep disruption increases with age and is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, integrative analyses of human and mouse transcriptomic and proteomic datasets identify proteostasis pathways whose aging trajectories align with responses to chronic sleep disruption across tissues, cell types, and molecular layers. Mouse brain and human blood analyses independently recover heat shock factor 1 (HSF1)-associated proteostasis as a recurrent feature of sleep-aging convergence. title: Could Underwater Data Centers Pose a Risk to AI Treaty Verification?
abstract: Proposals for international agreements that limit frontier AI development depend on verification, and a central challenge is detecting undeclared compute facilities used to evade restrictions. Underwater data centers (UDCs) have been suggested as one such evasion vector, but their feasibility at frontier scale and their detectability have not been seriously assessed. title: Intrinsic Vectorial Gradiometry via Quantum Control of a Spin-based Sensor
abstract: Gradiometry provides a versatile alternative to passive environmental shielding in quasi-static magnetometry, effectively suppressing background noise through differential signal extraction. Nevertheless, traditional implementations rely on multi-sensor architectures restricted to spatial gradients, where subtracting signals from independent detectors involves imperfect suppression of common-mode noise and artifacts, limiting their sensitivity. title: Surface Stokes drift from compact drifting wave buoys
abstract: Surface Stokes drift depends strongly on the energy and directions of short waves, which are incompletely resolved by routine wave observations. We derive surface Stokes drift vectors from wave measurements collected by compact drifting buoys during three deployments in the North-East Atlantic and the Alboran Sea. abstract: Disaster-risk-reduction archives describe hazard events in prose that databases such as EM-DAT (Delforge et al., 2025) cannot ingest directly. We present an LLM pipeline that generates candidate georeferenced event records using a controlled hazard vocabulary and fixed schema, retaining evidence for review. abstract: Most modern lattice QCD calculations take the masses of the light quarks to be degenerate, setting $m_u=m_d$, a choice that, while not physical, increases computational efficiency and lowers the complexity of simulations and analysis. title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied. title: Asteroids Impacting the Solar System Planets and the Moon. III. Real Impacts from Known Objects and LSST Discovery Predictions
abstract: Impact rates predicted using pre-impact source-population models and those inferred from observations disagree by a factor of a few to $\sim200$ across the Solar System planets and the Moon. An exciting opportunity for an additional observational constraint is the discovery of asteroids before impact and their tracking until impact. We evaluate this prospect based on both known objects and forecasts of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). title: Inoculation Midtraining with Learned Neologisms
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often learn both desirable and undesirable properties during post-training. We study whether midtraining, an earlier training stage, can shape which of these properties later generalise. We introduce Inoculation Midtraining, a technique that teaches a base model that unsafe behaviour belongs to a designated context, as indicated by the neologism (a new token) introduced during midtraining, and then post-trains the model on unsafe data within that context. title: Pseudo-Incrementality Testing: Measuring Advertising Lift from Naturally Occurring Interventions
abstract: We develop a method for measuring the incremental effect of advertising when randomized exper- iments are unavailable. Firms generate abrupt interventions in their own marketing as a byproduct of operations: budgets are cut, channels launch, programs pause. We propose a two-stage proce- dure that treats these events as quasi-experiments. title: Stress-testing Alignment Midtraining
abstract: When aligning frontier models through post-training techniques, it is not possible to directly demonstrate all of the behaviours we want a model to exhibit in all possible deployment environments; our model must generalise outside of the post-training distribution. One proposed solution is alignment midtraining (AMT), which continues pretraining on large volumes of alignment-relevant documents to encourage generalisation in later stages of training. title: Learning Air-Ground Motion Control with Temporal Mode Switching and Cross-Terrain Tracking
abstract: Passive-wheeled terrestrial-aerial bimodal vehicles (TABVs) combine aerial mobility with energy-efficient ground locomotion. However, reliable air-ground mode switching under limited onboard perception and robust ground trajectory tracking across diverse terrains remain challenging when targeting real-world applications. title: Distinct Population of Wolf-Rayet Stars in the Low-Metallicity Galaxy NGC 6822. Quantitative analysis of optical and UV spectra of the complete sample
abstract: Context: Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars are particularly rare in low-metallicity galaxies and remain poorly understood. Detailed studies of the presumably complete population of WR stars in the nearby Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) galaxy led to perplexing results. Aims: The nearby galaxy NGC 6822 has a similar metallicity to the SMC, and hence provides an excellent laboratory for a comparative study. We aim to derive the stellar and wind parameters of each known WR star in NGC 6822 by means of quantitative spectroscopy. The results are compared with the WR population of the SMC. abstract: We construct turbulent gravitational wakes in asymptotically AdS$_4$ spacetimes by solving the full non-linear Einstein equations in the characteristic formulation. Specifically, we show that a localized boundary deformation acting on a boosted black brane generates a wake whose boundary dynamics exhibit the formation of coherent vortical structures that are advected downstream by the background flow. title: Investigation of magnetic-field effects on photomultiplier tubes for the first Large-Sized Telescope of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
abstract: Photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) are widely used in imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes. Their response can depend on the telescope pointing direction through changes in their orientation relative to the geomagnetic field. Such a dependence was indicated during the calibration campaign of the CTAO LST-1. abstract: Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs) will become mandatory starting in December 2027 under the European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) [8]. Although previous studies have highlighted significant differences among SBOM generators, the reasons for these discrepancies remain unknown, as does whether they stem from implementation errors or deliberate design choices. title: Journeys of Parents with LGBTQ+ Children: How Trauma and Healing Reshape Identity and (Mis)Informating Practices
abstract: This study examines how parents of LGBTQ+ individuals in South Korea navigate the emotional rupture fueled by fear, isolation, and disorientation after learning their children’s queer identity, encounter queer-related (mis)information as a way of coping with this emotional toll, and come to listen to queer realities relationally. title: Depressive symptoms are reflected differently across digital contexts
abstract: As more of everyday life takes place online, digital behavior may provide a potential window into how depressive symptoms are reflected in daily life. Yet digital mental health studies have produced mixed findings. These inconsistencies may partly reflect how digital behavior is measured: self reported use, single device studies, and aggregate screen time can obscure differences across devices, activities, and patterns of engagement. abstract: Undesired information such as harmful content and private data propagates through Multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) via direct training and indirect cross-linguistic spread. Multilingual Machine Unlearning (MMU) aims to remove such information, yet its evaluation remains underexplored, leaving unclear whether unlearning truly eliminates target knowledge across all languages. title: Cryopower Unfrozen: No Carte Blanche under International Law for Sea Ice Geoengineering to Restore the Arctic Ocean
abstract: In response to the unprecedented environmental pressures on the Arctic marine cryosphere, sea ice geoengineering (SIGE) has recently emerged as a potential strategy to restore the Arctic marine environment. The restoration of the environment has been affirmed by international courts as part of states’ due diligence obligations or as a form of reparation deriving from state responsibility. title: Design development and performance evaluation of a novel bistable metallic shells enabled underwater glider
abstract: Underwater gliders are renowned for their endurance to explore marine resources. However, their slower response and high energy consumption, stemming from slower, less efficient ballast systems, limit their application in shallow estuarine waters with complex conditions, e.g., uneven, rocky floors that require rapid depth adjustments. abstract: We present the main submarine geomorphological features of the Gran Canaria island at a scale of 1:1,000,000 to improve seafloor knowledge. In 2024, two oceanographic cruises were carried out around the island of Gran Canaria, covering an area of ∼ 21,000 km2, from 54 to 3650 mwd. abstract: Planktonic foraminiferal assemblages preserved in deep-sea sediments provide valuable information on assemblage composition, diversity, and upper-ocean habitat structure. However, baseline assemblage data from remote high-seas regions of the western North Pacific remain comparatively limited. title: A rapid UAV LiDAR-based method for sea ice thickness retrieval in the Arctic
abstract: Sea ice thickness (SIT) is a critical parameter for polar navigation and operational safety, yet existing observations remain limited in spatial resolution, timeliness, or field accessibility. This study presents a rapid, high-resolution unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) LiDAR workflow for SIT retrieval using point cloud data acquired during the Following Arctic/Antarctic iCE 2024 (FACE2024) Expedition aboard the R/V Zhong Shan Da Xue Ji Di. title: Portrayal of the deep sea: Haeckel’s Atolla wyvillei, the challenger expedition, and the boundaries of science and illustration
abstract: The Challenger expedition marked a turning point for marine biology, revolutionizing the scientific research of ocean life. It yielded a report of 50 volumes totaling nearly 30,000 pages-a monumental result that remains unchallenged. Among its vast contributions are reports by Ernst Haeckel on previously unknown species of radiolarians and medusae, which stand out for their lasting influence on the taxonomy of marine organisms. abstract: To address the issue that current underwater glider deployments for in situ observation of the 3D structure of mesoscale eddies are largely guided by empirical knowledge rather than a systematic quantitative evaluation framework, this paper, based on a synthesized anticyclonic eddy field in the northern South China Sea, systematically evaluates the reconstruction performance of three array topologies (parallel, grid, and radial) through numerical simulations, and proposes a comprehensive metric integrating coverage, error, and correlation coefficient to assess the reconstruction performance. abstract: Abstract Existing underwater robotic platforms are typically designed around a single locomotion modality, such as drifting, gliding, or thruster-driven propulsion, limiting their adaptability across diverse tasks and operating environments. Drifting provides energy-efficient passive transport and is particularly well suited for collecting ambient flow information. abstract: Abstract To investigate the hydrodynamic interaction and drag-reduction potential of heterogeneous autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) formations during formation cruising, this study performs a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based analysis of a three-AUV heterogeneous formation consisting of one DARPA SUBOFF model and two Zebrafish 150 AUVs. abstract: The deep sea is increasingly recognized as vulnerable to anthropogenic pressures, including marine litter, yet large geographic gaps remain in our understanding of litter distribution and ecological interactions. Submarine canyon systems can act as conduits and accumulation zones for anthropogenic material, but data from the southwestern Atlantic are scarce. abstract: Ocean current interference is a critical factor affecting the path planning of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUV). In ocean current environments, conventional path planning algorithms often exhibit significant limitations in complex flow fields without proper consideration of current interference. abstract: The deployment of multiple Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) for large-scale oceanic search and mapping missions is frequently constrained by inefficient task assignment and strict collision avoidance protocols. abstract: Abstract Despite decades of research, fundamental gaps remain in our understanding of coral vital rates across taxa. abstract: Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) offers a promising pathway for evaluating wave energy converter–autonomous underwater vehicle (WEC–AUV) systems in the laboratory, where a mix of laboratory-scale waves and full-scale AUVs present significant challenges for conventional testing approaches. This study aims to develop and validate an HIL testing framework that reproduces wave forces and dock motions for WEC-AUV systems by integrating wave tank experiments with numerical simulations. abstract: An autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) is an important operation platform in ocean exploration engineering, and the operation state of its actuator directly determines the navigation safety. However, the marine environment is complex and changeable, and the state signal characteristics of autonomous underwater vehicles are complex and vulnerable to noise interference. title: An assessment of the multi-scalar risks and mitigative responses of Arctic cruise shipping
abstract: The rapid growth of Arctic cruise ship operations, driven by climate change-induced sea ice melt and increasing tourism demand, has raised significant concerns regarding the risks of such activities. This literature review synthesises the academic and grey literature published between January 2010 and April 2026 to address two research questions: (1) How do the risks of Arctic cruise ship operations and related touristic activities manifest across micro, meso, and macro scales? title: Assessment of Sea Surface Wind Measurements from Wave Gliders in Tropical Cyclones
abstract: Reliable in situ observations of sea surface wind (SSW) in tropical cyclones (TCs) remain extremely limited because of the difficulty of operating conventional observing platforms under severe weather conditions. Autonomous, uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs), such as Wave Gliders (WGs), offer a promising solution, but their observational reliability under TC conditions has not been systematically assessed. title: Distributed adaptive safety-critical coverage control of multiple autonomous underwater vehicles
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of distributed adaptive safety-critical coverage control for multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), and proposes a novel distributed control strategy to simultaneously ensure the safety and coverage of multiple AUVs. For AUVs with disturbances, a hierarchical control strategy is established to alleviate the design difficulty caused by complex AUV models or tasks, enhancing the practicality of the design. title: A new species of Bathyeliasona (Annelida, Polynoidae) from the abyssal plain of the eastern Indian Ocean
abstract: A new species of deep-sea polynoid, Bathyeliasona oceanxplorer sp. nov ., is described from the abyssal plain located in international waters between Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands in the eastern Indian Ocean from a single specimen collected at a depth of 4977 m. abstract: In this study, a numerical investigation on hydrodynamic characteristics of a cruise liner in the Gulf of Guinea was performed using ANSYS Fluent-based Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. The Gulf of Guinea presents severe operational challenges for maritime vessels due to complex oceanographic conditions including strong seasonal currents, elevated monsoon wave energy, and variable bathymetry. title: Formation control for multiple similar autonomous underwater vehicles with dynamic gaps via deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Dynamic gaps between simulation and real world environments are the major challenge for the implementation of deep reinforcement learning (RL) based formation control methods in systems composed of multiple similar autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), mainly involving hydrodynamic parameters and unknown disturbances. title: Age and origin of the Yilki Shore Platform, Encounter Bay, South Australia
abstract: Situated between Rosetta Head and the mouth of the Inman River on southern Fleurieu Peninsula, South Australia, the Yilki Shore Platform is a marine-abraded, seaward-sloping shore platform primarily developed on calcarenite. “Whole-rock” amino acid racemisation analyses reveal that the calcarenite is of Late Pleistocene age correlating with the Last Interglacial (MIS 5e; 132–115 ka), and the Upper Member of the Bridgewater Formation. title: The habitat use of ariid catfishes in coral reefs in northeastern Brazil
abstract: Ariidae species occur across a wide range of habitats from freshwater to fully marine environments and are typically associated with soft-bottom substrates. However, they are sometimes associated with hard-bottom substrates such as coral reefs, but such association is poorly documented. This study describes the occurrence and habitat use of six ariid species in the coral reef of Penha Beach, northeastern Brazil. abstract: Abstract During the Middle and Late Pleistocene, the Earth experienced rapid millennial-scale climate and sea-level fluctuations associated with 100 kyr-glacial-interglacial cycles. However, understanding of the timing and amplitude of these changes, and their impact on coral reef ecosystems remains incomplete. title: Impulsive consensus of multi-AUV systems under random packet losses and switching communication topologies
abstract: This paper studies the impulsive consensus problem for multiple autonomous underwater vehicle (multi-AUV) systems with switching communication topologies and random packet losses. To alleviate the bandwidth limitation of underwater acoustic communication, a periodic impulsive communication strategy is adopted, where neighboring AUVs exchange information only at discrete sampling instants. title: Backstepping Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for ROV Under Multi-Source Time-Varying Disturbances
abstract: To address the reduced motion control accuracy of underwater cleaning remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) caused by strongly coupled nonlinear dynamics and multisource time-varying disturbances, this study proposes a backstepping adaptive sliding mode control (B-ASMC) strategy. abstract: The interaction between climate-driven thermal disturbances and local anthropogenic pressures increasingly shapes coral reef trajectories. abstract: Reliable cooperative control is investigated for heterogeneous autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) formations with uncertain dynamics and control-channel deception attacks. abstract: This paper investigates the trajectory tracking control problem with prescribed performance for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) subject to lumped disturbances composed of model uncertainties and unknown time-varying external disturbances. abstract: For underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), homing path planning with initial and terminal attitude constraints is essential for feasible docking. abstract: Abstract This work investigates physical-layer security of underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) systems under covert non-line-of-sight (NLOS) eavesdropping caused by scattered photons. abstract: Steep submarine canyons pose challenges to deep-water pipeline routing because of rugged terrain and slide-related hazards. This study integrates 3D seismic data, shipborne and autonomous underwater vehicle bathymetry, sub-bottom profiles, sediment testing, and numerical simulations to characterize engineering geological conditions and examine local terrain effects on slide–pipeline interaction in the Qiongdongnan Basin. abstract: Hydrogen is increasingly regarded as a promising option for maritime decarbonisation, yet its implementation depends on far more than propulsion feasibility. abstract: Abstract Kelp forests are declining worldwide, but Patagonian giant kelp forests ( Macrocystis pyrifera ) appear to have remained stable over the past half-century. abstract: Comprehensive biodiversity inventories of abyssal and hadal ecosystems remain rare due to the financial and logistical challenges associated with operating in the deepest parts of the ocean. abstract: The impact and transport patterns of the 2011 Fukushima Dai-ichi Nuclear Power Plant (FDNPP) accident-derived radiocesium in the tropical North Pacific remain poorly understood. institutions: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

title: ETHNOMEDICINAL STUDIES OF GENUS: Butea USED BY THE ETHNIC GROUPS OF NORTH COASTAL ANDHRA PRADESH
abstract: The tribal people depend on forests for their livelihood and most of the rural people still depend on traditional medicine as a primary healthcare source. The paper deals with the ethnomedicinal treatment of Butea monosperma and Butea superba by the tribals of north coastal Andhra Pradesh. A total twenty-three practices recorded of which 6 are newly reported or less known.
journal: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)

title: Approximation of reception coefficients of cosmic ray neutron components for latitude measurements
abstract: When solving scientific and applied problems such as latitude monitoring, it is important to correctly exclude primary cosmic-ray variations from observational data. At any point in the world, primary variations with an hourly resolution are determined globally by the spectrographic method based on data from the worldwide network of neutron monitors. Therefore, the aim of this study was to develop and implement a monitoring data correction method primarily intended to obtain reception coefficients as a function of latitude. title: Upscale Hotel Markets in Vietnam’s Coastal Tourism Cities: Supply, Demand and the Risk of Overbuilding
abstract: Vietnam’s coastal destinations absorbed the largest share of hotel investment during the country’s post-pandemic tourism recovery, and by the third quarter of 2025 they held roughly 60 per cent of a national midscale-to-luxury stock of more than 192,000 rooms. This paper asks whether the upscale room supply now under construction in those destinations can be absorbed by plausible demand growth, and it develops a transparent method for answering that question when only published aggregates are available. The analysis rests on an accounting identity linking arrivals, length of stay and room stoc
journal: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies

title: Additions to the Pteridophyte flora of the Batanes Islands, a biogeographic link between the Philippines and Taiwan
abstract: Situated between Luzon and Taiwan, the Batanes archipelago forms an important biogeographic link between the floras of the Philippines and Taiwan. Ferns and lycophytes, many of which are capable of effective long-distance dispersal, are well represented on oceanic islands, and nearly 100 species have previously been recorded from Batanes. Based on a two-week botanical expedition to Batan and Itbayat Islands in 2026, we report six additions to the pteridophyte flora of the archipelago: Adiantum capillus-veneris subsp. lanyuanum, Cephalomanes atrovirens, Chingia paucipaleata, Crepidomanes kurzii

title: First graduates of the Hydrographic Institute of the Northern Sea Route (1935–1939): The work of graduates in the arctic in 1938–1940
abstract: This article is part of a publication series about students who entered the newly established Hydrographic Institute of the Northern Sea Route in 1935 and received their degrees as hydrographic engineers between 1938 and 1940. Consideration is given to the work of Hydrographic Institute graduates in the Arctic during the pre-World War II period.

title: Complex interplay of forcings drives Indian vegetation and summer monsoon variability during MIS 11
abstract: Marine Isotope Stage (MIS) 11 has long been considered a unique Quaternary interglacial stage due to its orbital similarities with the Holocene, persistent high atmospheric CO 2 concentrations and its extended duration, which triggered an unusual polar ice-sheet loss. Despite its importance, variability of the Asian summer monsoon, as well as its impacts on vulnerable tropical forests, during MIS 11 remain unexplored. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Northern smoothtongue: technochemical composition, nutritional and biological value
abstract: The aim: To study the size and weight characteristics, nutritional and biological value of the Northern smooth-tongue Leuroglossus schmidti caught in the Sea of Okhotsk in the spring. Materials and methods: Samples of the Northern smoothtongue were collected during a voyage on the research vessel «Professor Kaganovsky» in the Sea of Okhotsk (coordinates 55°30’5 N 152°52’3 E) from March to May 2025, frozen and delivered to the laboratory of aquatic organism processing technology of the Pacific branch of «VNIRO» («TINRO»), where experimental studies were conducted. title: La playlist de David Lynch
abstract: Un repaso por la evolución de la dimensión musical del cine de David Lynch, estrechamente ligada al diseño sonoro de sus películas y a su singular propuesta narrativa. Como música de fondo suenan temas de Angelo Badalamenti, Julee Cruise, David Bowie, Rammstein, Roy Orbison y las composiciones del propio David Lynch —este es un ensayo que se lee mejor con Spotify o YouTube a la mano—.

title: Navigating knowledge gaps: An emissions inventory approach to understand plastic pollution from international shipping
abstract: Plastic pollution is a complex environmental problem, requiring tailored solutions based on an understanding of contributing sources and mechanisms. Shipping activities significantly affect local plastic loads and, to respond to this ongoing problem, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) is coordinating efforts to address plastic emissions from international shipping. A global, sector-specific assessment could inform such actions, but is currently not feasible due to fragmented and missing data. In this study, a generic plastic emissions inventory framework of ship-sourced plastic flow

title: Ecological risk and source apportionment of PAHs and OCPs in surface sediments of the Upper Gulf of Thailand
abstract: This study investigates the occurrence, distribution, and ecological risks of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) in surface sediments collected from 17 stations in the Upper Gulf of Thailand (uGoT). Total PAH concentrations ranged from 6.6 to 744.6 ng g -1 dw, with the highest concentrations recorded at the Chao Phraya river mouth, primarily driven by pyrogenic sources and localized petrogenic inputs from maritime activities. In contrast, total OCP concentrations (ranging from 159.0–1,657.7 ng g -1 dw) exhibited an offshore maximum, suggesting that the
institutions: Department of Marine and Coastal Resources

title: Two New Species and Nomenclatural Changes of Brassicaceae Burnett (Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic, Azerbaijan)
abstract: The family Brassicaceae Burnett is one of the important families because of its position in nature and its economic status in human life. This family is represented by 3,628 species from 328 genera in the world. 248 species from 74 genera were identified in the Republic of Azerbaijan, and 165 species from 66 genera in the territory of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. Later, taking into account taxonomic innovations and newly discovered species, 62 genera and 183 species belonging to them were registered in the territory. During the expedition, we discovered new species of Draba bryoides Wil

title: Grey eel catfish (Plotosus canius) fishing by women fishers in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh
abstract: The Sundarbans' women fishworkers play a crucial role in the delta's ecological economy by harvesting, processing, marketing, and inventing within the fishing sector. Through a case study in Koyra, a region in close proximity to the Sundarbans mangrove with a significant reliance on fisheries for local livelihoods, this study examined women's participation in small-scale fishing, particularly in grey eel catfish, Plotosus canius (locally known as Kain magur). During ‘Mora goan’ (the last phase of the full or new moon lunar cycle), a group of women, primarily widows and divorced women, fish Kai

title: A REVIEW OF HIGH-PRESSURE WATER-DRIVEN VALVE ACTUATORS: MECHANISMS, CYLINDERS, MATERIALS, AND SEALING TECHNOLOGIES
abstract: The shift towards sustainable and environmentally friendly industrial technologies has spurred a significant resurgence of interest in water hydraulics, particularly for high-pressure applications in sensitive environments such as nuclear power, food processing, and underwater robotics. This review examines high-pressure water-driven valve actuators, focusing on the design, materials, and sealing technologies of the driving cylinders. Gear-rack actuators serve as the primary case study, reflecting their widespread use in quarter-turn valve service, and are compared with alternative rotary and
journal: Journal of Manufacturing Science and Mechanical Engineering

title: Orchidaceae Spirito-Sanctensis: A taxonomic and conservation synopsis of orchid diversity in the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil
abstract: The diversity of Orchidaceae in the state of Espírito Santo, southeastern Brazil, was reassessed 40 years after the last comprehensive survey conducted for the region. The study was based on the examination of herbarium specimens, a critical review of the literature, and targeted field expeditions carried out in different phytophysiognomies. A total of 730 taxa (728 species, one subspecies, and one variety) were documented, representing an increase of 130 taxa compared to the 600 previously recorded by Augusto Ruschi. Of these, 39% are currently included in a threat category on the official Re

title: A rare Arctic record of Haliphron atlanticus (seven-arm octopus) from Bodø, Norway
abstract: Abstract Haliphron atlanticus Steenstrup, 1861, the seven-arm octopus, is a large deep-sea octopod with circumglobal distribution, yet it remains poorly documented due to its inaccessible mesopelagic to benthopelagic habitat and elusiveness. Here we report a rare observation, based on disarticulated remains recovered from a stranding event in Bodø, Arctic Norway (67.27°N, 14.43°E) in March 2026, following an initial report by local citizens. title: Development and Internal Validation of a Risk-Based Safe-Manning Framework for Wing-in-Ground Craft
abstract: Purpose. This study developed and computationally verified a function-based method for determining core operational crew for wing-in-ground (WIG) craft. Methods. A frozen 37-source corpus was mapped to six safety-critical functions, six mission phases, a competence matrix, and phase loads. Bounded integer compositions were tested using an exact scalar max-flow/min-cut model, 20% reserve, utilization caps, role-removal screening, and 10,000-trial simulation. title: Aqueous extract of Nasturtium officinale: a potential therapeutic approach to be explored in the fight against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: The rise in global bacterial resistance has made the development of new therapies an urgent challenge, positioning Pseudomonas aeruginosa as a critical priority pathogen. In this context, phytotherapy stands out due to the wide diversity of bioactive compounds with antimicrobial potential. journal: Journal of the Iranian Chemical Society

title: Hantavirus: biology, immune responses, and pathogenesis
abstract: Abstract The recent Andes virus (ANDV) outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise has raised global public health alarms due to its dangerous ability to person-to-person spread. Hantavirus infections primarily manifest as hemorrhagic fever with Eurasian renal syndrome (HFRS) and Americas hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), both characterized by endothelial manifestation. Two principal mechanisms, virus-mediated cytopathy and host-driven immunopathology, have been proposed to account for the pathological progression, while their interplay is yet to be fully explored. title: Mercury cycling during the last glacial period in Arctic Lake El'gygytgyn, NE Russia
abstract: ABSTRACT Tectonic processes play a key role in the global mercury (Hg) cycle on geological timescales, by mobilising Hg from deep Earth reservoirs to the surface. These natural fluxes also introduce a dynamic component to the terrestrial Hg cycle that can interact with other environmental signals and influence Hg delivery to sedimentary records. For records extracted from tectonically active regions, this could complicate, obscure or even preclude accurate interpretation of sedimentary Hg responses to past centennial‐ to millennial‐scale environmental shifts. title: Extreme challenges in the coldest continent: 10 years of Antarctic adventure sport tourism (2014–2024), participation trends and qualitative risk analysis
abstract: Abstract Adventure tourism in Antarctica has expanded significantly over the past couple of decades and has brought along new challenges for managing human and environmental safety in one of the world’s most remote regions. This study provides a retrospective qualitative analysis of participation in and associated risks with adventure sport tourism activities conducted between 2014 and 2024, using data obtained from the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO). Activities examined include kayaking, polar plunges, scuba diving, mountaineering, skiing and endurance events.

title: South Atlantic range extensions of the caridean shrimps Synalpheus pandionis Coutière, 1909 (Alpheidae) and Periclimenaeus perlatus (Boone, 1930) (Palaemonidae), identified using an integrative taxonomic approach
abstract: We report range extensions for two species of caridean shrimp, Synalpheus pandionis Coutière, 1909 and Periclimenaeus perlatus (Boone, 1930), from the continental shelf off Bahia, Brazil. These records represent the southernmost occurrences for both species in the south-western Atlantic. Synalpheus pandionis was found associated with the sponge Mycale ( Zygomycale ) angulosa (Duchassaing & Michelotti, 1864), while P. perlatus was found associated with the sponge Aplysina fistularis (Pallas, 1766). title: Mercury in Fish from Guanabara Bay, Southeast Brazil: Tissue-Specific Accumulation and Human Health Risks
abstract: Abstract Guanabara Bay is Brazil’s second-largest bay and has a long history of intense industrial and domestic pollution. Some local communities rely on fish as a primary protein source, justifying an assessment of mercury (Hg) contamination. This study determined total mercury (THg) concentrations in nine fish species and evaluated the toxicological risks associated with human consumption. One hundred specimens were analyzed, and samples of muscle, liver, and gills were collected. title: İnsansız Deniz Araçları ve Savaşın Değişen Doğası: Modern Dönemde Deniz Operasyonlarının Teknolojik Dönüşümü
abstract: Teknolojik gelişmelerin 21. yüzyılda kaydettiği ilerleme modern savaş ortamı ve silahlanma yarışı gibi alanlar üzerinde gözlemlenebilir değişimler yaratmaktadır. Bu süreçte yapay zekâ, makine öğrenimi ve diğer modern teknolojilerin güvenlik sektöründe kullanımının yaygınlaşması bir taraftan askeri silah sistemlerinin kabiliyetini artırırken, diğer taraftan kara, hava ve deniz alanlarındaki operasyonel verimliliği ileri boyuta taşımaktadır. Bu kapsamda, gerek deniz yüzeyinde gerekse altında birçok farklı görev üstlenebilen insansız deniz araçları (İDA) mevcut konjonktürde deniz operasyonlarında
journal: Akdeniz Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi

title: Structural attributes of dominant seagrass species modulate invertebrate assemblages within the Shark Bay world Heritage Area
abstract: Abstract The structural complexity of seagrass meadows plays a central role in shaping the diversity and composition of associated invertebrate assemblages. In the Shark Bay World Heritage Area of Western Australia, the dominant species Amphibolis antarctica and Posidonia australis differ markedly in their above- and below-ground morphology, yet the invertebrate assemblages they support remain poorly characterised. title: ‘As miserable as a bandicoot’: 150 years of human-wildlife conflict with bandicoots in New South Wales, c. 1804–1954
abstract: Context Narratives around declines and extinctions of critical weight range (CWR) mammals in Australia have focused on the dramatic impacts of invasive predators and habitat decline. For some species, human-wildlife conflict has had a greater impact than previously perceived. Aims We aim to explore the role of human-wildlife conflict in the decline of bandicoots in New South Wales (NSW). A greater understanding of past actions and beliefs concerning bandicoots can shed light on current perceptions. title: Western Writings on Ottoman Algeria: Between Historical Documentation, Ideological Bias, and Military Intelligence
abstract: This paper investigates Western writings on Ottoman Algeria as more than mere historical documentation.The records left behind by consuls, diplomats, captives, clergymen, travelers and intelligence agents form a rich and diverse body of texts that, despite this diversity, converges on a single common purpose: gathering strategic intelligence that paved the way for the French invasion of Algeria in 1830.The research rests on four main axes: a typology of Western authors and their backgrounds; the writing techniques used by these authors and their sources of knowledge; the political, religious,

title: From electrocardiography to energetics: methods, constraints, and practical considerations for heart rate biologging in small animals
abstract: Physiological biologging is a flourishing field enabling researchers to answer fundamental questions about animal behaviour and physiology in their natural environment. As biologging devices are further miniaturised their use on small species (< 1.5 kg) is increasing-making this a pivotal time to review how this technology is being used, and what technological limitations and practices users must be aware of, to answer questions in small animals. title: Species diversity of Gelidium (Gelidiales, Rhodophyta) from Indonesia evaluated by molecular and morphological data, with descriptions of G. balteumsp. nov. and G. brevifolium sp. nov.
abstract: Gelidium from tropical waters has frequently been overlooked due in part to its small size and superficial morphological similarity even between phylogenetically different species, presenting a major challenge to our understanding of global biodiversity. To assess the diversity of Gelidium in Indonesia, specimens were collected on intertidal rocky shores of Bali and Lombok Islands over the period of 2009–2026. title: Evolutions of Non‐oxygenated Compounds in Sunlit Subarctic Thermokarst Pond Surface Waters
abstract: Abstract With global climate change, ground subsidence caused by permafrost thawing leads to the formation of thermokarst ponds, where organics from eroding permafrost accumulate in part as dissolved organic matter (DOM). Surface waters were collected from two subarctic thermokarst ponds with distinct characteristics: one palsa‐affected pond, which is organic‐rich, and another lithalsa‐affected pond, which is organic‐poor. title: First record of Terpsinoë musica Ehrenberg (Bacillariophyta) from Uganda and South Africa
abstract: African records of Terpsinoë musica Ehrenberg are scarce and mainly restricted to North and West Africa, with previous East African reports limited to Ethiopia and fossil material from Kenya. Here, we extend the geographic distribution of this species in Africa by including two new observations in East and Southern Africa: the first observation of the species in Uganda (East Africa) was in the guts of Oreochromis leucostictus collected from Lake George. title: Scientific Research as Geopolitical Practice: Innovation, Diplomacy, Subversion
abstract: This article examines scientific research as a geopolitical practice. Drawing from IR literature on innovation in geopolitics, scholarship on science diplomacy and hybrid warfare theory, the article suggests that scientific research is best understood as a practice that simultaneously aims at furthering the national interest and at tackling global challenges through diplomatic means. title: Look-up tables for complex refractive index correction of particle sizes measured by common research-grade optical particle counters
abstract: Optical particle counters (OPCs) are widely used to measure the aerosol particle number size distribution over a large size range encompassing sub- and super-micron diameters. The measurement principle of OPCs is based on the dependence of light scattering on particle size. However, this dependence is not monotonic at all sizes as light scattering also depends on the particle composition (i.e., the complex refractive index, m ) and morphology. title: A 400‐Year Antarctic Ice‐Core Perchlorate Record Reveals Variability in Stratospheric Chlorine Chemistry
abstract: Abstract Perchlorate (ClO 4 − ) in polar ice preserves past chlorine oxidation chemistry; however, multi‐centennial Antarctic ClO 4 − records and the mechanisms controlling their variability remain poorly constrained. Here, we present the first 400‐year (1616−2016) ClO 4 − record from an Antarctic ice core, revealing two regimes separated around 1980. Before 1980, ClO 4 − variability is primarily controlled by natural drivers. title: ‘My Single True Activity’: Sinéad Morrissey’s Found Architecture and Self-Conscious Ecopoetics
abstract: In this article, I will closely read Northern Irish poet Sinéad Morrissey’s more recent work to articulate a ‘found architectural’ mode of poetic attention. Her intricately formal poetry explores its own potential as an ecopoesis or ‘housebuilding’, self-consciously addressing climate catastrophe in ironising domestic registers and typographies. I argue that poems like ‘Found Architecture’, ‘Meteor Shower’ and ‘The Italian Chapel’ foreground the limits and complications of human-made artifice in the context of the overwhelming threat of environmental collapse. title: Free Space Optics: Present Applications and Emerging Future Challenges
abstract: Free Space Optics (FSO) is a communication method that uses open space as the medium between transceivers, which must be in line of sight (LOS) for successful optical signal transmission. The medium can be air, outer space, or a vacuum. This system is suitable for communication in various environments and offers advantages like high bandwidth and no need for spectrum licensing. However, FSO performance depends on atmospheric conditions, as factors such as rain, fog, haze, physical obstructions, scattering, and turbulence can affect transmission. journal: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies

title: Few large tree hollows in an endangered peri-urban ecosystem highlights the need to restore suitable habitat for dependent woodland fauna
abstract: Context Tree hollows are essential habitat resources used by fauna in woody ecosystems globally. In addition to extensive historical and ongoing clearing, human use of woodlands has left remnants with structurally modified tree assemblages, including reductions in large hollow-bearing trees. Aims We aimed to assess tree hollow resources for dependent, arboreal vertebrates in fragmented, peri-urban woodlands. title: Selection strategy for preserving physical fields in deep coal fidelity coring
abstract: Selecting preserving parameters is key to deep fidelity coring and cost reduction. For achieving cost-effective fidelity coring under the dominant controlling factors, first, this study employed local outlier factor algorithm to screen homogeneous samples. Then, the physico-mechanical response laws of coal and antagonistic mechanism were investigated through orthogonal test of temperature and pressure. title: Nonlinear composite observer-based predefined-time nonsingular terminal sliding mode fault tolerant control for distributed drive electric vehicles with unknown disturbances
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a novel predefined-time nonsingular terminal sliding mode control scheme based on a nonlinear composite observer for distributed drive electric vehicles subject to in-wheel motor fault and unknown disturbances. Firstly, a composite observer is designed using linear matrix inequalities and Lyapunov functions to achieve simultaneous estimation of the system states, disturbances and fault factors. title: A new species of Zonites Montfort, 1810 from the Aegean (Chtapodia, Greece): islet endemic and critically endangered
abstract: The species Zonites whittakeri n. sp. (Zonitidae) is described from two islets off Mykonos Island (Cyclades, Aegean, Greece). A small population of the species persists on the islet of Chtapodia, whereas only subfossil shells were recovered from Tragonisi islet, suggesting that the species is locally extinct. The species is diagnosed on the basis of shell morphology as well as its reproductive system, and is distinguished from congeners by a combination of characters including a medium-sized shell with 5.2–5.8 nearly flat whorls, shallow sutures, light brown colour, much paler underside; keel

title: Ontogenetic shift to more efficient locomotor morphology coincides with migration in anadromous alewife, Alosa pseudoharengus (Wilson, 1811) (Clupeomorpha; Alosidae)
abstract: Anadromous fishes experience different locomotory demands throughout their life cycle. We evaluated how functional locomotory traits change over ontogeny in anadromous Alosa pseudoharengus (Alewife). We found that as juveniles, a period in which predator avoidance, food acquisition and manoeuvring in complex environments are critical to survival, Alewife have traits conducive to higher turning performance. title: From Anthropocentrism to Hydrocentric Ethics: A Qur’anic Reading of QS. Al-Anbiya’ [21]:30 and the Global Water Crisis
abstract: The global water crisis raises fundamental questions about how human relationships with water should be understood beyond its treatment as an economic resource. This study examines QS. Al-Anbiyā’ [21]:30 and related Qur’anic passages to develop a water-centered ethical perspective in response to contemporary ecological challenges. Employing qualitative library research and tafsīr mawdū’ī (thematic exegesis), the study analyzes classical and contemporary interpretations by al-Qurtubī, Tantāwī Jawharī, Ibn ‘Āshūr, and M. journal: Al-Fahmu Jurnal Ilmu Al-Qur an dan Tafsir

title: Under pressure: Use of hyperbaric chamber therapy for management of dissolved gas disorders in fish—15 cases (2015–2025)
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to describe clinical findings, treatment protocols, and outcomes in captive fish presenting with ocular and/or buoyancy disorders attributed to dissolved gas disease undergoing novel treatment with hyperbaric therapy. METHODS: Electronic medical records were reviewed for 15 teleost fish comprising 10 species housed at a public aquarium and treated between 2015 and 2025 with hyperbaric chamber therapy for exophthalmos (n = 8), intraocular gas (n = 5), buphthalmos (n = 5), and/or positive buoyancy (n = 7). title: Real-time geomagnetic vector field estimation method based on marginalized particle filters
abstract: Abstract In recent years, research has shown that geomagnetic navigation technology can be an important alternative to satellite navigation for the navigation and positioning of aircraft. Due to the limited information contained in the scalar geomagnetic field, studying the application of geomagnetic vector fields is significant for the development of geomagnetic navigation technology. title: INNOVATION PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT OF SELECTED BALKAN COUNTRIES BASED ON THE GLOBAL INNOVATION INDEX USING AN ENTROPY-BASED TOPSIS FRAMEWORK
abstract: Innovation constitutes a fundamental driver of sustainable economic growth, productivity improvement, and structural convergence with the European Union, particularly for Balkan and Western Balkan economies. However, the considerable heterogeneity observed in innovation performance across the region necessitates a multidimensional and comparative evaluation framework. title: Drivers of self-reported destination loyalty intentions in an emerging tourism destination: A PLS-SEM study of tourists in Da Nang, Vietnam
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractGrowing competition among global tourism destinations has made it essential to understand what drives tourists to intend to return and recommend a place. This study aims to examine the direct and indirect relationships among destination image, tourist motivation, perceived value, destination experience, destination satisfaction, and destination loyalty intentions in Da Nang, Vietnam, in order to identify the key drivers of self-reported tourist loyalty in an emerging tourism destination. title: Topography of the High Country, Ancient Spatial Transformation of Eastern Anatolia from Uruatri to Armenia
abstract: This article examines how the topography of Eastern Anatolia was described, named and given meaning in ancient sources, arguing that its mountains, valleys and river systems functioned less as a physical backdrop than as an active component of political strategy, imperial ideology and the construction of local identity and memory. The discussion runs from the Uruatri and Nairi confederations through the Kingdom of Urartu to the Persian-Achaemenid, Hellenic and Roman periods. title: Four new species and new distributional records for Australian caddisflies in the genus Ecnomus McLachlan (Trichoptera: Ecnomidae)
abstract: A recent surge in collection of fresh caddisfly material for molecular studies resulted in the discovery of four new species of Ecnomus, the first since a major review of Australian members of the genus by Cartwright in 1990. Three of the new species are from north-eastern Queensland: E. giblini sp. nov., E. lesteri sp. nov. and E. mundyi sp. nov., the latter resulting from recognition that E. apiculatus Cartwright, 1990 comprises two distinct species. The fourth new species, E. barwonensis sp. nov., also derives from a split from another species, the very similar E. continentalis Ulmer, 1916.

title: Self-consistent fragmentation in dynamically dense turbulent fibre suspensions
abstract: Fragmentation of slender fibres by turbulence controls length distributions in many natural and industrial suspensions, yet most theories assume a prescribed carrier flow, and treat fibres as dilute and dynamically passive. Here, we develop a self-consistent kinetic description for fragmentation in the opposite limit of sufficiently dense fibre suspensions that back-react on the turbulence. Starting from an Euler–Bernoulli model in the quasi-static regime, we show that collective resistive-force drag defines a cut-off span upper L Subscript c L c $L_c$ inside the inertial range, marking the cr
institutions: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Genova

title: Between Segregation and Permeability: The VOC’s Spatial Dilemma in Zeelandia Facing External Actors and Intervening Groups (1624–1662)
abstract: Abstract This study re-evaluates the “dual city” model through the case of the VOC’s Zeelandia in the seventeenth century. It argues that the settlement’s spatial order was crucially shaped not only by Dutch-indigenous relations but also by an external force: Chinese pirate-merchant confederations. This Chinese intermediary group, forming the socio-economic core, fostered a colonial dynamic of simultaneous dependence and distrust. Spatially, this crystallized into a “confrontation model” of segregation—with rigid yet economically permeable boundaries between the Dutch Fort and Chinese Town, wh

title: Post-2020 conservation priorities are threatened by global mining
abstract: Abstract The United Nations has committed to halting and reversing biodiversity loss by 2030. Despite this commitment, mining remains a major driver of biodiversity decline, particularly in conservation priority zones (CPZs) and areas with high species extinction risk. Regardless of growing awareness, the full extent of current and future mining threats to biodiversity remains inadequately quantified, limiting effective global conservation strategies. Here, we quantify the threats of 145,000 km² of current mining land to biodiversity. We find that 34% (49,000 km²) of these mining areas overlap

title: From one tree to the canopy: an evolutionary design trajectory for tethered robotics in forest environments
abstract: Forest robotics has largely evolved along a ground-first and flight-dominant trajectory, treating the canopy as a region to observe or briefly access rather than a habitat to inhabit. In this Perspective, we propose an alternative canopy-first framework in which robots operate through anchoring, suspension, and tension-mediated interaction with the environment. We trace the progression from ground and aerial systems to perching mechanisms, identifying their shared limitation as transient canopy interaction. Tether-based robots instead enable sustained presence by transforming branches into str

Vaughn College of Aeronautics and Technology

title: A Competitive Model via k WTA Network for Multi‐Agent Systems Considering Noise and Communication Disturbances
abstract: ABSTRACT The ‐winners‐take‐all (WTA) problem, as a competitive selection strategy, is crucial in multi‐agent systems. However, existing noise‐robust WTA networks mainly address noise while overlooking communication disturbances. The coexistence of both factors significantly degrades solution accuracy and hinders distributed consensus estimation. To address these issues, this paper first proposes an accelerated‐convergence and noise‐tolerant WTA (ACNT‐WTA) network by introducing a nonlinear activation function and an error‐integral term. Second, a robust consensus estimator is developed and int

title: Measuring Market Accessibility of Insular Areas based on Network Distance and Shipment Cost
abstract: In this paper, we calculate the two-sided (consumer and producer) market accessibility of the Greek islands, based on different measures of transport cost, namely, the actual network distance and the freight shipment cost from/to mainland regions and between them. For this purpose, we employ a unique micro-dataset of 1,026,469 shipments for the year 2021 originated from the platform of Islands’ Transport Equivalent for firms. The shipment cost refers to the receipts of payments made by firms for outsourcing transport services to companies with public-use truck vehicles. The findings show the i
institutions: Centre for Planning and Economic Research

title: Understanding Obese Tourists’ Travel Intentions: Integrating Social Identity and Complexity Theories
abstract: Obese tourists represent a growing yet underexamined market segment whose decision-making processes remain insufficiently understood within tourism development research. This study investigates the psychological and experiential factors shaping obese tourists’ travel intentions by integrating social identity and complexity theories. Data were collected from 400 obese tourists in Greece and analysed using fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), complemented by Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA). Findings reveal three distinct consumer pathways leading to high travel intentions: (a)

title: Iron Age Trade in Bronze Age Scarabs at el-Ahwat, Israel
abstract: A newly discovered scarab from the 2024 excavation season at el-Ahwat features a well-known depiction of an Egyptian king on a chariot – a hallmark of Ramesside royal iconography. Similar scarabs from the Southern Levant are known from Late Bronze Age funerary contexts, but the el-Ahwat scarab was found in a secure Iron Age IB context, at a site that was not settled during the previous Late Bronze period. Therefore, this scarab, together with a previously published rich glyptic assemblage from the site, offer a unique data point to the corpus of Egyptian-style glyptic material in Canaan after

title: Adapting digital humanities tools for biodiversity science: A case study in field notebook digitization and the Extended Specimen Network.
abstract: Field notebooks represent invaluable primary sources of biodiversity information, yet their rate of digitization has lagged behind that of natural history specimens. This disparity stems from multiple challenges, including the perception of notebooks as personal rather than institutional records, their complex and idiosyncratic content, and the lack of standardized protocols for creating discoverable linkages between field notebooks and their associated specimens—a key component of the Extended Specimen Network concept. This paper presents a case study demonstrating an efficient, specimen-firs

title: Design and Stability Analysis of an Aerosonde UAV Using Linear Quadratic Regulator Control
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly important in surveillance, environmental monitoring, mapping, and scientific research, where flight stability and control performance are essential for safe and reliable operation. This study focuses on the modeling and stability analysis of an Aerosonde UAV using a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control approach. The main objective is to develop an optimal state-feedback controller capable of improving the stability and dynamic response of the UAV. A mathematical model of the Aerosonde UAV is established using longitudinal and lateral

title: Policy responses to overtourism
abstract: Overtourism has emerged as one of the most debated challenges affecting major tourist destinations, with Italy frequently cited as a prominent case. This paper examines the policy responses to overtourism in Italy, focusing on how institutional arrangements, interest groups, and public discourse shape the management of tourism growth. Drawing on existing literature and emblematic cases - most notably Venice and Florence - the study argues that overtourism cannot be understood solely as the outcome of excessive visitor numbers. Instead, it results from long-term structural transformations, incl
publisher: Oñati International Institute for the Sociology of Law

title: Уточнения по типовым экземплярам северной пищухи Ochotona hyperborea (Pallas, 1811) (Lagomorpha, Ochotonidae) c Чукотки и Камчатки
abstract: The ambiguous situation with type specimens of the northern pika from Chukotka and Kamchatka is considered. The geographic location of the "type locality" for the nominal taxon Ochotona hyperborea (Pallas, 1811) is clarified. Nomenclatural confusion regarding the northern pika subspecies from Kamchatka is resolved. The classification of the subspecies Ochotona hyperborea minima (Sokolov, Ivanitskaya, Gruzdev, Heptner, 1994) as a synonym of the nominal subspecies Ochotona hyperborea hyperborea (Pallas, 1811) is confirmed. ?he intraspecific structure of Ochotona hyperborea in Northeast Asia is s
journal: Bulletin of the North-East Science Center
institutions: Institute of Biological Problems of the North

title: An integrated AHP-DEMATEL-QFD-FBS framework for designing an in-carriage intelligent delivery cart for China’s high-speed rail
abstract: To address the problem that manual delivery services cannot adequately meet the needs of complex service scenarios in crowded high-speed rail cars in China, this study proposes an integrated design framework for in-carriage intelligent delivery carts. User needs were collected through questionnaire surveys, semi-structured interviews, and behavioral observation, and a need indicator system for high-speed rail in-carriage delivery services was constructed. AHP was used to calculate the initial weights of need indicators, and DEMATEL was applied to revise the interrelationships among indicators.
institutions: North China Institute of Aerospace Engineering

title: WARDING OFF A ROMAN INVASION IN AETHIOPIA (UPPER NUBIA) WITH TALL ELEPHANT TALES? REVISITING PLINY, NATURALIS HISTORIA 6.186
abstract: Abstract It has recently been suggested that the Romans baulked at the idea of expanding their empire beyond Egypt into Aethiopia (Upper Nubia) during the principate of Nero because they were tricked into thinking that a powerful army equipped with war elephants awaited them. This discussion aims to demonstrate that such a view, based on a minority reading of Pliny, HN 6.186 that plumps for 3,000 elephants once being stationed on the island of Meroë, is difficult to support on both textual and contextual grounds.

title: ‘ALLOWING THE MOST CAPABLE TO LEAD’: ELITE LEADERSHIP, COMPETENCY, AND CAPACITY IN THE FIFTH-CENTURY ATHENIAN STRATĒGIA
abstract: This paper interrogates the paradox of military leadership in the Athenian democracy within the analytical framework of mass and elite political negotiation. Although the stratēgia (the Athenian generalship) was filled by election rather than by democratic lottery, thereby privileging wealthy, notable citizens as candidates for office, the institution simultaneously incorporated robust democratic oversight and availed the dēmos of benefits that attended the personal networks of the Athenian elite. Building on seminal works on the stratēgia , the paper demonstrates that the seemingly undemocrat

title: Boycotting racial capitalism
abstract: This article explores how racial capitalism in colonial Ireland was successfully challenged through the world’s first ever boycott. In the political economy of the late nineteenth-century, race and class were mutually constituted. The colonial landholding system of Ireland was a peripheral part of the British Empire. Catholic Irish tenants were cast as an inferior Celtic race in opposition to superior Anglo-Saxon Protestant English landlords. In County Mayo, in 1880, farm labourers refused to work for, or conduct business with, an English land agent—an historic moment of anti-colonial oppositi

title: Facial emotional responses to visual representations of deprived experiences in ICE environments: an exploratory analog space mission case study
abstract: Isolated, confined, and extreme (ICE) environments, such as space analog habitats, expose individuals to prolonged sensory and social deprivation, posing risks to psychological well-being. This exploratory study examined whether visual representations of everyday experiences unavailable during isolation elicit measurable facial emotional responses in analog astronauts. Data were collected from eight participants during two 14-day missions at the LunAres Research Station. Participants viewed short videos depicting deprived experiences (e.g., nature, social interaction, physical activity) at reg
