title: Practical Reflections on Nutritional Intervention to Regulate Body Hormone Levels Under Survival Conditions in Extreme Environments
abstract: Extreme working conditions such as high-altitude hypoxia, polar cold temperatures, and limited field supplies continuously impose physiological stress on the human body, keeping it in a prolonged state of high metabolic pressure. These harsh environments disrupt the dynamic balance of the endocrine system, triggering hormonal imbalances, physical performance decline, and weakened immune function—key factors contributing to reduced environmental adaptability and diminished work efficiency among field personnel. Based on practical experience in frontline physiological support, traditional pharma
journal: International Journal of Education and Social Development

title: Rethinking “Dead” Objects: Baya Pandang and the Cultural Lives of Iban Artifacts in Sarawak Museum Collections
abstract: Museums are among the most important institutions safeguarding indigenous cultural heritage. However, their colonial institutional origins have often obscured the original uses, values, and meanings that cultural materials hold for the indigenous communities who created and continue to claim them. This study examines three Iban cultural objects held in the Sarawak Museum that are widely assumed, within a Western museological frame, to have lost their significance once removed from their original cultural and social context. Drawing on Iban epistemology, and specifically the concept of baya pan

title: Un oracional del siglo xv en aljamía hebraicoaragonesa: textos y vocabulario
abstract: The following pages present the transcription of a small corpus of texts in Hebrew-Aragonese aljamía, datable to the last third of the fifteenth century. These texts appear to have originally formed part of a prayer book intended for women. An appended vocabulary is included as an accompanying resource.

title: Cultural heritage objects in lack of anchoring communities. An unfinished reflection on a relational ethics of care
abstract: The return of cultural artefacts taken during the colonial era seems to be a matter of course in our time. But what happens if the communities to whom these objects should be returned have for long ceased to exist and their successors are involved in a civil war? At the example of manuscripts taken from Ethiopia after the Battle of Maqdala, this contribution discusses ethical, legal and social issues (ELSI) surrounding such cultural heritage objects and calls into question the premises of recent calls for their return. This article discusses the history of these manuscripts and the case of mis

title: A systems-level analysis of energy, infrastructure, and economic viability of commercial hypersonic point-to-point (P2P)
abstract: Introduction Commercial hypersonic point-to-point (P2P) travel promises intercontinental flights in under 90 min, yet viability depends on systems-level integration of advanced technologies and infrastructure. This paper addresses the critical question of whether such travel can be technically feasible, economically viable, and environmentally sustainable within the coming decades. Methods We analyze two core technological pillars—Turbine-Based Combined Cycle (TBCC) propulsion and adaptive morphing aerodynamics—integrated within a multidisciplinary framework addressing thermal management. The

title: Tourism opportunities created by COVID-19 pandemic in Vhembe District Municipality, Limpopo Province, South Africa
abstract: Like all other forms of pervasive disruption, COVID-19 disrupted the world's economic and social systems, while creating opportunities for some and devastating threats for others.The South African economy, through the tourism sector, was highly affected.This paper, therefore, investigated the opportunities created by the COVID-19 pandemic in the tourism sector, with a focus on South Africa's Limpopo Province, specifically the Vhembe District Municipality.The study employed quantitative methods supported by a descriptive research design.For this study, a survey questionnaire was distributed to

title: A Design of Relief Logistics System by Axioms
abstract: Aim: This study scientifically addresses aid logistics operations, a subfield related to disaster management. It aims to conduct a design study that will guide those in authority. The study is in line with the classical logistics flow, with a value-oriented lean perspective, and eliminates processes that are not beneficial to disaster victims and include waste. The application of the axiomatic design approach in logistics, particularly in relief logistics, is relatively new and is expected to contribute to the existing literature gap in this area.Method: This study presented a complete, separa
journal: İstanbul Gelişim Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Dergisi

title: Integration of Photocatalytic Hydrogen Production with a Pem Fuel Cell-Based Off-Grid Cold Storage System: Thermodynamic, Dynamic Solar, and Environmental Performance Analysis across Three Technology Readiness Scenarios
abstract: This study presents a thermodynamic, dynamic solar, and environmental performance analysis of an integrated off-grid system combining photocatalytic hydrogen (H2) production with a proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell and a vapor-compression cold storage unit (R290) for a representative Mediterranean site (Adana, Türkiye, 37.0°N). A critical methodological advance over prior simulations is the adoption of a three-scenario framework explicitly grounded in real outdoor pilot data: Scenario S1 (STH = 0.9%, TiO2-CuO/P25); Scenario S2 (STH = 2.81%, Pd/TiO2); and Scenario S3 (STH = 10%, Z-scheme
journal: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science

title: Toward sustainable river tourism in the Brahmaputra River Basin: A socio-ecological perspective on climate adaptation, smart tourism, and community well-being
abstract: River tourism has emerged as an important means of promoting sustainable regional development, especially in ecologically and culturally important destinations. However, increasing climatic variability, technological transformation, and growing community expectations pose significant challenges to the long-term sustainability of the river tourism system. This study explores the future of sustainable river tourism in the Brahmaputra River Basin, Assam, India, through a socio-ecological perspective informed by resilience theory and socio-ecological systems (SES) theory. Using a qualitative explo

title: Characterization of recombinase-based genetic parts and circuits using nanopore sequencing
abstract: Abstract Recombinases are versatile enzymes able to perform the precise insertion, deletion, and rearrangement of DNA and can act as a foundation for programmable genetic logic and memory. Crucial for their use are accurate measurements of function. However, these are often laborious, time-consuming, and costly to collect. To address this, we develop a semi-automated workflow that combines low-cost liquid handling robotics, multiplexed long-read nanopore sequencing, and a supporting computational analysis tool to enable the high-throughput and detailed characterization of recombinase parts and

title: Women in Geosciences: an overview
abstract: This article examines the evolving role of women geoscientists, highlighting both progress and persistent inequalities that continue to shape this discipline. Although women now account for approximately 40% of researchers worldwide, their representation in Geosciences remains uneven, particularly in senior academic, leadership and decision-making positions. Data from the United States, Europe and at country level consistently reveal a pronounced “leaky pipeline,” whereby female representation declines progressively beyond the PhD stage, often falling below 20% among full professors. In Italy,
journal: JOURNAL OF GEOETHICS AND SOCIAL GEOSCIENCES

title: Entwining sound, space and narratives. Sound design approaches in exhibitions
abstract: This article explores the evolution of exhibition design, focusing on the integration of sound as a key narrative and experiential element. In recent decades, technological advances and discoveries in neuroscience have influenced the design of exhibition spaces, transforming them into multimodal experiences that go beyond mere visual engagement. Sound emerges as a central tool, capable of shaping the emotional, spatial, and narrative dimensions of exhibitions. Through case studies and interviews with exhibition and sound designers, I propose four sound design approaches – transparent, relation
journal: Museum Materials and Discussions Journal of Museum Studies

title: A new Lecidea species from Dismal Island (Antarctic Peninsula, Antarctica) supported by morphological, chemical, and nrITS phylogenetic evidence
abstract: Antarctica remains one of the least explored regions of the world in terms of lichen diversity, and many remote localities still harbor undescribed taxa. In this study, a new saxicolous lichen species belonging to the genus Lecidea is described from Dismal Island, located in the East Antarctic Peninsula region, based on an integrative taxonomic approach combining morphological, anatomical, chemical, and nrITS phylogenetic evidence. The examined material was collected from ice-free rocky habitats and deposited in the Erciyes University Lichen Herbarium (ERCH). Morphological and anatomical obser

title: DISTURBING THE HEARTH: ARISTARCHUS’ HELIOCENTRIC UNIVERSE AS COURT PARRHÊSIA
abstract: Abstract Aristarchus of Samos’ heliocentric model of the universe has usually been treated by modern scholars as an astronomical controversy somehow removed from the ideological concerns of the Ptolemaic court in which it was produced. This traditional approach has not fully accounted for the contemporary reception of the astronomer’s work, which included accusations of disruption, and even impiety, by scholarly rivals. Consideration of Aristarchus’ astronomy as an expression of scientific parrhêsia (frank speech) for his royal patron may help account for the hostile response. This article ide

title: Auto‐Tuning Weights Model Predictive Control for Three‐State Switching Cell Boost Converters
abstract: ABSTRACT This work presents an improved robust model predictive control (MPC) for DC‐DC boost converters operating under polytopic uncertainty. The proposed controller guarantees constraint satisfaction for voltage, current, and duty cycle bounds while ensuring asymptotic stability through a common quadratic Lyapunov function. To circumvent the computational complexity of online optimization, the control law is synthesized offline via semidefinite programming (SDP) using linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), yielding a static state‐feedback gain. An adaptive weight tuning algorithm is developed t

title: One new obligate commensal species of Coenaletes (Collembola, Coenaletidae) from the hermit crab Coenobita compressus (Crustacea, Coenobitidae) from Colombia
abstract: A new species of Coenaletes associated with the hermit crab Coenobita compressus H. Milne-Edwards, 1836, living in shells of Tegula atra Lesson, 1830 (Gastropoda: Tegulidae) on the seashores of Chocó, Colombia, is described and illustrated. The ontogenetic development, including measurements and ventral setation from first instar to adult, is provided. A key for the identification of the three species known in the genus is included.

title: Challenges of Goronyo Dam in the Agricultural Activities in Sokoto State 1984 -2025: From Historical Perspectives
abstract: Although the challenges encountered due to the Goronyo Dam disaster have caused agricultural backwardness, socio-economic and environmental effects in the area of study are worthy of discussion, therefore, this paper seeks to examine the nature and magnitude of the soil erosion, flooding, among others which is the major factor in this content. Also, identify the real causes of these and a historical review of the challenges of Goronyo Dam in agricultural activities in Sokoto State and other Dams as well. The paper has also examined the damages and changes it has coursed on vegetation covers, a
journal: African Journal of History and Archaeology

title: Lichens and lichenicolous fungi of Prins Karls Forland (Svalbard Archipelago)
abstract: The paper presents data on lichens and lichenicolous fungi for Prins Karls Forland (NW of Svalbard archipelago). For the island, 283 species of lichens and 21 lichenicolous fungi have been identified to date. Seventy species of lichens and 17 lichenicolous fungi are listed for the first time for the study area, of which Arthonia epipolytropa, Gyalecta peziza, Lasiosphaeriopsis christiansenii, Porpidia rugosa, and Sclerococcum protothallinum are reported for the first time for the Svalbard archipelago. The central part of Prins Karls Forland is the most studied now (157 taxa of investigated gro
institutions: Komarov Botanical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences

title: Undisciplining service design: Towards a grammar of possibility
abstract: Despite its ambitions to transform service systems, service design has been critiqued for reproducing the status quo and normalizing others into dominant social expectations. To move away from the circulation of hegemonic structures, the service design discipline needs to be challenged. Drawing on queer theory, this paper explores how service design can be undisciplined to create a grammar of possibility for making service systems otherwise. Based on experiences from an experimental seven-week service design research and education collaboration with hospital-based mental health services in Nor
institutions: Oslo School of Architecture and Design

title: PIRATE FESTIVALS AROUND THE WORLD AND THEIR SIGNIFICANCE FOR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT
abstract: The shift of contemporary tourism toward experiential, cultural, and thematic experiences creates new opportunities for destinations seeking differentiation, an extension of the tourism season, and stronger local entrepreneurship. In this context, pirate festivals constitute a distinctive form of event tourism because they combine historical or mythological narratives, harbour landscapes, re-enactments, parades, music, and participatory entertainment. This article examines three international pirate festivals—Pirates Week in the Cayman Islands, the Gasparilla Pirate Festival in Tampa, and the
journal: Global Journal of Engineering and Technology Advances
institutions: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

title: Biomorphology, transformation, and differentiation of joints and digits of the limbs in vertebrates
abstract: The study of morphogenesis, differentiation, and transformation of joints and digits of the vertebrate limbs is a fundamental task of comparative and veterinary anatomy, which can be directly integrated into the practice of clinical surgery and orthopedics. In this context, the anatomical and topographical features of the joints and limb autopodia of both extinct and extant vertebrate species are of particular importance. publisher: National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine
institutions: National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine

title: Books on the Road: Experiences of Reading in Robert Lee’s Travel Journal, 1824–1826
abstract: This article considers the reading life of the early-nineteenth-century British traveler and physician, Robert Lee (1793–1877). Drawing on evidence from Lee’s unknown manuscript travel journal penned during his travel to and residence in the Russian Empire in 1824–1826, where he worked as a family physician at Count M. S. Vorontsov’s household, it reconstructs his reading list and discusses the circumstances in which his reading acts took place. title: Rare and delicious: from monster to meal in Japanese gourmet fantasy manga
abstract: This study examines how gourmet fantasy manga, particularly Delicious in Dungeon and Campfire Cooking in Another World with My Absurd Skill, reconfigure monstrosity through the act of cooking and consumption. Drawing on textual, semiotic, and cultural hermeneutic analysis, the study argues that such transformations are not merely aesthetic, but grounded in deeper symbolic and cultural logics. The analysis identifies three key dimensions underlying this transformation. First, monsters are culturally and visually constructed through folkloric traditions and recognisable visual features. Drawing

title: Efficient Coverage Path Planning via Gradient-Based Rectangular Segmentation
abstract: Coverage Path Planning (CPP) is the task of finding a route that covers every point in a region or volume (i.e., all reachable cells) while avoiding obstacles. A typical CPP solution proceeds in two main stages: partitioning the environment into subregions, and planning a path within and between these regions. Effective segmentation is critical for smooth and efficient operation. For example, dividing the area into rectangular cells allows a simple back-and-forth (boustrophedon) sweep in each cell, exhaustively covering it without overlap. journal: Journal of Automation Mobile Robotics & Intelligent Systems
institutions: Wuhu Hit Robot Technology Research Institute

title: Detrás del telón. El motivo visual de la cortina en el cine de David Lynch
abstract: En esta segunda parte, el motivo visual de la cortina se expande más allá de su presencia escénica para convertirse en un mecanismo que altera la percepción del espacio y fractura la identidad en el cine de Lynch. Su función opera como un dispositivo liminar que articula refugio, ilusión y tránsito, donde lo inestable se convierte cada vez más en la norma.

title: IS Aba1‐ mediated crp‐osmC amplification enhances host‐associated fitness in Acinetobacter baumannii
abstract: Abstract Acinetobacter baumannii is a pathogen, highly adaptable to both hospital‐ and host‐associated environments. Understanding the genetic mechanisms underlying its adaptability is critical for controlling its persistence. Our study identified the crp‐osmC gene cluster, flanked by IS Aba1 elements, as a significant genetic structure undergoing amplification in A. baumannii . By experimentally mimicking the amplification of this gene cluster, we found that it substantially enhanced bacterial growth and competitive fitness, promoted survival in mouse serum, and improved colonization in murin
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Parachiloglanis gurungi, a new species of torrent catfish (Teleostei: Sisoridae) from western Bhutan
abstract: A new species of Parachiloglanis is described, based on specimens collected from the Kalikhola stream, a tributary of the Jaldhaka River, Samtse Dzongkhag, Bhutan. Parachiloglanis gurungi, new species, differs from its congeners in having a white bar on anterior flanks on dorsum of the body, white spot at the upper caudal-peduncle base, short and deep caudal peduncle, long predorsum, and differences in vomerine toothplate shape. title: From internal peace to the discourse of holy war: Tracing discursive continuities from the peace of god movement to the letters of Catherine of Siena
abstract: In medieval Latin Christendom, the discourse of peace was not confined to the mitigation of conflict and the prevention of war; rather, it developed into an ideological mechanism that oriented collective energies toward specific purposes. This study investigates how, in Medieval Western Europe, the discourse of peace, initially intended to bring violence to an end, gradually ceased to aim at its complete elimination and was transformed into a politico-religious mechanism that reordered and externalized violence. Within this framework, the study analyzes whether there exists an intellectual and

title: Behind the facades of Ctesiphon: an archaeometric study of stucco architectural decoration from the Sasanian and Early Islamic periods
abstract: Abstract Ctesiphon, the capital of the Sasanian Empire (ca. 224–651 CE), was a major center of political power and artistic production in Mesopotamia. Excavations conducted in the 1920s–30s by the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and the Metropolitan Museum of Art revealed an extensive corpus of stucco decorations from Sasanian and Early Islamic contexts. Their varied forms, decorative patterns, architectural contexts, and dates of production make these stuccos particularly valuable for comparative study. Despite their significance, however, the technology of stucco production at Ctesiphon has rema

title: Rediscovery, new records, and conservation assessment of the rare orchids Bletia concolor and B. similis (Orchidaceae) in Michoacán, Mexico
abstract: Background: Bletia comprises 56 species distributed throughout the Americas, with its principal center of diversity in Mexico. Among them are Bletia concolor and B. similis, two rare species for which information on morphology, distribution, and ecology is limited. Neither species had been recorded for the last 13 and 62 years, respectively, since their most recent collections. Questions: How do the new records of Bletia concolor and B. similis contribute to the knowledge of their distribution and to the assessment of their conservation status? Studied species: Bletia concolor and B. similis.
publisher: Sociedad Botánica de México, A. C.

title: Updated checklist of non-psoroptidid Astigmata in China (Acariformes)
abstract: This paper presents a revised checklist cataloging 160 species across 61 genera in 17 families of non-psoroptidid Astigmata known to occur in China. Among these, eight species have been newly documented since the 2010 review, and a further nineteen previously overlooked species have now been incorporated. Furthermore, one erroneous record, Sancassania karnatakaensis (Krishna Rao & Ranganath), has been corrected by its removal. The updated binomial name, Chinese name, and detailed information regarding hosts, distribution, and other relevant data are provided for each species.

title: Colonial memories in landscapes and waterways: the vital materialism of troubling childhood histories
abstract: This article shares a postqualitative, new materialist approach to memory work and storytelling, foregrounding the entangled colonial histories embedded in water and landscape. With its life-giving properties, water is a vital matter through which we can rethink histories to connect with the more-than-human and decolonise ourselves. Using new materialism, we create a watery assemblage (images and text) to challenge our thinking around the colonial histories embedded in the waterscapes. We consider situated epistemologies that emerge through thinking with water, waterways, landscapes, humans, a

title: Distributed Agent-Based Scheduling of Smart Port Operations under Cost and Emissions Constraints
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a distributed, emission-aware scheduling framework for smart port energy management, designed to coordinate heterogeneous flexible electric loads under operational, economic, and environmental constraints. The proposed approach addresses the coordinated scheduling of refrigerated containers (reefers), plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), and shore-to-ship power supply systems, with the objective of reducing total operational cost while satisfying asset-level constraints and ship-level and port-level emission limits. A key feature of the framework is the modeling of be
institutions: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

title: From forbidden site to global attraction: Alula's narrative re-engineering
abstract: This paper examines the socio-political and religious transformations in Saudi Arabia's AlUla region, with a focus on Hegra. Once avoided for religious reasons, the site has been repurposed within Vision 2030. This study offers a systematic textual account of this narrative shift using Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) on three corpora: state documents (including the tourism website), media, and religious texts. title: Techno-Economic Assessment of LOHC-Based Hydrogen Export from Australia to Japan
abstract: Abstract This study develops a corridor-specific techno-economic framework for LOHC-based hydrogen export from Australia to Japan and applies it to four representative carrier systems: toluene/methylcyclohexane (TOL/MCH), dibenzyltoluene/perhydrodibenzyltoluene (H0-DBT/H18-DBT), N-ethylcarbazole/perhydro-N-ethylcarbazole (H0-NEC/H12-NEC), and benzene/cyclohexane (BZ/CH). title: From Nahda to Naksa: Some Marxist Perspectives on the Arab National Question
abstract: This article examines the trajectory of Arab nationalism through a Marxist lens, analyzing its historical emergence, political ascendancy, and eventual decline. It posits the Palestinian question as central to the development of Arab nationalist consciousness and anti-imperialist struggle, arguing that the fragmentation of a unified Arab stance reflects broader geopolitical defeats and the consolidation of dependent capitalist relations. abstract: Among the key media used to form collective memory or to convey historical concepts and the narrative point of view adopted in such dramas it has a direct bearing upon the audience ' s ideas of, and attitude toward, history. title: Two new threatened Inversodicraea (Podostemaceae) species from waterfalls in Sierra Leone: I. joulei and I. lebbiei
abstract: Summary Two threatened new species of Podostemaceae belonging to the genus Inversodicraea , I. joulei and I. lebbiei , both from the Republic of Sierra Leone, are described and illustrated. A first record in Sierra Leone of the genus Lestestuella is also reported. Inversodicraea is the most species-rich genus of Podostemaceae in Africa and now comprises 38 species. title: A Perspective on the Historical Role and Future of Bactris Gasipaes as a Food Crop
abstract: Peach palm (Bactris gasipaes) is a domesticated perennial of the tropical Americas historically cultivated within Indigenous agroforestry systems. Interdisciplinary evidence indicates that it functioned as a staple in pre-Columbian Amazonia, embedded in diversified, human-managed forests. Despite its nutritional and agronomic potential, modern development efforts have not integrated it into contemporary food economies, largely due to a mismatch with prevailing models based on annual monocultures. title: Analysis of the current state and medium-term forecast of transport system development parameters up to 2028
abstract: The article presents an analysis of the dynamics of key indicators of the development of the Russian transportation industry in 2023–2025. It provides forecast values for the period up to 2028, taking into account current trends and exogenous macroeconomic parameters defined in the latest Forecast of the Social and Economic Development of the Russian Federation for 2026 and for the Planning Period of 2027 and 2028, as well as in other strategic documents.

title: Portable Web Applications: Feasibility, Limitations, and Applications of Flash Drive Deployment
abstract: Traditional enterprise web applications rely on centralized, cloud-hosted client-server architectures that assume continuous broadband connectivity, DNS resolution, and administrative access on the local host for runtime execution. In infrastructural edge-deployment zones, post-disaster humanitarian settings, high-security isolated networks, and digital-divide educational institutions, this centralized paradigm runs into severe operational barriers. title: Engaging the public to unveil urban biodiversity: a decade of ant monitoring in Italy
abstract: Abstract Citizen science (CS) has become an increasingly effective approach in biodiversity research, helping to overcome data gaps that are difficult to address through conventional methods. In entomology, CS initiatives have grown significantly, yet ants (Hymenoptera: Formicidae) remain underrepresented, partly due to challenges in species identification. The Italian “School of Ants” (SoA) project aimed to fill this gap by engaging over 6,000 participants from diverse backgrounds between 2012 and 2023 to monitor urban ant diversity across the country. title: The limits of models in the debate on Great Moravian centres
abstract: The paper examines the limits of existing models used to interpret the functioning of Great Moravian centres through the case study of Bojná-Valy in Western Slovakia. While recent debate has been structured around Jiří Macháček’s triad of models (agrarian hinterland, autarky, and local market) critically revised by Michal Hlavica, this study argues that such frameworks are insufficient when applied to non-standard sites. title: Mongolian Loanwords in Kazakh: A Semantic and Cultural Analysis
abstract: This study provides a detailed analysis of Mongolic loanwords in Kazakh in terms of their historical origins, phonological and morphological adaptation, and semantic change. The main source of the research is Kazak Tiliniŋ Kirme Sözder Sözdigi (The Dictionary of Borrowed Words in the Kazakh Language), which represents a comprehensive corpus of borrowed vocabulary. Through a systematic and detailed examination of this dictionary, a large number of words of Mongolic origin have been identified and compared with their occurrences both in historical records and in modern Kazakh. title: “ … based on the skewed theory building of the postcolonial movement”: Media conflicts surrounding postcolonial studies and antisemitism in Germany
abstract: The increasing recognition of postcolonial studies gave rise to a revisionist counter-movement on the conservative side in Germany, which went largely unnoticed until 2019. In the course of media conflicts over antisemitism in recent years, however, a majority opinion emerged in the liberal and left-wing camps that fundamentally suspected and criticized postcolonial studies as antisemitic. title: Representations of air tragedy in Chinese press: a corpus-driven critical discourse study
abstract: This article examines discourses surrounding air tragedies, aiming to investigate differences in ideological stances adopted by Chinese journalists toward three social actor groups associated with the crashed China Eastern Boeing 737. By integrating theories and methodologies from corpus linguistics and critical discourse studies, and employing corpus linguistics software, the study reveals that Chinese media constructs a positive representation of the “Our” group (the Chinese government and China Eastern Airlines) while framing the “Others” group (Boeing) negatively. title: Teaching Thoughtful Statistical Inference: Stories for the World Beyond p < 0.05
abstract: ABSTRACT Statistical hypothesis tests and p values are poorly understood by many students of statistics. Poor application and misinterpretation of statistical inference procedures are common in published research. Over‐reliance on the “ p < 0.05” threshold to claim “statistical significance” often masks weaknesses in the evaluation of statistical evidence. This state of affairs presents a challenge for statistics education. This article proposes to teach statistical inference in the context of teaching statistical thinking. title: Opioid use following spinal cord injury: a qualitative study of the perspectives of healthcare providers and people with lived experience
abstract: Purpose This qualitative study sought to understand opioid use following spinal cord injury (SCI) and identify capacity for improving patient safety from the perspective of people with lived experience and healthcare providers (HCPs).Materials and methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 participants (14 HCPs; 9 people with SCI) from January to September 2025, using interpretive description. title: ‘The worst of all Turkish peoples’: Ibn Faḍlān’s travel account as British naval intelligence
abstract: Abstract The tenth-century CE Arabic travel account of Aḥmad Ibn Faḍlān has seen many reactions, receptions, and afterlives in Islamicate languages and in European settings. These relate both to the identity and presumed authority of Ibn Faḍlān as an eyewitness observer and presumed diplomat, and to the contents of his account. Considering different presentations of Ibn Faḍlān’s role and identity, this article approaches reactions to and uses of Ibn Faḍlān’s descriptions of the Bāshghird, particularly within a 1918 British military intelligence document, in order to consider Ibn Faḍlān’s poten

title: GREEK ATHEISM: A REALITY
abstract: This article is a response to Thomas Harrison’s lively thesis that atheism in ancient Greece is not a historical reality but ‘fundamentally, a scholarly mirage’. Repurposing and updating the arguments from the influential work of Lucien Febvre, The Problem of Unbelief in the Sixteenth Century , Harrison reasons that atheism could not have emerged in the age of Socrates and Plato: all we have from this period are empty accusations of atheism, a religious mentality which was incompatible with total unbelief, and a society in which religion dominated every sphere of personal and public life. title: Does capitalist risk-taking justify profits?
abstract: Abstract The profits collected by owners of companies are commonly taken to be a just and rightful compensation for the economic risks that they take. However, in the last two-and-a-half centuries, the risk-taking that follows with ownership has been drastically reduced as a consequence of legal and organizational changes, including incorporation, limited liability, and diversified investment. abstract: En la presente publicación se realiza una propuesta funcional y simbólica para el conjunto áureo procedente del santuario tartésico de El Carambolo (Camas, Sevilla). Para ello se han tomado como principales referentes las joyas y representaciones iconográficas chipriotas, sirias y asirias de los siglos X-VI a. title: Ferry Retrouvé : Leaving the History of Empire Out of the “Liberal Moment” in France
abstract: This article examines how and why empire went missing from the liberal revival that began in 1970s France by examining a nineteenth-century political figure “rediscovered” during it: Jules Ferry, who as premier between 1880 and 1885 oversaw not only the creation of a secular school system in France, but also a huge burst of overseas expansion. In their portraits of him starting in the 1980s, historians such as François Furet and Mona Ozouf emphasized the former, while minimizing or excusing the latter. title: Feeding power
abstract: Even after 150 years of archaeological research on fortified centres, to which key central functions in early medieval Central Europe are generally attributed, we still do not have a clearer idea of how their populations were supplied with basic goods in practice. This text follows on the discussion opened by Jiří Macháček (2026) for Great Moravian agglomerations. It presents a systematic analysis of possible subsistence strategies, consistently linking them to the social profile of the inhabitants of the centres and to the property regimes that determined the forms of exchange. title: The materiality of postapartheid: post-racial signifiers in Gray Hofmeyr’s Yankee Zulu (1993) and Mad Buddies (2012)
abstract: In 1994, South Africa transitioned from apartheid rule to a post-apartheid democracy, with a constitution in place. Significant scholarship has since covered the many constitutionalised aspects of the period after the end of apartheid: governance, political, social, cultural, and economic, among others. abstract: This article is the outcome of the exploratory phase of a research project on collective filmmaking in South Africa that focuses on the lived experience of workers in the audiovisual industry. The first part offers a brief overview of South African colonial history and multilingual culture, of early film exhibition and production in South Africa, of the development of the Afrikaans film industry under apartheid and of its institutional transformation in the post-apartheid period, highlighting how social and political factors shape the industry's evolution. title: Bajo asedio: la defensa de Filipinas de las incursiones neerlandesas (1600-1648)
abstract: La Compañía de las Indias Orientales neerlandesa (VOC), a lo largo de su enfrentamiento con la Monarquía Hispánica, realizó durante casi medio siglo más de una veintena de ataques de diferente índole sobre las Filipinas. El archipiélago se convirtió en un frente estratégico y activo de la guerra entre la Monarquía Hispánica y la República Neerlandesa durante la primera mitad del siglo XVII. title: Prácticas trans-archivísticas y archivo fotográfico en Argentina. Memoria travesti, comunidad y acceso en el Archivo de la Memoria Trans y la Biblioteca Claudia Pía Baudracco
abstract: This article examines Archivo de la Memoria Trans and Biblioteca Claudia Pía Baudracco as community-based archival experiences that reshape the way photographic archives are understood in Argentina. Drawing on a qualitative and situated approach, it analyzes the transition from intimate and dispersed memories to a public infrastructure of preservation, description, access, cultural circulation and historical repair. title: Characterizing Wildlife Response to Biomimetic and Conventional Underwater Vehicles
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are a promising alternative to divers for scalable collection of natural ocean ecology data. However, these robots may disturb local fauna and cause drastic behavioral differences compared to other monitoring techniques, decreasing their value as scientific tools. A promising prospect is to make AUVs that are more biomimetic, with the hope that taking on the form and behavior of a non-predatory animal may reduce adverse responses. abstract: We present Underwater C$^{3}$-JEPA (cross-view, control-conditioned, context-extended), an object-centric multi-view predictive world model for near-field heavy-load underwater ROV salvage. Without contact sensors, it predicts in latent space how the task-object state evolves through contact interaction and under the hydrodynamic lag of the vehicle, from synchronized multi-view RGB observations and vehicle control signals. abstract: Localizing an autonomous underwater vehicle without pre-deployed seabed transponders, or direct access to onboard vehicle sensors remains a core challenge. We present a receiver-passive 3-D localization and spatial mapping system utilizing a single floating surface buoy equipped with a hydrophone array and an inertial measurement unit (IMU). abstract: In this work, we propose a communication-free framework for vision-based formation control of fully actuated underwater robots subject to sensing constraints, collision-avoidance requirements, and input saturations. Recentered barrier Lyapunov functions encode sensing and collision-avoidance constraints, while command-filtered backstepping extends the design to the second-order vehicle dynamics. abstract: Many spatial (3D) vehicles, including AUVs and fixed-wing aircraft, are effectively nonholonomic and subject to limited actuation, such that continuous time-invariant stabilization is fundamentally obstructed by Brockett's necessary condition. To overcome this obstruction, we exploit the geometric singularity of spherical coordinates to design a backstepping continuous, time-invariant feedback law that exponentially stabilizes a 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated solely by forward surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate. title: Partial-Scan-and-Move Source Seeking for Mobile Robots
abstract: This paper presents a partial-scan-and-move strategy for source seeking with a mobile robot equipped with an offset scalar sensor. At each robot position, the sensor collects source field measurements while the robot rotates. Instead of requiring a complete circular scan before every move, we ask when the measurements collected over only part of the circle are already sufficient to determine the next action. abstract: Abstract The effects of anthropogenic underwater noise, such as operational noise from offshore wind farms (OWFs), on plankton are poorly understood. A significant challenge in assessing the impact of noise on natural communities is the lack of holistic and ecologically relevant experimental setups mimicking soundscapes and communities under close-to-natural conditions. abstract: Abstract This article describes an ocean-bottom seismic data set collected offshore New Zealand’s North Island as part of a multinational amphibious experiment investigating the Auckland volcanic field. From August 2023 to September 2024, 20 broadband ocean-bottom seismographs were deployed at water depths of 1200–2700 m, yielding approximately one year of continuous recordings from 15 successfully recovered instruments. abstract: During the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM), atmospheric p CO 2 was approximately 90 ppm lower than in the pre-industrial era. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain this difference, including changes in nutrient supply, increased iron input to the ocean, reduced air-sea gas exchange due to changes in sea-ice coverage, and variations in overturning circulation strength driven by differences in wind stress and atmospheric moisture diffusivity. title: Changing coastal distribution and life-history patterns of Inconnu in northwest Alaska
abstract: Climate change is driving shifts in fish distributions across Arctic ecosystems. Inconnu (Stenodus leucichthys) are an important subsistence and recreational fishing species and depend upon a mosaic of aquatic habitats that are rapidly changing. The freshwater migratory patterns of these fish are well-documented, but information on their coastal movement patterns and life histories are largely unknown. abstract: The marine dinoflagellate genera Pyrocystis and Dissodinium are core components of coastal phytoplankton and bioindicators for eutrophication monitoring, yet long-standing taxonomic confusion, misapplied Latin epithets, and inconsistent morphological records widely exist in domestic marine surveys across China’s seas. abstract: Early marine diagenetic dolomites in peritidal settings are geologically abundant and regarded as promising seawater archives, yet their application is hindered by the still-enigmatic processes governing their formation. We investigate subrecent (<7 ka) dolomites extracted from classical evaporative peritidal carbonates near Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, one of the few settings documenting (sub)recent dolomite formation. abstract: Fluvial sediment transport plays a key role in geomorphological and hydrological processes, influencing river morphology, watershed and coastal sediment balances, and the environmental response to climatic and anthropogenic changes. In Italy, the availability of homogeneous and long-term data is strongly limited due to the discontinuity of monitoring activities and the fragmentation of existing sources. abstract: This study examines the adaptability of civil engineering materials in marine environments, investigating deterioration laws of five material types under multi - environmental coupling effects. abstract: Anthropogenic sound has become an increasingly important environmental stressor in marine, estuarine, and freshwater ecosystems. Fishes rely on acoustic information for communication, orientation, habitat selection, predator and prey detection, social interactions, and reproduction. abstract: This study presents the first Mediterranean-wide assessment based on the complete original MYTILOS database, generated through coordinated mussel transplantation campaigns conducted under a common harmonized monitoring protocol. Although subsets of this dataset have previously supported scientific publications, the complete database has never been analyzed as a single basin-scale synthesis. abstract: In the Eastern Tropical Pacific (ETP), colonies of the genus Pocillopora dominate reef frameworks and are widely used in restoration initiatives. abstract: The genus Dendronephthya , a soft coral lacking zooxanthellae, is taxonomically complex and poorly documented in the Arabian Sea region. In this study, we collected and identified a colony fragment of Dendronephthya cf. sinaiensis from the Lakshadweep Archipelago in the Arabian Sea. abstract: The aim of this article: to investigate the infl uence of climatic factors on the dynamics of the main commercial fish species of the Baltic Sea based on current data (through 2025/early 2026), to identify key climatic parameters that determine changes in the structure, abundance and biomass of marine fish populations. abstract: James Hutton recognised that some components of sedimentary rocks have a biological and marine origin as they contain ‘ solid parts ’ (mainly calcite) of past sea life, and so might offer an archive of Earth's history. abstract: Coral reefs are marine ecosystems composed primarily of calcium carbonate and characterized by diverse growth forms that reflect environmental conditions. Physicochemical factors, including water temperature, depth, and salinity, may influence coral growth and community distribution. This study aimed to analyze the distribution and diversity of coral growth forms and the physicochemical characteristics of the waters surrounding Badi Island, Pangkajene and Islands Regency, South Sulawesi, as baseline information for the inventory and assessment of coral reef ecosystem conditions. abstract: Impact statement Marine ammonia‐oxidizing archaea (AOA) have evolved into diverse lineages and ecological niches. abstract: Plastic additives are increasingly recognized as emerging chemical contaminants in marine ecosystems, yet their effects under ocean warming remain poorly investigated. abstract: EMODnet is a European infrastructure dedicated to collecting, harmonizing, and disseminating marine data while promoting FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and Open Science. Through a network of more than 160 data centers, EMODnet supports scientific institutions, public authorities, and private organizations in sharing datasets on bathymetry, geology, biodiversity, physics, chemistry, and human activities. title: Marine restoration and willingness to pay: are preferences ecosystem specific?
abstract: Marine ecosystem restoration is expensive, and clear quantification of benefits will likely be required to support funding allocation. Much of the value associated with marine restoration is non-use, non-market benefit values, which require the use of stated preference surveys to uncover. This quantification in itself is costly, and value transfer studies rather than primary stated preference surveys are likely to be preferred. title: The value of multi-year sampling for detecting fine-scale population genetic structure in marine fishes: A case study of juvenile southern flounder
abstract: Understanding population structure is critical for effective fisheries management in species with complex life histories and variable recruitment. Southern flounder (Paralichthys lethostigma) is a valuable flatfish species with declining populations in the Southeast United States. Improved management may depend on a better understanding of fine-scale and temporal population genetic structure in this region; however, such structure remains poorly characterized. title: The Green Upgrading of Digital Infrastructure: The Impact of Green Data Centers on Air Pollution
abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy coincides with escalating environmental challenges, making Green Data Centers (GDC) an important form of digital infrastructure with potential implications for environmental governance. However, existing studies mainly evaluate data centers from the perspectives of energy efficiency, electricity consumption, and carbon emissions, while city-level evidence regarding their effects on ambient air pollution remains limited. title: Growth rates of Korean strains of 10 marine diatom species under different temperature and light conditions
abstract: Diatoms are major contributors to marine primary production and frequently dominate phytoplankton blooms. However, growth rate data remain limited for many diatom species, and strain-level variability remains insufficiently documented. We investigated the growth rates of ten marine diatom species isolated from Korean coastal waters under independently manipulated temperature (20 and 25°C) and light (50 and 100 μmol photons m-2 s-1) conditions, representative of conditions under which temperate marine diatoms actively grow. title: Engineering Assessment of Long-Term Coastal Siltation in the Northern Sector of Taichung Port, Taiwan, Using Tide-Normalized SAR Time Series
abstract: Persistent coastal siltation at port entrances increases dredging demand and threatens navigation safety, while bathymetric surveys remain costly for decadal assessment. This study presents a tide-aware Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) framework for quantifying siltation evolution in the northern sector of Taichung Port, Taiwan, using 276 Sentinel-1 ascending-track VV images acquired from 2015 to 2024. title: PALEOENVIRONMENTAL RECONSTRUCTION OF THE OLIGOCENE TRANSGRESSION IN THE CENTRAL-EASTERN TERTIARY PIEDMONT BASIN (NW ITALY): INSIGHTS FROM STRATIGRAPHY, PALEONTOLOGY AND GAMMA-RAY EMISSIONS
abstract: This study presents the first integrated lithostratigraphical, paleontological and spectral gamma-ray (SGR) dataset from the central-eastern sector of the Tertiary Piedmont Basin (TPB). The TPB is a late- to post-orogenic sedimentary basin system deposited during a widespread marine transgression. The Molare Formation of the TPB records the evolution of shallow-marine depositional systems developed within a tectonically active basin during the Oligocene. title: Projected Habitat Expansion of the Invasive Striped Eel Catfish Plotosus lineatus in the Mediterranean Sea Under Future Climate Conditions
abstract: The striped eel catfish Plotosus lineatus is a venomous Indo-Pacific species that has rapidly expanded within the Mediterranean Sea following its Lessepsian migration through the Suez Canal. Understanding its current distribution and future invasion potential is essential for evaluating ecological risks under ongoing climate change. In this study, ensemble species distribution models were applied to predict the present and future habitat suitability of P. lineatus across the Mediterranean Sea under the CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 climate scenario. Georeferenced occurrence records were compiled from publish

title: Ecological research on hydropower impacts in lakes is falling behind that in rivers
abstract: Abstract Hydropower is expected to play an important role in future energy systems by helping balance variable wind and solar energy production. While hydropower impacts on river ecosystems have been extensively studied, far less attention has been given to lakes. It remains unclear whether the current knowledge base is sufficient to enable biodiversity conservation. We performed a bibliometric study comparing lake- and river-focused research to assess existing knowledge of the ecological effects of hydropower on lakes and the relative maturity of lake-focused research. institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

title: A near miss: invasive non-indigenous mussels and barnacles transported deep into Antarctic waters
abstract: Abstract The Southern Ocean around Antarctica remains the only large area on the planet populated by almost entirely native and mainly endemic species. Despite being one of the most constant environments for millions of years and still the least human populated, the polar regions are now hotspots of physical climate change, and this is likely to make the shallow waters less inhospitable to invading non-indigenous species (NIS). title: Documenting the coastal erosion-driven collapse of a Cold War underground monitoring station via laser scanning
abstract: Rapid soft-cliff coastal erosion along the Holderness Coast, United Kingdom, continues to result in the loss of infrastructure, including buildings of local historical interest. The terrestrial laser scans presented in this data note were collected to document the post-failure condition of the Tunstall Royal Observer Corps monitoring post; a Cold War structure progressively exposed by ongoing soft-cliff coastal erosion. The structure was discovered to have collapsed onto the beach by local residents on the morning of 23 January 2026 and was subsequently surveyed by the authors on the same day.

title: Staking out the frontiers: The limits of the metazoan shallow marine fossil record
abstract: The fossil record is inherently incomplete, yet its physical limits remain largely uncharted. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal coverage of the global shallow-marine metazoan fossil record across the Phanerozoic, using a large dataset of georeferenced collections intersected with global geological data. Modeling historical sampling trajectories, we show that for most time intervals, future data accumulation is expected to be negligible, and geographic coverage is approaching saturation. title: Sonic selves, ancestral archives: Identity, language and cultural memory in amaXhosa sacred practice
abstract: Among the amaXhosa of South Africa’s Eastern Cape, knowledge lives less in texts than in bodies, voices and sacred landscapes. In Hamburg, at the mouth of the Keiskamma River, knowledge of the ocean, river, forest and healing plants is transmitted in isiXhosa through song, carried by elders whose authority rests on accountability to the ancestors rather than institutional credentials. This article examines how amaXhosa sacred spaces function as living archives where language, music and cosmology converge to form identity, sustain memory and enact healing. title: Underwater virtual reality for neurodivergent participation in scuba diving: an integrative review and sensory-adapted framework
abstract: Purpose Despite growing interest in virtual reality (VR) as a tool to support neurodivergent individuals, limited attention has been given to how immersive and underwater virtual reality (UVR) can be designed and implemented as enabling technologies within leisure and therapeutic contexts. This study aims to develop a sensory-adapted framework to guide the design and implementation of UVR systems that support neurodivergent participation, well-being and accessibility. title: Reflections on Creative Responses to Archival Collections in PARADISEC
abstract: The Pacific and Regional Archive for Digital Sources in Endangered Cultures (PARADISEC) is a digital archive of some of the many small cultures and languages of the world, particularly from the Pacific region. The article reflects on a collaborative outreach project involving the creative response of a group of Papua New Guinean people to archival collections held in PARADISEC. The project demonstrates how reciprocity, long-term relationships and the valuing of Indigenous knowledge holders can invigorate cultural practices, adding value and meaning to the archive. title: Non-destructive approach using micro-CT for understanding the strategy of mesoparasitism of the genus Cardiodectes (Copepoda: Siphonostomatoida: Pennellidae) on marine fishes, with a new species description from coastal waters of the Ryukyu Islands, the western North Pacific
abstract: Abstract A new species of pennellid copepod (Siphonostomatoida), Cardiodectes laybackinabaueroides sp. nov., is described based on postmetamorphic adult females collected from the coastal waters of the Ryukyu Islands, western North Pacific, Japan. The new species differs from other congeners by having the following unique characters: the cephalothorax bearing three pairs of lateral lobes, the first to third pedigerous somites formed a swollen bulge, the elongate trunk constricted at posterior four-fifth length. title: Morphological and Genetic Characteristics of Bleekeria mitsukurii Jordan and Evermann, 1902 (Labriformes; Uranoscopiformes; Ammodytidae), Collected in Sagami Bay, Japan: Presence of a Swim Bladder
abstract: Sandlances of the family Ammodytidae are small marine teleosts comprising 35 valid nominal species in seven genera, found from the Arctic to tropical seas. The family is known for its unique morphological specializations: degeneration of the pelvic fins and air bladder, coupled with a remarkably high number of abdominal vertebrae among teleosts. However, in the present study, the presence of a swim bladder was documented for the first time in Ammodytidae, specifically in specimens of Mitsukuri's sandlance Bleekeria mitsukurii Jordan and Evermann, 1902, collected in Sagami Bay, Japan (35°15′N,

title: Rare Earth Elements in Chile: A Critical Review of Primary, Secondary and Marine Resources, Metallurgical Recoverability and Future Supply Chain Opportunities
abstract: The economic value of rare earth elements (REE) is concentrated in Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb. The supply chain for these elements is dominated by a single country, China, which accounts for about 60% of mined production, over 90% of refinement, and nearly 95% of permanent magnet manufacturing. This shifts the critical question from geological availability to the capacity to convert resources into products. title: Does light and short-term high food availability enhance larval success in the coral eating crown-of-thorns seastar (Acanthaster cf. solaris)?
abstract: Abstract Understanding the environmental drivers of Crown-of-thorns seastar outbreaks is important for predicting and managing coral reef decline. Larval survival and development are strongly influenced by phytoplankton food availability, which is highly variable in space and time and often occurs as short-lived nutrient-driven pulses. Light may also indirectly support larval nutrition via phototrophic bacteria. title: Mid-Miocene palaeohydrology archived in palaeosols of La Tatacoa, Colombia
abstract: Abstract Mid-Miocene palaeosols of the Baraya Member (Villavieja Formation, La Tatacoa, Colombia) record contrasting pedogenic pathways developed within fine-grained floodbasin environments under subhumid tropical conditions. The Ferruginous Red Bed (FRB) and La Venta Red Bed (LVRB) form thick, cumulatively accreted palaeosol successions produced under low sedimentation rates, where pedogenesis proceeded contemporaneously with slow overbank deposition. title: Spatiotemporal variability of sea level fluctuations according to IMMOAD SSHA data after additional correction of the tidal component
abstract: Seasonal and interannual variability of sea level fluctuations in the northwestern Pacific Ocean and the Far Eastern seas was analyzed using the empirical orthogonal function decomposition of the original data series. The study is based on a data set of altimetric observations from the IMMOAD SSHA for the period 1993–2021, which included additional tidal correction and monthly averaging of data at each point along the satellite tracks. title: Mycobiota of the Bottom Sediments of the White Sea: Metabarcoding and Cultural Method
abstract: Abstract Knowledge of the composition of fungi in sediments is necessary to understand many biological processes, the decomposition of organic substances in aquatic ecosystems in particular. However, the diversity of fungi in the Arctic seas remains poorly studied, and single studies have been performed, using metabarcoding of DNA from sediments. Such studies for the White Sea are absent, and the composition and structure of fungal communities in its bottom sediments are known only on the basis of inoculation on nutrient media. title: The climate-conflict nexus and environmental governance in southern Thailand
abstract: The connection between climate change and peacebuilding is increasingly recognised globally, yet little is known about how these dynamics unfold within contexts of ongoing violent secessionist conflict. This study explores the conflict-peace-climate nexus in the protracted ethno-nationalist conflict in Thailand’s southernmost provinces, drawing on analyses and recommendations from local civil society organisations. title: Strategic Management of Household Economic Resilience among Coastal Communities under Relocation Pressure
abstract: The relocation of coastal communities, in the context of industrial area development, has not only changed residential locations but also livelihood structures, resource access, and household economic management. This study aims to analyze household strategic management in maintaining economic resilience under relocation pressure. The study employs a qualitative case study using semi-structured interviews and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), as well as thematic analysis to identify patterns of strategies and supporting factors of economic resilience. abstract: Abstract While climate change scenarios consistently project future changes in ocean circulation, an inter-basin assessment of the extent, intensity and underlying mechanisms driving these changes is still needed. Therefore, this study quantifies alterations in ocean currents’ volume transport (VT) and assess their relationship with subtropical gyre branch displacements and wind forcing changes based on projections from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6. title: Temporal variability of emerging contaminants and estrogenic activity in sediments of a tropical coastal lagoon
abstract: Abstract The increasing occurrence of emerging contaminants in aquatic environments has raised concerns about their persistence and ecological impacts, particularly in coastal lagoons subjected to anthropogenic pressure. Here, we investigated the occurrence of pharmaceuticals, alkylphenols, bisphenol A (BPA), and steroid estrogens, together with their estrogenic activity, in surface sediments from Maricá Lagoon (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil), testing the hypothesis that contaminant occurrence and biological responses vary between sampling years despite persistent anthropogenic inputs. title: Valuation of Flood Risk in Coastal Housing Markets: Evidence from Tampa Bay
abstract: Florida exhibits growing tension between urban population growth and increasing exposure to coastal flooding risk. More than half of the state’s municipalities are threatened by chronic flooding, and in recent years the insurance market has been characterized by rising premiums and insurer withdrawals. Despite these signs, the Tampa Bay region remains one of the fastest-growing metropolitan areas in the United States. title: Determinants of CSA Adoption in Coastal Bangladesh: An Application of Structural Path Analysis
abstract: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted to reconcile productivity, resilience, and emissions goals among smallholder farmers, yet adoption of capital-intensive CSA technologies remains low and uneven in climate-vulnerable coastal agriculture. This study examines socio-demographic, institutional, and behavioral determinants of CSA adoption among farming households in selected coastal districts of Bangladesh. title: The first GBIF dataset on the distribution of fish assemblage in inland and transitional waters of Sicily (Central Mediterranean Basin)
abstract: Mediterranean inland and transitional waters are fragile ecosystems currently facing rapid biodiversity loss due to anthropogenic pressures and climate change. In Sicily, the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, knowledge of ichthyofaunal assemblages of these ecosystems has remained fragmented, sporadic, and largely confined to "grey" literature for long. The present paper presents a dataset built with the aim to fill this gap. The dataset aggregates 808 occurrence records from 108 water bodies and localities, spanning a 50-year period (1976–2025). title: Analysis of environmental conditions of offshore raft-culture areas in Dongshan Island
abstract: Dongshan Island is one of the important mariculture bases in Zhangzhou City, Fujian Province. Relying on its long coastline, it has developed three different aquaculture models: floating raft hanging culture, offshore fish cage net culture, and onshore high-position pond culture, nurturing distinctive aquaculture species such as oysters, Decapterus maruadsi, green abalone, and asparagus seaweed. Fisheries serve as the primary source of livelihood income for local coastal residents. title: Pathologic and immunohistochemical findings in sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) naturally infected with Aeromonas veronii biovar veronii
abstract: Tissue samples from European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) naturally infected with Aeromonas veronii biovar veronii were subjected to bacteriological, molecular, pathological, and immunohistochemical analyses. The fish were sourced from aquaculture farms in the Aegean region of Turkiye. Clinical and postmortem examinations revealed granuloma formation as the most prominent lesion, primarily affecting the skin, spleen, kidneys, and liver. title: Soil redox potential and plant species identity likely affect root-associated fungi in salt marshes
abstract: Abstract Root-associated fungi (RAF) are important for plant performance because they form beneficial, neutral, or pathogenic relationships with their hosts, thus regulating nutrient uptake, stress tolerance, and overall plant fitness. At the transition from marine to terrestrial ecosystems, salt marshes are shaped by strong environmental gradients and provide vital ecosystem services such as climate regulation and coastal protection, yet RAF remain poorly understood in these systems. title: Thrombolite Genesis Under Dynamic Hydrocarbon Fluid Flux: Microbial Records From New Zealand Paleo-Seeps
abstract: Distinctive associations of microcrystalline thrombolites and fibrous aragonite cements in deep-marine Miocene New Zealand hydrocarbon seep carbonates capture snapshots of microbial resilience and adaptation to changing seepage intensity driven by hydrocarbon-rich fluid fluxes. These successions record repeated fracturing, sealing, and seepage recurrences, with thrombolites occurring within fractures and vugs and as coatings on worm tubes, intergrown with multiple generations of fibrous aragonite cements. title: Tracing microplastic footprints in beach sediments along the Qatar coast: A risk-based approach to pollution assessment
abstract: Surface and subsurface sediments from twenty representative beaches along the Qatar coast were analyzed following standardized NOAA protocols, including sieving, density separation, microscopic observation, and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, to investigate the horizontal and vertical distribution, physical characteristics, polymer composition, and environmental risks of microplastics (MPs). MPs were detected at concentrations ranging from 0 to 855 MPs kg −1 dry sediment. abstract: 计算鬼成像是一种利用已知照明图案与单像素桶探测信号之间的关联恢复目标图像的成像技术。水下脉冲计算鬼成像中，水体吸收和散射会造成目标回波能量衰减；散射光子传播路径差异还会引发回波时间展宽，影响桶探测信号中的目标有效信息。针对上述问题，本文提出一种基于独立元分析的时间分辨桶信号提取方法。该方法将每次测量获得的脉冲回波划分为多个时间窗，经互补差分构造多时间窗桶测量矩阵，采用快速独立元分析得到统计相对独立的候选桶序列，用相关重构算法进行图像重构。实验表明，随着水体衰减系数增大，直接积分和固定时间门控结果逐渐出现弥散亮斑和目标结构弱化，所提方法则能改善目标结构可辨识性。在衰减系数c=3.25 m−1条件下，直接积分的感兴趣区域相关系数和带符号对比噪声比分别为−0.347和−0.954，独立元分析方法分别达到0.386和0.443。结果表明，利用多时间窗观测的统计差异提取桶序列，可提高浑浊条件下重构图像与目标物的相关性和对目标物的区分能力。

title: THE LEBANESE JEWISH COMMUNITY (1856-1943): A DEMOGRAPHIC AND SOCIO-POLITICAL EXAMINATION
abstract: The Jewish community in Lebanon is among the least-studied religious groups in the region's history. This study examines the community's demographic, social, and political dimensions from 1856 to 1943, aiming to fill this gap. Most accounts of Lebanese Jews are rooted in religious and cultural factors, and their presence rarely extended beyond a few families. The community grew significantly in the late 19th century. abstract: ABSTRACT Pedicellariae are small appendages on the surface of the echinoid test, involved in defence, cleaning, and locomotion. Pedicellariae in three species of camarodont sea urchins common in UK waters ( Paracentrotus lividus [Lamarck, 1816], Psammechinus miliaris [P.L.S Müller, 1771] and Echinus esculentus [Linnaeus, 1758]) are the focus of this study, with new characterisation and comparisons by light and scanning electron microscopy. title: Ngarrawa (mound spring) sediments as archives of Holocene environmental change in arid central Australia: Insights from Itrax XRF scanning
abstract: ABSTRACT Central Australia's ngarrawa, or ‘mound springs’, are unique hydrological systems that serve as some of the only near‐permanent sources of water and continuous sediment deposition in Australia's arid interior. As such, they hold significant potential as palaeo‐climate and ‐environmental archives in a region where many aspects of past climate remain uncertain. title: Laying the Groundwork for Moveable Heritage Disaster Risk Management: A Database-Driven Evacuation Tool at the Musée d’Archéologie Nationale
abstract: This paper presents a case study conducted at the Musée d’Archéologie Nationale (National Archaeology Museum) in France, to develop a dedicated database application to safeguard its moveable heritage from risks, as a foundational component of the museum’s wider Disaster Risk Management (DRM) strategy. abstract: Slow spreading ridges typically show deep axial valleys due to low magma supply from depth. title: Resilience of blue carbon microbiomes in response to ecological and anthropogenic filtering
abstract: Global change is threatening the microbial consortia that sustain the services and functions of blue carbon ecosystems (BCEs), but little is known about how the composition and functioning of these consortia will respond to ecological and anthropogenic stressors. abstract: euphausiid krill to forage fish, mesopelagic fishes, cephalopods, crustaceans, carrion and, in some generalist species, terrestrial or anthropogenic food. abstract: Two hundred and ninety-seven lots of acanthocephalan material, registered in the Australian Helminth Collection of the South Australian Museum since 2015, were examined. abstract: Introduction: Fish freshness is a determining factor for quality and consumer acceptability during ice storage, particularly in locally consumed species for which information on postmortem changes is limited. abstract: Ecological phase shifts from coral to macroalgae dominated benthic communities on Caribbean coral reefs have, in part, been attributed to an abrupt and significant reduction in grazing pressure caused by mass die-offs of the keystone herbivore, Diadema antillarum , in both 1983-84 and in 2022. title: Identifying Tourism Hotspots in Caraga Region through Spatial Clustering Techniques: Basis for Data-Driven Development Insight
abstract: The Caraga Region, contributing only 2.3% of total domestic tourist arrivals, requires data-driven spatial planning. This study applied the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm to 8,081 tourism-related Points of Interest (POIs) from the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap (HOTOSM) Philippines repository to identify and map tourism hotspots across Caraga's five provinces. title: Futures Right in Front of You: Participatory Futuring on Sea-Level Rise and Climate Adaptation at Dutch Water Heritage Sites
abstract: In the Dutch delta, climate adaptation is inevitable. Water heritage sites can help Dutch citizens to imagine and discuss the uncertain futures related to that fact. This article proposes public engagement programs in which heritage organizations and water management institutions use historical locations for participatory futuring with citizens on the impacts of sea-level rise. During physical and/or digital tours along various heritage sites, participants can be invited to reflect on scenarios for the Dutch delta. The sites are not just backdrops. title: Atmospheric rivers drive compound flooding potential along the U.S. west coast
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are a major driver of hydrometeorological extremes along the U.S. West Coast, yet their role in generating events with high compound flood potential remains poorly understood and quantified. Here, we assess the contribution of ARs to compound flood potential by analyzing the joint occurrence of extreme rainfall and non-tidal total water levels (nTWL) across coastal catchments in the study region. title: The risk of thiamine deficiency in common eider ducklings increases when females consume large prey
abstract: Episodic mass mortality due to thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency is a major threat to marine top-consumers worldwide. Recent reports have shown that thiamine deficiency can lead to high mortality rates of common eider (Somateria mollissima) ducklings in the Baltic population. It is unclear whether the drastic reduction in offspring recruitment is linked to the changes in egg thiamine levels. This would have an additional negative impact on the Baltic population of the common eider, which is mainly driven by increased predation pressure. title: Students’ Online Usage Patterns of Electronic Resources at St. Augustine University of Tanzania, Mwanza Campus: Evidence to Inform University Administration
abstract: The rapid growth of information and communication technologies has transformed how universities worldwide provide access to scholarly materials. Electronic resources (e-resources)—including online databases, e-journals, e-books, and digital repositories—have become essential for teaching, learning, and research in higher education. In developing countries such as Tanzania, these resources offer particular promise by overcoming the limitations of physical library collections, enabling remote access, and supporting the expanding number of undergraduate students. title: Ostracod Biostratigraphy, Paleoecology, and Their Response to Lake-Level Changes in the Lower Nenjiang Formation (Upper Cretaceous) from Borehole J79, Songliao Basin, NE China
abstract: Cretaceous paleoenvironmental reconstructions have relied heavily on marine records, whereas lacustrine deposits, though offering valuable high-resolution archives for non-marine environmental changes, remain underexplored. The Songliao Basin, the largest Mesozoic continental basin in East Asia, preserves a continuous succession of ostracod-rich sediments in its lower Nenjiang Formation, deposited during the largest Late Cretaceous lacustrine transgression (Santonian–early Campanian), yet the ostracod fauna and their ecological responses to lake-level fluctuations are poorly constrained. title: Low prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 gene deletions in archived samples collected before and after nationwide malaria-RDT rollout in Kenya
abstract: Rapid and accurate malaria diagnosis is essential for effective treatment and malaria control. In Kenya, most malaria testing relies on P. falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (PfHRP2)-based rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). However, deletions in the pfhrp 2/ pfhrp 3 genes can lead to false-negative RDT results, which can sustain transmission and worsen clinical outcomes. title: Climatic and Tectonic Controls on Late Quaternary Fluvial Terrace Development in the Turpan Fold–Thrust Belt, Eastern Tianshan
abstract: Fluvial terraces provide important archives for understanding the relative roles of tectonics and climate in landscape evolution. Here, we investigate late Quaternary fluvial terraces in the tectonically active Turpan fold–thrust belt (FTB) of the eastern Tianshan using geomorphic surveys, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived topography, and optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating. title: Action-conditioned dynamics learning for model predictive control of flexible fish locomotion
abstract: Closed-loop navigation of an autonomous flexible fish requires rapid prediction of the trajectory evolution induced by body-wave commands. However, evaluating candidate command sequences one by one with high-fidelity flow simulations would incur prohibitive computational cost. To address this challenge, this work proposes an action-conditioned fish–fluid dynamics learning framework for predictive planning of flexible-fish locomotion. The framework uses disagreement-driven active sampling to selectively enrich the trajectory database in regions where the latent dynamics remain highly uncertain.

title: The Evolution of Accessible and Inclusive Tourism: A Multi-Dimensional Assessment with Evidence from Portugal
abstract: Accessible and Inclusive Tourism (AIT) has gained growing prominence over recent decades, yet important questions remain regarding whether this increased visibility corresponds to substantive advances across research, education, and tourism practice. title: Unveiling the Hidden Struggles: Waste Management Practices of Pre-Service Teachers
abstract: Purpose This qualitative case study explores the lived experiences, challenges, and perceptions of pre-service teachers in Bongao, Tawi-Tawi, regarding waste management implementation and environmental education integration in their future classrooms. abstract: The aim of this paper is to report and document the models integrated into the ecosystem quality part of the first life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) version of the GLAM (Global Guidance for Life Cycle Impact Assessment Indicators and Methods) project. The focus is on endpoint models, and all included models provide characterization factors related to the loss of species richness, indicated in potentially disappeared fraction of species (PDF·yr). title: A review on thermodynamics and kinetics of quartz dissolution under supercritical geothermal conditions
abstract: Abstract The knowledge of the dissolution behavior of quartz is crucial to understanding geochemical processes in supercritical geothermal systems, as well as hot dry rock, offshore geothermal, and mid-ocean ridge systems. This review presents the experimental and model studies of quartz-water reactions under supercritical geothermal conditions. title: GRIND-ECT: geological research through integrated Neoproterozoic drilling – Ediacaran–Cambrian transition
abstract: GRIND (Geological Research through Integrated Neoproterozoic Drilling), sponsored by the International Continental Scientific Drilling Program (ICDP), aims to create a core archive of the Neoproterozoic Era via three phases: Tonian (GRIND-TON), Cryogenian (GRIND-CRY), and Ediacaran–Cambrian Transition (GRIND-ECT). The latter is the first phase undertaken and focuses on the geological and biogeochemical context of Late Ediacaran environmental perturbations and biological turnovers that culminated in the Cambrian Explosion. abstract: ABSTRACT Volcanic ash (tephra) provides an important chronostratigraphic framework for correlating Quaternary records. title: Small modular reactors in future energy systems: A study of grid support, distributed energy systems, non-electric applications, and economic drivers
abstract: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) are emerging as a potential low-carbon technology for grid decarbonization and industrial applications. This paper provides a comprehensive review and critical synthesis of SMR technology and its role in enabling operational flexibility and reliability in future energy systems. We systematically review 70 SMR designs, categorizing them by reactor type, technology readiness level, and operational characteristics.
