title: Cosserat Modeling of Trimmed Helicoid Soft Arms with a Separated-Section Constitutive Law
abstract: Cosserat rod models for soft robots usually construct sectional stiffness by summing material properties over a common cross-section. This assumption becomes inaccurate for trimmed helicoid arms, where load-bearing helix domains are separated and connected only through sparse fused crossings. abstract: We report the environmental qualification and performance of CombSat, a dual optical frequency comb payload designed for deployment on a 12U CubeSat in low Earth orbit. The payload integrates two self-referenced, 200 MHz hybrid fiber-waveguide frequency combs, a narrow-linewidth optical reference, a heterodyne beat detection unit, and FPGA-based control electronics in a total mass of 8.3 kg and volume of 5.7 L, and nominal power consumption of 21W. abstract: The vanilla scotogenic model (VSM) featuring three right-handed neutrinos and an inert scalar doublet, offers a unified explanation of neutrino masses, dark matter (DM), and the baryon asymmetry of the Universe through leptogenesis. title: Performance Analysis of Low-Order, GPU-accelerated Finite Element Kernels using Kokkos
abstract: We study performance portability for low-order, matrix-free finite element kernels, using the example of a vectorial, variable-coefficient PDE operator originating in geophysical models. Written in Kokkos, the kernel is compared on NVIDIA H100, AMD MI250X, AMD MI300A and Intel PVC Max 1550 GPUs. title: Narrowband, angle-stable, and highly efficient polariton organic light emitting diodes employing thermally activated delayed fluorescence
abstract: Narrowband emission is crucial for next generation optoelectronic devices to satisfy demands for high color brilliance. Microcavities can narrow the emission spectra of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) through the creation of resonant standing waves, independent of emitter material, enabling flexibility in molecular and device design. title: Integrated Guidance and Control of a Mother-Child UAV-UGV System for Cooperative Missions
abstract: Autonomous recovery of a small multirotor onto a hovering multirotor carrier differs from recovery onto ground or shipborne platforms because the recovery surface is itself an actively controlled, thrust-limited aerial vehicle. This paper presents a field-validated autonomy framework for a heterogeneous rover-mothership-child system executing rover supervision, mothership transit, child deployment and sortie, autonomous return, aerial recovery, and synchronized descent. title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied. A user study ($N=26$) reveals that relay operators, though not universally aware of the EoL policy, generally view it favorably. title: Advancing data integration in marine citizen science: insights from a collaborative workshop
abstract: The ocean remains critically under-observed, particularly in coastal zones where traditional monitoring is limited by cost, logistical constraints, and competing regulatory priorities. Marine citizen science offers an emerging and powerful complementary approach to addressing these gaps; however, data management challenges currently limit its full integration into scientific and policy data infrastructures. The inaugural workshop of the Marine Citizen Science Data Network (MCSDN), held in February 2026 in Ostend, Belgium, brought together approximately 200 participants from over 30 countries.

abstract: Environmental justice has become one of the defining principles of modern international environmental law, traditionally focusing on the equitable distribution of environmental benefits and burdens, public participation in environmental decision-making, and protection against environmental discrimination. title: Sea Surface Roughness Trends Estimation using Power Waveforms of BeiDou MEO Satellite Reflected Signals
abstract: The sea surface is a crucial climate regulator and the boundary where air and water interact. It fuels global weather systems and tempers climate change by absorbing heat and carbon dioxide, while its microscopic marine life generates a major portion of Earth's breathable oxygen. Sea surface roughness monitoring is essential for assessing ocean conditions and improving sea-state and marine weather forecasting. title: Climate Pressure and Labor Vulnerability in Colombian Caribbean Coastal Cities: Open-Data Evidence from Barranquilla, Cartagena, Santa Marta, and Riohacha
abstract: This study examines the association between coastal climate pressure and labor market vulnerability in four Colombian Caribbean cities: Barranquilla, Cartagena, Santa Marta, and Riohacha. Using open-access secondary sources from DANE, IDEAM, UNGRD, INVEMAR, and DNP, the study constructs a 48-observation city-quarter analytical panel and estimates city and period fixed-effects models, distributed-lag specifications, and an event study design. abstract: Abstract As one of the four core components of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement), area-based management tools (ABMTs), including marine protected areas, are intended to advance the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction (ABNJ). abstract: The place of hippocamps in the Graeco-Roman cultural imagination was highly uneven, as they appeared prominently in visual media, but were exceedingly rare in ancient literary sources. title: Osmomixotrophy in Phytoplankton: Analysis of 46 Strains From Marine and Freshwater Habitats Indicates Prevalent Use of Organic Compounds
abstract: Osmomixotrophic use of dissolved organic compounds may be more widespread than previously recognized, but research seems so far isolated and mostly focusing on single phytoplankton groups or strains. Here we combined data from 24 marine and 22 freshwater strains to analyse their ability to use dissolved organic compounds. The results emphasize that osmomixotrophy is ubiquitous in phytoplankton across functional groups and taxa isolated from various habitats and not strictly dependent on light or nutrient deficiencies. abstract: Introduction: The conservation of Indonesia's coastal environment is highly dependent on the role of customary law communities that uphold local wisdom. title: Employee fairness perceptions through social dialogue and proactive communication: evidence from Moroccan organisations
abstract: Employees’ fairness perceptions have become increasingly important in contemporary human resource management (HRM) because they are closely associated with employee well-being, workplace relationships and organisational effectiveness. Although organisational justice has received considerable attention as a framework for understanding employees’ fairness perceptions, limited evidence explains how participatory, communicative and regulatory organisational mechanisms are jointly associated with these perceptions, particularly in emerging organisational contexts. title: CWAS: A Dense Passive-Source Seismic Survey to Image Northwestern Australia
abstract: Abstract Northwestern Australia preserves a complex record of Precambrian craton formation and passive-margin evolution, yet its lithospheric structure remains poorly constrained because of thick sedimentary cover and sparse seismic observations. To address this gap, the China–Western Australia Seismic Survey was conducted between 2017 and 2019 by the Institute of Geology and Geophysics, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Macquarie University, and the Geological Survey of Western Australia. title: OFFSHORE WIND ENERGY ON THE COAST OF THE BRAZILIAN STATE OF RIO GRANDE DO NORTE: A CASE STUDY WITH ARTISANAL FISHING COMMUNITIES
abstract: Offshore wind farms (OWF) have become a vital renewable energy source and represent a promising sector for electricity generation in Brazil. Consequently, the country already has 59 projects registered with IBAMA, with 8 located along the coast of Rio Grande do Norte. In this context, there is a need to recognize the socio-environmental externalities related to their implementation. This study analyses the potential socio-environmental impacts of these projects, focusing on local fishing communities. title: ENVIDDA: Environmental data discovery and access framework
abstract: The relevance of environmental data as a major category of geospatial information is evident, as demonstrated by the continuously growing volume of data produced by observation and modeling systems. Ensuring compliance with the FAIR principles in environmental data discovery and access infrastructures requires not only the registration of rich metadata, but also the systematic documentation of contextual and provenance information, together with the adoption of standard protocols and data formats. title: Common Heritage of Mankind: The Evolution of the Concept and Its Significance in Contemporary International Law
abstract: The study examines the concept of the common heritage of mankind (CHM) and its role in contemporary international law. The historical context of the development of this concept is analyzed, its development since the mid-20th century and the reasons for its support by developing countries advocating for a new international economic order are traced. abstract: Abstract Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen is among the most celebrated of Portuguese poets, yet the eight literary fairy tales gathered in English as The Girl from the Sea and Other Stories (2020), first published separately in Portuguese from 1958 onwards, have rarely been read for their form. This essay reads the collection, together with the separately published Saga , as Kunstmärchen, fairy tales composed by a named author who deliberately reworks an inherited tradition. title: Об’єкто-орієнтоване архівування даних для довготривалого радіолокаційного моніторингу
abstract: The article considers the methodological foundations of object-oriented data archiving for long-term satellite radar monitoring of engineering structures using interferometric methods (InSAR). The relevance of the study is driven by the need for systematization, scalability, and reproducibility of InSAR analysis results when working with multi-year SAR image time series. The main focus is placed on the integration of new radar data acquired by the Sentinel-1 mission into existing InSAR projects implemented using the Persistent Scatterer Interferometry method within the StaMPS software package.

abstract: Small-scale fisheries account for 40% of global fish catch, employ 90% of the world's fishers, and play a pivotal role in food security, poverty reduction, and sustainable resource utilisation for a substantial portion of humanity. Fisheries co-management is now widely considered to be the most appropriate, fair, and effective form of governance for small-scale fisheries. abstract: This study aims to analyse the extent to which the Montara compensation has impacted the business sustainability and increased profitability of small-scale fishermen in Rote Ndao Regency. Previous research on oil spills has generally focused on direct economic losses and the fairness of compensation but has not examined how compensation translates into business sustainability and long-term profitability. abstract: Large unmanned cargo airships may support heavy-lift logistics in regions without runway infrastructure, but payload release produces a rapid buoyancy surplus and changes the vehicle mass properties. This study develops a simulation framework coupling six-degree-of-freedom variable-property flight dynamics, an active seawater ballast system, and constrained ballast-flow allocation. title: Organizational justice: a multidimensional analysis of military students’ perceptions
abstract: This study examines perceptions of organizational justice, namely distributive, procedural, and interactional justice, among military students enrolled in a Romanian military educational institution. Using survey data collected from 245 cadets, the analysis combines descriptive statistics, psychometric validation, non-parametric group comparisons, and regression modeling to investigate the multidimensional structure of organizational fairness perceptions. title: La confrontación entre el ordenamiento federativo y el ordenamiento estatal. A propósito del caso Dani Olmo
abstract: This article examines the conflict between federative and state legal systems through the case of Dani Olmo, whose registration was denied due to a breach of Financial Fair Play regulations. The study assesses the reasonableness of such denial under the principle of proportionality, weighing the balance between competition stability and the fundamental rights of professional footballers, particularly the right to work. The conclusion is that the registration ban fails the proportionality test.

title: On the Concept of Documedial Cooperativism
abstract: The contemporary data economy is characterized by unprecedented opportunities for value creation alongside significant inequalities in the distribution of that value. Existing data governance frameworks, largely founded on the understanding of data as information and centred on privacy protection, have proven inadequate in addressing power asymmetries between data subjects, data holders, and data users. abstract: Abstract Earth and other natural scientists frequently depict human-caused global environmental change as a recent development, a perspective exemplified by the proposal to formalize a human epoch in the Geologic Time Scale—the Anthropocene—beginning in 1952. Yet the science of archaeology offers abundant evidence of anthropogenic planetary change over thousands of years, from land clearing using fire to early methane emissions from agriculture, preindustrial lead pollution, and long-sustained Indigenous practices that continue to shape ecosystems and biodiversity. title: De mujeres de guardaparques a guardaparques mujeres
abstract: In this paper we reconstruct the events that led to the Argentine National Park Ranger Corps (CGN) formally granting women access to the job in 1986. A qualitative methodology is used, with interviews as the primary data collection technique. We understand this opening as occurring at the intersection of, on one hand, the agency of women demanding fair recognition for their work and seeking to occupy a position previously denied to them. title: Blue Cities, Green Laws: Legal Models for Urban Climate Resilience in the Global South
abstract: Blue cities are cities that plan themselves around water rather than against it: rainwater is stored, recycled and reused, streets and parks are given permeable surfaces, wetlands and lakes are protected and restored, and coastal settlements are defended by mangrove belts and flood-resistant construction. Rivers, lakes, drainage, drinking water supply, sewage and storm water are treated as one interconnected system, and nature-based solutions such as rain gardens, bioswales and urban forests are preferred to concrete drains that push water downstream. title: From Conservation to Commodification? A Comparative Analysis of Quota-Based Fisheries Governance in Indonesia, Iceland, and New Zealand
abstract: Background: Quota-based fisheries management aims to reconcile stock conservation with efficient access, yet harvesting entitlements may evolve from public allocations into asset-like interests. International lawof the Sea provides conservation frameworks but does not mandate private rights or quota markets. title: Dissemination of Sustainable Whiteleg Shrimp Farming Practices for GEDSI Groups in Dadap Village, Sambelia, East Lombok
abstract: GEDSI groups in coastal areas still face limited access to information, training, technology, and decision-making in productive economic activities, including whiteleg shrimp farming. This community service activity aimed to improve the knowledge and understanding of GEDSI groups in Dadap Village, Sambelia District, East Lombok Regency, regarding sustainable, inclusive, and environmentally friendly whiteleg shrimp farming practices. title: Improving landcover data governance in developing countries
abstract: Recent advances in open-access satellite imagery and processing tools have accelerated the production of national-scale landcover (LC) maps for land use planning and ecological monitoring. While such technological democratisation has expanded analytical capacity, it has also generated a new governance challenge: the coexistence of multiple, independently produced LC datasets without institutional coordination or custodianship. title: POPULATION GROWTH AND THE AVAILABILITY OF SOCIO-COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE CENTRAL ARRONDISSEMENT OF GRAND-POPO, BENIN
abstract: This study analyzes the impact of population growth on the availability of socio-community infrastructure in the central district of Grand-Popo, Benin. It is based on a review of existing literature and a field survey of 227 households in the Onkuihoué, Houssoukouè, and Ewe-Condji neighborhoods. The results indicate that 89% of respondents attribute population growth to natural factors and migration. abstract: Against the backdrop of the in-depth advancement of the Silk Road Economic Belt initiative, environmental protection in the overseas investment of Chinese enterprises has increasingly attracted the attention of the international community. From the perspective of international environmental law governance, this paper systematically examines the basic principles that should be established for the environmental legal system of the Silk Road Economic Belt. title: Malay Manuscripts as Cultural Memory: Islamic Knowledge Transmission in the Malay-Indonesian World
abstract: This article examines Malay manuscripts as media of cultural memory in the transmission of Islamic knowledge in the Malay-Indonesian world. Rather than treating manuscripts only as philological sources, material objects, or historical documents, it asks how material form, textual patterning, and social use jointly stabilize knowledge across generations. title: Multifaceted dynamics in variety and seed choices: the case of pumpkin farmers in northern Vietnam
abstract: Abstract Smallholder farmers’ crop variety and seed choices shape agro-biodiversity and livelihood sustainability. However, existing studies often overlook the dynamic, context-specific nature of these choices. We explored how introductions of hybrid pumpkin affected farmers’ pumpkin variety choices, seed sourcing, and seed management strategies across spatial and temporal contexts. title: Sources and environmental impacts of Kura River pollution under anthropogenic pressures in Azerbaijan
abstract: The Kura River is Azerbaijan’s principal river system and supports drinking-water supply, irrigation, hydropower, fisheries and riverine ecosystems. At the same time, its transboundary character and intensive human use make it vulnerable to multiple forms of pollution. This study examines the principal anthropogenic sources of Kura River pollution and their environmental implications by integrating two independently prepared research dossiers with a targeted review of scientific and institutional literature. abstract: This paper studies the dilemma and optimisation ideas of liability division in international cargo multimodal transport. abstract: Abstract Objective We sought to validate grandparentage analysis as a method to quantify the reproduction of hatchery-origin steelhead Oncorhynchus mykiss and fall Chinook Salmon O. tshawytscha in the wild by identifying natural-origin individuals with hatchery broodstock grandparents for each species in the Snake River basin. abstract: Territorial well-being analysis requires integrating two complementary families of information: objective indicators (equipment, composite quality-of-life scores) that characterize structural conditions, and subjective perceptions (citizen survey verbatims, interviews) that reflect lived experience. abstract: The ultimatum game (UG) and the dictator game (DG) are two of the most prominent tools in experimental and behavioural social sciences. Originally designed to study bargaining behaviour and decision-making in economics, these simple yet versatile scripts have come to be viewed by many as reliable instruments for measuring prosocial preferences, such as altruism, generosity, or sensitivity to social norms. abstract: Background and objective. Griffonia simplicifolia is a woody vine found in the secondary forests of West and Central Africa. Its seeds are an important source of 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP), a precursor of serotonin, and contain an oil rich in linoleic acid. Traditional knowledge and uses of this oil remain poorly documented. This study aims to document the ethnobotanical knowledge relating to the species in Togo, with a particular focus on the seed oil. abstract: Global warming is no longer merely an environmental or atmospheric phenomenon; it is an increasingly profound anthropological challenge affecting human health, livelihoods, migration, settlement, food systems, cultural practices, social institutions and relations between humans and the environment. abstract: Abstract Several types of nonlinear energy sinks have been proposed in the literature for shock and seismic vibration mitigation of dynamical structures. title: CLIMATE CHANGE IS HERE: WHY LAW MUST SHIFT FROM PREVENTION TO ADAPTATION
abstract: Objective: Climate change is no longer just a future problem, it's a current issue that affects how we govern, our rights, how we spend public money, and who is responsible for what. While it's still crucial to reduce the amount of greenhouse gases we release to limit how bad things will get, we also need to adapt to the changes that are already happening. Method: We should look at what's working and what's not, like the European Court of Human Rights' decisions on climate change, and use that to make our laws better. title: Evaluating the Livelihood Impact of Tourism Revenue Sharing Funded Projects in Communities Around Musanze District, Rwanda
abstract: Tourism Revenue Sharing (TRS) is a policy mechanism with a pivotal role to promote community development and conservation around protected areas in Rwanda. While the TRS programme has invested heavily in social infrastructure and community projects, there is a lack of empirical evidence on the impact of TRS on the livelihoods of households. title: “It is a sham process with participation.” Ten forms of citizen participation for sustainable development in the Norwegian Arctic
abstract: Achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) requires action at all levels, from local to global, through synergy among all societal actors. Norway shares responsibility for SDG-based sustainable development with local authorities (municipalities and counties). The Planning and Building Act’s purpose clause stipulates that it shall promote sustainable development for the benefit of individuals, society and future generations. Municipal responsibility for sustainable development, when incorporated into planning processes, is complex and requires the inclusion of diverse knowledge holders.

Conventional manual methods for digitizing these documents and estimating steel quantities are labor-intensive and error-prone, making it difficult to produce accurate quantity takeoffs within the tight timelines of the bidding phase. abstract: This research note, informed by qualitative fieldwork with resource harvesters in Nova Scotia, explores the effect of economic change and ecological crisis, the outcomes of rural development strategies, and demographic shifts that have shaped the province's rural areas in recent years. It argues that our present moment is ripe with opportunities for a renewed sociological attention on livelihoods in this region, which should take as its focus the relationship that people, communities, and government have with their physical environment. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of climate change on rice transplanting timings in Japan, focusing on Hyogo and Niigata Prefectures. title: An Exploratory Accounting Approach for Balancing Environmental Impacts of Point and Diffuse Sources in Nitrogen Trading
abstract: Nutrient trading between point and diffuse sources of nutrients offers an integrated watershed nutrient management approach to achieve nutrient reduction goals that benefit both the terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. This market-based approach requires quantification of the environmental impacts of nutrients derived from different sources. abstract: The planet cannot survive without a sustainable approach to development, and global energy systems are rapidly evolving to meet the growing demand for clean, renewable alternatives. In this context, wind energy plays a crucial role, particularly in regions rich in abundant wind resources. Since wind energy is free and has no emissions, it can provide the electricity needed to manufacture green hydrogen (GH2), which makes the combination of wind and hydrogen production a promising solution in the energy transition. abstract: Clear adaptation outcomes are essential for driving climate action and assessing progress. However, developing a shared vision of desirable adaptation outcomes and the steps to achieve them requires a shared understanding of what constitutes a well-adapted place and what resources are needed to enable communities to create and implement such visions. title: Moving beyond the common ground in normative theories of territory
abstract: In the last decades, political theorists have turned their attention to territorial rights and their normative justification. Here I suggest that, despite their differences, normative theories of territory share five assumptions: statism, groupism, sedentarism, anthropocentrism and resourcism. abstract: The rapid growth of tourism and urban activities has significantly increased household waste generation in Bali, while existing waste management systems face persistent capacity and behavioral challenges. title: The Effectiveness of Legal Protection for Sustainable Tourism in Ujung Kulon National Park
abstract: The legal protection of conservation areas has become increasingly important in achieving sustainable tourism, yet previous studies have generally examined conservation law enforcement, protected area management, and sustainable tourism separately. This study examines the effectiveness of legal protection for the Ujung Kulon National Park ecosystem in supporting sustainable tourism development. abstract: Abstract Research on the fishing industry typically centres the male-dominated catching sector, neglecting the post-harvest fishery historically sustained by fishermen’s wives. While existing curricula support teachers in connecting NGSS-aligned scientific sensemaking to the cultural, ecological, and political dimensions of the communities they serve, few frameworks integrate authentic rural educator perspectives and experiences. abstract: Maximising energy extraction in wave energy converters remains challenging due to the non-causal nature of the optimal control, complex interactions and real-time constraints. This paper presents a benchmarking of four strategies: LiTe-Con, LiTe-Con+, model predictive control (MPC) and spectral control. Drawing on the SSI research movement and Vision III of scientific literacy, we conceptualise critical modelling as a situated, collective, and deliberative practice that integrates disciplinary reasoning with ethical, political, environmental, and cultural dimensions of knowledge. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines why Gulf foreign aid has remained predominantly bilateral and fragmented since its emergence in the 1960s, despite the establishment of regional institutions, recurring regional crises and repeated calls for greater coordination. Bilateralism has been a persistent and defining feature of Gulf aid, and no effective regional humanitarian coordination mechanism has emerged even as Gulf donors have expanded and professionalised their aid institutions. title: Polyoxymethylene ethers as attractive hydrogen transport vectors? - Concept evaluation and steam reforming investigations
abstract: The efficient and safe transportation of renewable hydrogen remains a major challenge. Polyoxymethylene dimethyl ethers (OMEs) might be promising hydrogen transport vectors due to their liquid state at ambient conditions, low toxicity and high technical hydrogen capacity. However, two major bottlenecks for their application are identified: the direct synthesis of OMEs from CO 2 and H 2 and the catalytic steam reforming of OMEs for hydrogen release, which remains largely unexplored. abstract: Litigation focusing on advancing Indigenous Peoples’ rights, or provision of remedy where these rights have been impacted, often relies on a combination of legal frameworks and principles across international environmental law, international human rights law, biodiversity law and national indigenous rights law. This is apparent in the extractives context where Indigenous Peoples have sought to challenge the continued violations and a constant lack of recognition of their rights, whilst also simultaneously advancing the protection of biodiversity. abstract: The present paper is concerned with the ongoing debate on neurorights from the standpoint of legal philosophy. The fundamental question is whether these rights should be understood as a reinterpretation of existing fundamental rights or as a distinct emerging legal category. abstract: This study investigates the interrelationships among Emotional Intelligence (EI), Teaching Self-Efficacy (TSE) and Classroom Incivility Management (CIM) among university faculty members in Gujarat, India. abstract: Inland fisheries provide livelihood, nutritional, and leisure opportunities to people around the world; associated biodiversity and functioning freshwater ecosystems are necessary for sustainable inland fisheries. These connections and contributions, however, have largely been overlooked or under-appreciated by national and international development and conservation communities. abstract: Introduction Traditional dress constitutes an important medium through which cultural meanings, social identities, and collective memory become materially and visually communicable. abstract: Urban communities continue to face unequal exposure to climate impacts and exclusionary governance; however, cities are increasingly deploying joint mitigation and adaptation interventions. This paper presents a rapid review of global case studies to map promising pathways for achieving urban climate justice. abstract: Land governance persistently fails to achieve its stated objectives, producing unintended outcomes, coordination failures, and inequality. This paper argues that a major reason is the treatment of land use, land rights, and land value as parallel administrative domains rather than as mutually constitutive components of one recursive governance structure. The Land Triadic Nexus, developed here, explains governance outcomes as a function of the degree of alignment among these three domains. abstract: Abstract The circular economy (CE) has gained substantial policy traction, yet its social dimensions — particularly the roles, contributions, and vulnerabilities of social economy actors in the Global South—remain insufficiently mapped. This systematic scoping review examines how waste-pickers, cooperatives, social enterprises, and informal sector workers are positioned within CE transitions, adopting a multi-level analytical framework spanning micro-level livelihood outcomes, meso-level institutional and governance mechanisms, and macro-level CE system performance. abstract: The Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Trade-offs Habitat Quality (InVEST HQ) model offers a spatially explicit approach for assessing habitat quality utilizing relatively simple, readily available data and an intuitive interface. In this paper, we provide a literature review of the InVEST HQ application based on 61 scientific papers, which have been systematized, analysed, and interpreted using a detailed and structured original template. title: Divergent fertility responses to cyclones and floods: a mixed-methods study from rural Bangladesh
abstract: Over the past decade, Bangladesh has experienced substantial demographic change alongside increasing climate-related disruption. This study examines the links between extreme climatic events and fertility among married Bangladeshi women of childbearing age who already have children, focusing on how cyclones and floods relate to fertility behaviour in cyclone- and flood-prone villages. title: A multi‐objective decision‐analysis framework for addressing human–wildlife conflicts
abstract: The costs and frequency of negative interactions between people and wildlife (that is, human–wildlife conflict or HWC) are increasing globally and hindering conservation efforts. Practitioners are challenged to manage wildlife populations and consider human health and livelihoods simultaneously. Principles and tools of conservation decision‐making can help relevant parties navigate the complexities, uncertainties, and difficult trade‐offs involved in managing HWC. title: Killing Nature to Save It: Conservation Science, Biotechnology, and Ethical Extermination
abstract: There is a deep tension within conservation: The field aims to protect the well-being of flora, fauna, and ecosystems, but often goes about doing this by mass-killing invasive animals. Into this picture comes biotechnology, a field of research that engages with modifying the fundamental building blocks of life. Biotech, and in particular suppression gene-drives, seem to promise win-win solutions that allow us to painlessly and gently remove invasive species from ecosystems. title: Coupled drought–land use dynamics and agricultural resilience in mainland Southeast Asia
abstract: Abstract Drought is initiated by climatic anomalies, but its development and consequences often unfold as a coupled socio-ecological process shaped by interactions among land use, water infrastructure, resource management, and governance. This coupling is particularly pronounced in Mainland Southeast Asia (MSEA), where strong monsoon dependence, rapid land-system transformation, expanding hydraulic infrastructure, and intensive water use influence how climatic water deficits propagate through hydrological, agricultural, and livelihood systems. title: Few-frame depth image reconstruction algorithm for GM-APD LiDAR based on three-dimensional spatiotemporal kernel density estimation
abstract: Echo data acquired by Geiger-mode avalanche photodiode (GM-APD) LiDAR under conditions of limited frame accumulation and low signal-to-background ratio (SBR) exhibit severe sparsity and discreteness, making it difficult for conventional one-dimensional histogram-based methods to accurately retrieve target depth. title: Mapping justice claims for solar geoengineering
abstract: Solar geoengineering is a set of controversial emerging technologies that seek to cool the planet by reflecting sunlight. These technologies may be able to reduce the worst impacts of climate change by lowering global temperatures temporarily. They also come with great risks, including as related to technological lock in and mitigation deterrence, among others. Balancing these potential risks and benefits demands a careful interrogation of justice and ethics. Unlike many scholars who assert a clear justice landscape, we argue here that the terrain is complicated, nuanced, and not fully mapped.

title: Automatic evergreen forest mapping based on Harmonised Landsat Sentinel-2 and existing broad-category land cover product within Google Earth Engine
abstract: Evergreen forests retain green foliage throughout the year and exhibit distinct phenological and biophysical characteristics. However, although many regional and global land cover products are available at 30 m resolution, most adopt coarse classification schemes and do not explicitly distinguish evergreen forests from other forest types. This study proposes a novel Automatic Evergreen Forest Mapping (AEFM) framework to generate annual evergreen forest maps at the city scale using dense Harmonised Landsat Sentinel-2 time-series data on the Google Earth Engine platform. title: Reproductive hesitation in the Norwegian petrostate
abstract: This article responds to calls for critical engagement with the entangled politics of reproduction, population, and climate breakdown by exploring analytical avenues that refuse both the individualization of responsibility and the logics of population. title: Effects of Renewable Energy Adoption on Public Health Outcomes in Nigeria's South-South Region
abstract: The worldwide transition to renewable energy is crucial for tackling environmental deterioration, climate change, and health issues related to reliance on fossil fuels. This research focused on the influence of renewable energy on public health and examined perceptions, possibilities, and obstacles concerning the energy shift in Nigeria's South-South area. A mixed-methods approach was employed, involving 400 questionnaire participants and 60 interviewees chosen from six states in the region. abstract: The International Symposium "Microbial Growth and Behavior: From Bench to Nature" was held as part of the annual meeting of the Society for Genome Microbiology, Japan. This session was designed to highlight challenges in modern microbiology: how to connect molecular insights obtained from laboratory model systems with the dynamic and complex responses of microbes in natural environments.

abstract: Alzheimer's disease and related dementias are increasingly understood as multicellular disorders in which neurons, glia, and vascular-associated cells may contribute differently to cognitive status and neuropathologic burden. abstract: After more than two decades of development, China has remained the world’s largest online retail market for 13 consecutive years, achieving a remarkable transformation from “the world’s factory” to “the world’s shopping center” and leading the development of the global e-commerce industry. abstract: This article re-examines the claim that international law is an autopoietic legal system. Autopoiesis remains attractive because it explains how a legal order may preserve a distinct identity through self-reference, recursive norm production, and operational closure in the absence of a central legislator, compulsory jurisdiction, or unified enforcement. abstract: Sporotrichosis, a subcutaneous mycosis caused by Sporothrix spp., has emerged as a major zoonotic disease in Brazil, primarily driven by Sporothrix brasiliensis. title: Network science reveals the structure and lasting impact of the Roman road system
abstract: Ancient infrastructure can leave lasting imprints on modern settlement patterns and mobility. The Roman road network connected vast regions of Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East, and is often mentioned as an example of such long-term impact. Yet its structural characteristics remain largely unquantified. Here we present a high spatial resolution quantitative exploratory analysis of the Roman Empire's road system, enabled by our creation of a spatially detailed Empire-wide dataset. abstract: Excessive carbon emissions are recognized as a significant contributor to climate change and environmental degradation. abstract: Abstract Modeling highly stable GNSS receiver clocks helps to increase the stability of correlated parameters, especially the station height. The use of a piece-wise linear receiver clock model, which is a common method for clock parametrization in Very Long Baseline Interferometry, has not yet been extensively investigated for GNSS. In this work, we examine piece-wise linear receiver clock modeling for GNSS. Based on a one-month series of kinematic Precise Point Positioning analyses for 56 highly stable hydrogen maser stations, the effects of piece-wise linear clock modeling are demonstrated.

abstract: Heat stress is an increasing concern as climate change drives more frequent and intense extreme heat episodes. The Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) is a widely used ISO-standard heat stress index that integrates air temperature, humidity, wind speed, and radiation (both shortwave and longwave) to assess heat stress. abstract: Astyanax Baird & Girard, 1854 is a widely distributed and species-rich genus of Acestrorhamphidae, whose abundant populations in Neotropical basins play a crucial ecological role at the trophic level. abstract: Green roofs provide a diverse array of ecosystem services, yet within the domain of natural and engineering sciences, where green roof research is most situated, performance-related studies are unevenly distributed across thematic dimensions. abstract: Abstract Determining earthquake magnitude and location through fast, automated methods is fundamental for seismic monitoring. abstract: In the context of global decarbonization imperatives, renewable energy expansion drives the energy transition while intensifying local socio-environmental conflicts. Although environmental and economic impacts of wind energy are widely researched, the role of democratic communication in legitimizing this transition remains underexplored. abstract: Groundwater amphipods in the Pilbara region of Western Australia are under pressure from the impacts of mining operations, particularly from groundwater extraction. abstract: Abstract The annual festival of Shāh-e Sarāb has been a major Hazara pilgrimage in Waras district of Afghanistan’s Bamiyan Province on the fourteenth day of Jawzā/Khordād (June 4). title: Insights and opportunities from materials chemistry research at primarily undergraduate institutions in the U.S.
abstract: Materials chemistry research at primarily undergraduate institutions (PUIs) in the United States is often characterized by the constraints faculty face: limited instrumentation, smaller research groups, heavier teaching loads, and rapid student turnover. This Perspective argues that PUI materials chemistry research is better understood not as a diminished form of research university science, but as a distinct and productive research mode with its own logic and strengths. abstract: Indigenous societies along the temperate Pacific coast of North America embody diverse cultural institutions. This variation is conventionally classified into two distinct cultural areas: the Northwest Coast (NWC) and California (CAL). abstract: Current patterns of food production and consumption are widely recognised as unsustainable. This review explores opportunities to shift food systems towards healthy diets and secure food yields while remaining within planetary resource boundaries. abstract: Digital transformation has emerged as a critical driver of agricultural supply chain resilience, yet the mechanisms through which technology investment translates into resilience outcomes remain inadequately understood. abstract: Flexible satellite structures with lightweight solar panels are naturally prone to structural vibrations caused by attitude maneuvers, continuous environmental disturbances and deformation during deployment. These vibrations can lead to a decrease in pointing accuracy, a degradation in payload performance, and an adverse effect on the overall stability of the spacecraft, thereby stressing the importance of effective vibration control. abstract: Despite growing interest in bat–virus interactions, experimental infection studies (EIS) remain taxonomically and geographically restricted, limiting inference about bat immunology and zoonotic risk. abstract: As funders of health and care research increasingly mandate inclusive research practices, the Manchester Biomedical Research Centre (BRC) and Clinical Research Facility (CRF) developed a comprehensive Inclusive Research (IR) Strategy to embed the principles of inclusivity across their experimental medicine research. This paper presents the co-production of the Strategy, shaped by collaboration between Inclusive Research Methods (IRM), Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI), and Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement (PPIE) teams, alongside public contributors and wider stakeholders. abstract: Abstract Achieving high‐peak‐to‐average power ratio (PAPR) remains a fundamental challenge in orthogonal frequency‐division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. abstract: Aspergillus flavus is a ubiquitous fungus commonly found in a variety of ecological niches including soil, crops, the air, and humans. In humans, it is the second leading cause of invasive aspergillosis (IA) and is linked to other illnesses through contamination of agricultural products with aflatoxins. As such, A. flavus threatens food safety, economic wellbeing, and human health, particularly in less developed regions and countries such as Cameroon. abstract: The study investigated the effect of audit committee attributes on the quality of financial reporting among listed consumer goods firms in Nigeria. This was with a view to providing information on the relevance of audit committee attributes to the enhancement of financial reporting quality (FRQ) in Nigeria. abstract: La polinización artificial en cultivares híbridos interespecíficos de palma de aceite (O×G) representa una de las labores de mayor demanda operativa y de mano de obra dentro del proceso productivo. abstract: This study undertakes a systematic review to examine the role of space science and technology in addressing Africa’s pressing challenges in agriculture, water management, disaster resilience, urbanization, and digital inclusion. Evaluating how Earth Observation, satellite navigation, and communication technologies contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) being its main objective. title: Implementation of an agribusiness system to support rice farming performance in Grobogan, Indonesia
abstract: Examining the implementation of an agribusiness system and its effect on rice farming performance in Grobogan is crucial for identifying challenges and opportunities to improve farmers’ productivity, efficiency and profitability. The findings of this analysis can serve as a foundation for developing suitable policies and programmes to support advancement of rice-farming in Grobogan. This study analysed agribusiness implementation, production, efficiency, profitability of rice farming. title: Normative Legal Analysis of Corporate Legal Responsibility for Greenwashing Practices and Environmental Damage: Case of Dayak Kanayat’n
abstract: This study investigates corporate legal liability for greenwashing practices that cause environmental harm in Indonesia. Growing global pressure for sustainable business practices has prompted many corporations to publicly commit to protecting the environment, but such narratives often serve as public relations efforts rather than genuine ecological responsibility. Using a normative juridical method with statutory and conceptual approaches, this research identifies the patterns and defining features of greenwashing while assessing the sufficiency of Indonesia's existing legal framework. abstract: This paper explores the connection between consumer knowledge and sustainability, examining how new sustainability-related information can influence consumers' willingness-to-pay (WTP) for sustainable products. Our analysis was based on an adapted version of Ajzen's Theory of Planned Behavior model, in which knowledge is conceptualized as a dynamic, modifiable variable that can reshape behavioral intentions. abstract: Introduction West Nile virus (WNV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus maintained in bird–mosquito cycles, with occasional spillover events causing neuroinvasive disease in humans and animals. This study describes two fatal cases of WNV lineage 2 infection in captive harbor seals housed in a zoological park in southern Italy, together with genomic characterization and phylogenetic analysis of the detected strains. title: Minority State Ownership and Compensation Outcomes in Privately Owned Enterprises: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT Persistent compensation disparities between privately owned enterprises (POEs) and state‐owned enterprises (SOEs), together with substantial pay gaps within POEs, are salient manifestations of income inequality in China. This study examines how minority state ownership reshapes the compensation structure of POEs. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how Chinese television dramas socially construct corporate social responsibility (CSR) in the context of ethical family‐business succession. Drawing on stakeholder theory and qualitative content analysis, we analyze eight widely viewed TV series (including one negative case) that dramatize succession processes in Chinese family firms. title: Polychlorinated Biphenyls in Samples from Polish Lactating Women. Exposure Assessment and the Correlations Between Pollution Content and Data from the Medical Questionnaire
abstract: Chemical substances used in various industrial applications can pose serious environmental risks. Among them, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are of particular concern. These compounds have been detected in both environmental and biological samples, including human breast milk. In this study, seven PCBs (PCB 28, 52, 101, 118, 138, 153, and 180) were quantified in 67 breast milk samples from lactating mothers residing in the Kuyavian-Pomeranian region of Poland. abstract: Abstract Human-wildlife conflict is a major challenge in conservation biology with ecological and socioeconomic consequences. The problem is particularly delicate when the animals involved are threatened with extinction and experiencing rapid habitat loss due to climate change and anthropogenic actions. Here, we examined crop-foraging on farms in Central North Algeria by the Endangered Barbary macaques ( Macaca sylvanus ) to understand the conflict severity. title: Methodological Variations in Environmental Justice Screening Tools and Their Impact on Disadvantaged Community Designations
abstract: Government agencies in the United States have developed environmental justice screening tools (EJSTs) and designations to promote equitable distribution of benefits from environmental policies to disadvantaged communities (DACs). However, the methodological choices embedded in these tools, including the selection, weighting, and aggregation of environmental justice indicators, vary across EJSTs, and their implications for DAC designation outcomes are poorly understood. abstract: The 2025 release of court documents connected to convicted sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein included a wire transfer label reading “Baal name”—a typographical anomaly that ignited viral claims connecting Epstein’s network to an ancient Canaanite child-sacrifice cult. title: From brain drain to geopolitical talent competition: scientific diasporas and the future of Global South development
abstract: Scientific diasporas have emerged as increasingly important actors in global science, technology, and innovation (STI) ecosystems. In the context of geopolitical fragmentation, technological competition, and intensifying global inequalities, talent mobility is no longer solely a migration issue but a strategic dimension of development, science diplomacy, and international influence. Among various imaging techniques, thermography is a promising noninvasive, non-ionizing, and cost-effective modality for real-time diagnosis. This study proposes a multilevel threshold segmentation approach based on Enhanced Hippopotamus Optimization (EHO) for breast thermographic images. abstract: Abstract In this paper, we study the impact of short-term rentals (STR) on housing markets in Portugal, exploiting a 2014 policy reform that eased registration requirements. Using a novel dataset of property transactions from 2010 to 2017 for the Lisbon and Porto metropolitan areas, we estimate the effect of STR expansion using a two-way fixed effects model and a difference-in-differences design that leverages staggered treatment across postcodes. abstract: Remote sensing and Earth observation technologies are expanding rapidly across scientific, commercial, and governmental domains, yet limited empirical research has examined how these roles are defined in practice. This study analyzes 250 public remote sensing job postings across 33 nations collected over an eight-month period in 2025. abstract: The engineering planning and design of Small Water Impounding Projects (SWIPs) necessitates proper site selection to ensure technical viability and sustainability. abstract: This study investigates the direct and indirect impacts of work-life balance and career development on employee performance at the Semarang Tengah Primary Tax Service Office (KPP Pratama Semarang Tengah), utilizing job satisfaction as a mediating variable. abstract: Purpose The human extracellular matrix (ECM) provides essential cues for intestinal homeostasis. While most studies focus on ECM degradation by host cells, emerging evidence suggests that commensal gut bacteria may also contribute to these remodeling processes. abstract: Abstract What defines an émigré scholar? When scholars became refugees, they had to find ways to move their knowledge with them. abstract: Short-term congestion at public electric-vehicle charging stations depends on both near-future demand and how vehicles are distributed across the network. abstract: This study examines the contribution of sustainable tourism to increasing Local Own-Source Revenue (LOSR) in Klaten Regency, Indonesia. The analysis is based on four key dimensions of sustainable tourism: economic, social, environmental, and institutional. abstract: This study evaluated the implementation and effectiveness of police patrol operations in Northern Samar, Philippines, to establish an empirical basis for strategic interventions. abstract: For its outstanding biodiversity Ecuador has been designated as one of ten megadiverse countries. Due to its location on the equator, it enjoys many climates, soils and diverse geological processes. In Ecuador, palms represent the group of native plants with the greatest diversity of uses per species. Cluster farming has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance smallholder resilience; however, existing evidence remains fragmented. abstract: For more than seven decades, the US alliance has been a central pillar of Australian security policy. Yet the last decade has seen US commitments become increasingly conditional and uncertain. Why has Australia responded to growing uncertainty about the reliability of the US by binding itself more deeply to the alliance? title: Effectiveness of emergency nutrition program for toddlers after Mount Semeru eruption in Lumajang: CIPPO evaluation
abstract: Malnutrition in toddlers remains a public health concern in Indonesia. East Java reports a relatively high prevalence of wasting (7.2%), while Lumajang Regency recorded a severe wasting prevalence of 6.9% in 2022, exceeding WHO public health thresholds and increasing from the previous year. The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru disrupted food systems and limited access to health and nutrition services, increasing nutritional risks among affected toddlers. title: Language shifts as a catalyst for social and educational cohesion in multilingual societies
abstract: Although the Indonesian New Capital City, or Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN), is a potential living laboratory of a multilingual society, studies investigating the extent to which language shift conditions stimulate educational cohesion remain limited. To fill this gap, this research aims to investigate language shifts at schools in IKN to achieve equitable education. The participants were teachers and high school students who lived in three subdistricts of IKN (Sepaku, Penajam Pasir Utara, and Muara Jawa). title: Tracing the development of primary students' expressed sustainability conceptions through SDG-based classroom action research
abstract: This qualitative classroom action research study traced the development of primary school students' expressed sustainability conceptions during an 8-week interdisciplinary process based on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Participants were 31 fourth-grade students (aged 9–10) in one intact classroom of a public primary school in Istanbul, Türkiye. Instruction comprised 24 class periods of 40 min across eight weekly action research cycles; the second author taught all lessons while the first author observed every session. Data comprised pre- and post-instruction conception tasks, learn

title: Water resources in Spain: addressing challenges to water security
abstract: Successfully addressing and resolving water challenges, in a global context where the vectors of population growth, urbanisation, climate change and globalisation are at work, is a key element to foster sustainable development and achieve an improvement in the quality of life of societies and people. It is essential that water is on the political agenda and that many actors play their role properly, with the appropriate governance. The Sustainable Development Goals are not always synergistic among them, and SDG 6 on water interacts with a number of other SDGs. Understanding this is essential t

title: Derechos humanos frente a la automatización de las decisiones públicas: revisión bibliográfica
abstract: La automatización de las decisiones públicas mediante sistemas de inteligencia artificial plantea riesgos relevantes para la protección de los derechos humanos, especialmente cuando sus resultados inciden en derechos, obligaciones o acceso a servicios públicos. El estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar las implicaciones jurídicas de estas tecnologías y las principales garantías aplicables frente a sus riesgos. journal: Journal of Multidisciplinary Novel Journeys & Explorations

title: Plant part substitution as a sustainable conservation strategy for some medicinal plants based on phytochemical equivalence
abstract: Abstract Medicinal flora represents an essential source of bioactive substances for both conventional and contemporary medicine; nevertheless, excessive extraction of non-renewable parts such as roots, bark, and heartwood has led to significant reductions in wild populations, especially among endemic and slow-growing species. This review proposes and evaluates the substitution of plant parts by replacing vulnerable bark and roots with renewable aerial parts, using published evidence of phytochemical equivalence for sustainable conservation of medicinal plants. title: A comprehensive review of U.S. wholesale electricity markets: Structure, challenges, geopolitical tensions, current trends and future directions
abstract: Restructuring has transformed the United States (U.S.) electricity sector from cost-based, vertically integrated monopolies to competitive Wholesale Electricity Markets (WEMs), marking one of the major shifts in the modern energy industry. Independent System Operators and Regional Transmission Organisations (ISOs/ RTOs) have led this transition by coordinating generation, transmission, and market operations across large regions. This paper reviews the evolution of U.S WEMs and examines how restructuring has shaped market competitiveness, operational efficiency, and environmental performance. S

title: Long-Term Drought Variability in Southwestern Uganda: A Comparative Analysis of Ground and Satellite Rainfall Data for Mbarara
abstract: This study analysed drought occurrence in Mbarara District using ground-based observations and satellite-derived rainfall estimates from the Climate Hazards Infrared Precipitation with Stations (CHIRPS) data (for the period 1981–2024) and the Climate Prediction Center Morphing Technique (CMORPH) datasets (1998–2023). A comparison between satellite-derived and in-situ rainfall data was performed using simple linear regression and error metrics, while seasonal trends were assessed using the non-parametric Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen methods. title: Developmental and tissue expression breadth define distinct but overlapping classes of housekeeping genes
abstract: Housekeeping genes are commonly defined as broadly expressed genes that support essential cellular function. However, their identification in genome-wide datasets typically relies on spatial variation across adult tissues, while largely overlooking developmental time as an additional dimension of gene expression diversity. Here, we systematically compare gene expression breadth across developmental stages and adult tissues using zebrafish (Danio rerio) transcriptomic datasets that span embryogenesis and differentiated tissues. title: Governing green enabling megaprojects: reconciling transformative risk-taking with megaproject delivery discipline
abstract: This paper introduces green enabling megaprojects (GEMs) to characterize an increasingly important class of infrastructure for climate change mitigation. GEMs are large-scale green infrastructure projects whose primary value lies in enabling broader socio-technical transformation through subsequent adoption, diffusion, and scaling. GEMs sit at the intersection of two distinct literatures and governance imperatives: mission-oriented innovation policy (MOIP), which emphasizes public-sector transformative risk-taking under deep uncertainty, and megaproject management (MPM), which emphasizes megap

title: Derecho de supresión en modelos de inteligencia artificial generativa: estándar de neutralización funcional
abstract: El entrenamiento de modelos de inteligencia artificial generativa ha transformado los desafíos del derecho a la protección de datos frente a sistemas cuyo funcionamiento dificulta la eliminación de la información. En ese contexto, el objetivo de este artículo es analizar el alcance jurídico del derecho de supresión previsto en el artículo 17 del Reglamento General de Protección de Datos (RGPD) cuando los datos personales han sido incorporados al entrenamiento de un modelo de inteligencia artificial generativa. journal: Revista de la Facultad de Derecho y Ciencias Políticas

title: Evaluating geoscience campaigns in the conservation of water resources in the Western Region, Ghana
abstract: The Western Region of Ghana faces persistent water resource issues due to pollution, illegal mining, unsustainable land use, and degrading ecological integrity, public health, and livelihoods. Though geoscience-based water conservation campaigns have been initiated to remedy these issues, limited empirical data exist on their effectiveness in encouraging the conservation of water. This study assessed the impacts of these geoscience-based water conservation campaigns on water resource conservation in the area by evaluating their approaches, stakeholder involvement, and conservation results. title: Functional memory of drought affects leaf chemical defenses and microbial interactions in aspen
abstract: Abstract Drought is an increasingly important driver of tree mortality, but its long-term impacts on trait expression remain poorly understood. Leaves are a key interface at which trees respond to abiotic stress, and foliar traits such as chemical defenses and microbial communities may play an important role in determining post-drought resilience. Here, we tested whether prior-year drought leaves a persistent imprint on leaf traits in Populus tremuloides. institutions: The University of Texas at Austin

title: Mineralogical characteristics and soil behaviour of lime-stabilised dredged sediment from Sengguruh Reservoir for sustainable fill applications
abstract: Severe sedimentation in the Sengguruh Reservoir has reduced its effective storage capacity to approximately 24% of the original value, creating persistent dredging and spoil bank management problems. This study aimed to evaluate the potential reuse of dredged spoil bank sediment as sustainable fill material through lime stabilisation. Natural sediments and sediments treated with 10% and 15% calcium oxide on a dry weight basis were evaluated experimentally. journal: Journal of Water and Land Development

title: Hybrid quantum-inspired secure and energy-efficient framework for wireless sensor networks using quantum key distribution and optimization techniques
abstract: Abstract Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) require secure and energy-efficient communication because sensor nodes operate with limited battery power, constrained communication range, and high vulnerability to interception, spoofing, and malicious forwarding. Existing methods usually optimize security, clustering, or routing independently, which reduces overall network efficiency under dense and adversarial conditions. institutions: Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science

title: Inteligencia artificial en educación superior: transformación sociotecnológica y desafíos éticos-regulatorios
abstract: Este ensayo reflexivo de corte documental examina la evolución histórica, los fundamentos técnicos y las implicaciones socioeducativas de la inteligencia artificial (IA), con énfasis en educación superior. Se parte de la trayectoria de la IA desde sus bases formales y hitos fundacionales hasta su consolidación contemporánea mediante aprendizaje automático, redes neuronales y aprendizaje profundo. title: The environmental consequences of rising political populism and growing economic inequality
abstract: This paper examines how political populist support and income inequality are associated with the ecological footprint and its two sub-components: the carbon footprint and the non-carbon footprint (land and water use). Using a panel dataset covering 16 high-income European countries from 1990 to 2022, we estimate a dynamic panel error correction model. Three findings stand out. Right-wing populist support is positively associated with the carbon footprint, whereas left-wing populist support is negatively associated with the carbon footprint. journal: Journal of Environmental Economics and Policy

title: The rule of law in EU enlargement policy
abstract: Abstract Russia’s war in Ukraine has revived the European Union’s enlargement policy, placing it at the forefront of the EU’s priorities. This process is being viewed as the next phase of EU enlargement, encompassing the Western Balkans, Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia. This article examines the new framework for EU accession negotiations adopted in 2022, which regrouped the chapters of the acquis (presently 35 negotiating chapters) into six clusters. title: Shirking Responsibility and Accountability: Racial Capitalism, Biculturalism and the Ethics of the Crusaders Super Rugby Franchise’s Rebranding
abstract: This article examines the Crusaders Super Rugby franchise’s partial rebranding after the 15 March 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks as a case study in how sport reproduces settler/invader colonialism, racial capitalism and white possessive power in Aotearoa New Zealand. While the attacks prompted public scrutiny of the franchise’s name, medieval crusading symbolism and pre-match performance culture, New Zealand Rugby and the Crusaders retained the “Crusaders” name and substituted the horseman logo with koru-inspired branding. title: Exploring Mediated Electron Transfer in Vibrio natriegens
abstract: Vibrio natriegens is a promising biotechnological chassis distinguished by exceptionally rapid growth and dynamic metabolism. This microorganism can deliver electrons both directly to electrodes via the well‐established MtrCAB electron export system, as well as mediated through redox shuttle molecules. Notably, mediated electron transfer (MET) results in higher currents. Bioelectrochemical systems offer a possibility to influence the metabolic product spectrum of V. natriegens by using a poised anode as terminal electron acceptor. title: A Writer’s Universe: John Updike on Physics and Astronomy
abstract: Abstract Among the many twentieth-century authors who have been inspired by developments in science, the American novelist and poet John Updike stands out as a fascinating example. Interested in science and its history, he was well informed by his reading of popular science books and journals. From where did he get his information? How did scientists respond to his literary works referring to science, if at all? This paper offers a critical survey of Updike’s science-related writings from the mid-1950s to his death in 2009. title: Arab nationalism and historicity in the 1980s novel: Haydar Haydar’s Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr and Rachid Boudjedra’s Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq
abstract: Two 1980s novels from the Maghreb and Mashreq, respectively – Algerian writer Rachid Boudjedra's Maʿrakat al-Zuqāq (Battle of the Strait, 1986) and Syrian writer Haydar Haydar's Walīma li-aʿshāb al-baḥr (Banquet for Seaweed, 1983) - offer formal and thematic critiques of a regime of historicity that they link to Arab nationalist states after decolonization. Using François Hartog's regimes of historicity, this essay reads these modernist novels as sites of delayed processing for the thwarted hopes of progressive, anti-colonial emancipation. title: Learning to start a new business with values: the challenge of sustainable entrepreneurship in university teaching
abstract: Purpose This study aims to present a teaching methodology that integrates sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into entrepreneurship education to foster the development of sustainable business models (SBMs) through challenge-based learning (CBL) in higher education. Design/methodology/approach The methodology was implemented over five years at the University of Valencia and the University of Turku, combining CBL with a proprietary framework for designing, testing and scaling SBMs. A systematic literature review (2003–2024) was conducted to support the approach. journal: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education

title: Graph-guided MADQN based handover strategy for LEO satellite networks
abstract: In low earth orbit satellite networks, the high orbital velocity of satellites causes frequent communication link handovers, which adversely affects user service quality and the efficiency of network resource management. To maintain communication continuity, an effective handover strategy is required. Traditional handover strategies are typically based on fixed decision rules, which makes it difficult to balance handover frequency, signal quality, and network load balancing. title: Robustness Evaluation of Hyperspectral Image Classification Models Using Degradation-Aware Metrics
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification studies are generally evaluated on clean benchmark datasets and often report high-accuracy values. However, because real sensor data can be affected by different degradations, such as Gaussian, impulse, stripe, dead-line, and mixed noise, clean-data performance alone may be insufficient to explain the reliability of models under practical conditions. In this study, SVM, k-NN, 1D-CNN, 2D-CNN, 3D-CNN, Hybrid CNN, Dense CNN, and a transformer-based model were evaluated on the Indian Pines, Pavia University, and Salinas datasets under controlled noise scenarios.
journal: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science

title: TOURISM SITUATION IN THAILAND AND APPROPRIATE STRATEGIC ADJUSTMENTS
abstract: Tourism serves as a vital engine for the Thai economy, contributing significantly to national wealth; however, persistent disparities exist in income distribution between primary and secondary provinces. This study aims to analyze the current tourism situation in Thailand and identify appropriate strategic adjustments to enhance the industry’s resilience and sustainability. By evaluating the concentration of visitors and revenue, the research seeks to provide a roadmap for more equitable economic growth through tourism. This research utilizes secondary time-series data from 2012 to 2023 obtain

title: Modeling the pathway from transformational leadership to innovative work behavior via AI readiness: advancing SDG 4 and SDG 8 in Indonesian higher education
abstract: Drawing on a cross-sectional survey of 250 lecturers and administrative staff from Indonesian higher education institutions (HEIs), this study examined the statistical relationships among transformational leadership, AI readiness, and innovative work behavior (IWB) using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings showed that transformational leadership was positively associated with AI readiness (β = 0.654, p < 0.001) and IWB (β = 0.322, p < 0.001), while AI readiness was positively associated with IWB (β = 0.451, p < 0.001). title: Assessment of Household Water Security in Makurdi Town, Benue State, Nigeria
abstract: Makurdi town is contending with many water related issues that impede efforts targeted at achieving water security for the growing population. Water security is a multidimensional concept that seeks to address the array of issues related to water. Previous studies in Nigeria and Makurdi in particular, employ a methodology for water security assessment that merely accounts for water access or water scarcity, thereby limiting the scope of the concept. title: Addressing the ‘Airport Operations Challenge’: Stakeholder Perceptions on Business Investment Opportunities and Regulatory Uncertainty in Autonomous Ground Handling
abstract: Abstract Regulation and technology innovation are crucially intertwined in many cases and industries, notably in air transportation. Airports are safety- and security-critical environments governed by detailed regulatory frameworks at multiple authority levels. The deployment of automation solutions in ground operations remains loosely regulated. abstract: Kualitas layanan diakui sebagai determinan utama kinerja perusahaan pariwisata, berbagai studi menunjukkan bahwa terdapat kesenjangan antara ekspektasi wisatawan dan persepsi layanan yang diterima, terutama pada dimensi bukti fisik, keandalan, dan daya tanggap layanan. title: The Contribution of Shell Petroleum Company Toward Healthcare Delivery in Onne Oil Bearing Communities
abstract: The study investigated the contribution of Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) toward healthcare delivery in Onne oil bearing communities. While the Nigerian state depends extensively on petroleum revenues and oil Companies focus primarily on extraction and profitability, communities such as Onne in Eleme Local Government Area disproportionately bear the environmental and health consequences of oil operations. title: Provincial differences and model-based driver attribution of carbon emissions in China: A swarm intelligence–optimized random forest and scenario analysis
abstract: Assessing the long-term environmental implications of low-carbon development pathways requires methods that can capture nonlinear patterns and provincial differences. This study develops a swarm intelligence–optimized Random Forest model within an extended Stochastic Impacts by Regression on Population, Affluence, and Technology (STIRPAT) framework for provincial carbon-emission driver attribution. title: Delivering sustainable food: exploring college students’ willingness to pay for carbon labels in China via a choice experiment
abstract: The rapid expansion of online food delivery has intensified concerns about packaging waste and carbon emissions, making sustainable consumption an increasingly important component of the sector’s low-carbon transition. Whether environmental information disclosure can shift consumers’ choices toward lower-carbon alternatives is therefore an important issue for improving the sustainability of digital food-delivery platforms. title: Does Islamic Finance Flatten the Environmental Kuznets Curve?
abstract: This study evaluates the role of Islamic financing in moderating the Environmental Kuz-nets Curve (EKC) dynamics in Saudi Arabia using Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach applied to annual data from 1990 to 2024. The empirical result contradicts tradi-tional EKC hypothesis as it confirms a long-run U-shape relationship between income and CO2 emissions. title: Professional legitimacy in Swedish wildlife management: frontline bureaucrats in a gendered governance landscape
abstract: Swedish wildlife management is characterized by multi-level governance, stakeholder conflict, and strong cultural ties to hunting. In this contested arena, frontline wildlife officers play a central role in mediating between state authority and local interests, making professional legitimacy a critical institutional resource. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with wildlife officers from 20 out of 21 County Administrative Boards, this article examines how wildlife officers in Sweden build and sustain professional legitimacy through everyday practices within a gendered governance landscape a
journal: Journal of Environmental Planning and Management

title: Data is not Labor: A reply to Kim and Vincent
abstract: Abstract In a recent article in this journal, Kim and Vincent (2026) argue that the everyday interactions of ordinary users with digital platforms like Facebook, Google, and Amazon involve data-producing labor . I argue that Kim and Vincent’s view is either independently implausible or redundant by their own lights. Whatever the injustices of everyday user interactions with these platforms—and they are many—they do not involve the exploitation of their data-generating labor.

title: ‘My In-Laws Forced Me to Have an Abortion’: Coercive Control and Gendered Entrapment Among Migrant Women During COVID-19 in India
abstract: Abstract Violence Against Women and Children represents a global health crisis which was made worse by the COVID-19 pandemic. Yet, empirical investigations of how gender-based violence changed with the pandemic remain scarce. This article seeks to understand migrant women’s experiences with coercive control in the context of COVID-19 in India. title: INFLUENCE OF BIOCLIMATIC CONDITIONS ON REPORTED UNCOMPLICATED AND SEVERE MALARIA CASES IN THE SECOND DISTRICT OF COTONOU, BENIN
abstract: Malaria remains a major public health concern in Benin, and its seasonal pattern may be influenced by local climate. This study examined associations between bioclimatic conditions and reported uncomplicated and severe malaria cases in the second district of Cotonou. Monthly temperature, relative humidity and rainfall data for 1995-2024 were obtained from Météo-Bénin, while monthly malaria data for 2005-2024 were obtained from the Littoral Departmental Health Directorate.
