title: Navigating Organisational Change in the Australian Public Service: Demographic Shifts and Leadership Perception
abstract: Organisational cultural change driven by demographic shifts is affecting employee perceptions of leadership roles within the Australian Public Service (APS). Despite longstanding diversity challenges, the APS has implemented policies to increase female employees’ representation in senior roles. This study examines the demographic composition and perceptions of Senior Executive Service (SES) leaders in the APS from 2018 to 2024, using APS census data (N = 127,262) and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression to analyse relationships among age, gender, and perceived leadership effectiveness. title: The Spiritual Dimension of Palliative Care Patients and Their Caregivers in a Compassionate Community in Two Brazilian Favelas1: A Mixed-Methods Study
abstract: Spirituality is a key dimension of palliative care, contributing to well-being, supporting adjustment to illness, and serving as an important coping resource for patients and caregivers. In socially vulnerable settings, compassionate community initiatives may facilitate the integration of spiritual care and help mitigate the effects of limited access to health and social resources. title: Harmine selectively enhances human beta cell identity markers and function via protein kinase A pathways
abstract: AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Harmine and other small-molecule inhibitors of the kinase, dual tyrosine-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A), induce human beta cells to replicate and regenerate in vitro and in vivo and are effective at reversing diabetes in animal models. title: Quality of Road Transport Infrastructure and Intra-African Agricultural Exports: A Long Run Two-Step System Generalized Method of Moments Analyses
abstract: Sustainable growth requires developing economies to simultaneously attain economic and environmental sustainability. This study examines the effect of the quality of road transport infrastructure of the exporting and importing countries on intra-African agricultural exports from 2006 to 2018. To achieve this objective, the study employed the two-step system generalized method of moments, short-run and long-run estimators. title: Utilizing Architectural Design Strategies to Optimize Spatial Efficiency in A Proposed Convention and Exhibition Centre in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates how architectural design strategies can optimise spatial efficiency in convention and exhibition centres, with application to a proposed facility in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Convention centres are increasingly required to host simultaneous programmes (conferences, exhibitions, banquets, and civic events) and to support rapid changeovers; consequently, efficient spatial planning, clear circulation, and adaptability are critical to operational performance and user experience (Ovais Ansari, n.d.; Jude Barnaby & Igwegbe Uzodinma, 2024). title: Military Coup and Regional Integration in Africa: Themes, Trends and Threats to ECOWAS
abstract: West Africa in the past decade has witnessed an alarming resurgence of military coups. This article examines the implications of this coup wave for regional integration as it affects Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) using democratic theory as its framework. This article is predicated upon qualitative method of research, utilizing secondary sources of data collection from Journals, newspaper publications, online news outlets, official documents, etc. Anchored on the preceding methodology, we reviewed the literature on African coups and regional integration. title: The Negotiation of New Heights and Essence by Bakossi Traditional Authorities Under Colonial Rule
abstract: This paper aims to present the pride and prejudice of the Bakossi traditional authority in the south-west region of Cameroon. It shows how the imposition of colonial rule led to a systematic abuse and disregard for the local institutions that were so dear to the people. The Germans then British modified the political structures in which the traditional elite enjoyed a privileged position to their own advantage. title: Impact of Cost Transparency and Mixed Revenue Use on the Maximum Acceptable Carbon Tax
abstract: Abstract Public acceptability remains a major barrier to implementing effective carbon taxes. Resistance often stems from misconceptions about the costs and benefits of the policy. Two potential tools to improve acceptability are revenue recycling, which links the tax to tangible benefits, and cost transparency, which presents the financial burden in more concrete and understandable terms. This paper examines the effects of mixed revenue use and cost transparency on carbon tax acceptability, drawing on representative survey experiments in Germany ( n = 1327) and Italy ( n = 1293). title: Análisis informétrico del impacto social en la producción científica de Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Colombia y México (2016–2024)
abstract: En el contexto de los debates recientes sobre la función social de la ciencia, el impacto social ha adquirido una presencia creciente como categoría discursiva en la evaluación de la ciencia, especialmente en América Latina. Este artículo analiza, desde un enfoque informétrico, la manera en que el impacto social es tematizado en la literatura científica producida en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Colombia y México durante el periodo 2016–2024. title: Transfer learning-based fault diagnosis of wind turbine high-speed shaft bearings using CWRU pretraining and public run-to-failure data
abstract: Fault diagnosis of wind turbine high-speed shaft bearings (HSSBs) is hindered by the distribution gap between laboratory data and field signals, and by the lack of labeled run-to-failure recordings. This study proposes a three-stage transfer learning framework to address both problems. Stage 1 pretrains a lightweight convolutional backbone with a frequency-domain attention module (FAM) on the CWRU bearing dataset. abstract: This article draws on a corpus of oral history interviews collected in Serra da Estrela, Portugal, to examine how community memory, territorial knowledge, and lived relationships with the mountain contribute to understanding socio-ecological change and rethinking sustainability in a context of climate disruption. title: Research progress in the preparation of lactic acid from biomass by chemical catalytic process
abstract: Abstract Lactic acid (LA) is a versatile platform chemical widely used in food, pharmaceutical, and biodegradable plastic industries. While industrial LA production predominantly relies on fermentation, the chemo-catalytic conversion of renewable biomass-especially non-edible lignocellulosic feedstocks-has emerged as a promising alternative due to its potential for higher efficiency, lower environmental impact, and reduced competition with food resources. title: Talking about abortion in public: A dialogue with Emily C. Bloom and Stephanie Insley Hershinow
abstract: In this dialogue, Emily Bloom and Stephanie Insley Hershinow discuss public scholarship about abortion after the Dobbs decision. They share their experiences writing both personal and scholarly contributions about abortion in the contemporary US and in their respective historical fields as literary critics. They share their sense of the current legal landscape and discuss representations of abortion in a variety of contemporary discourses, including film, celebrity memoir, television, and narrative non-fiction.

title: Aspectos éticos en el tratamiento de los autores de abusos y de los acusados de abuso en el contexto eclesiástico
abstract: Dado el hecho de que durante mucho tiempo el modo en que la Iglesia afrontó los casos de abuso dentro de su ámbito de responsabilidad fue completamente insuficiente, descuidando de manera gravemente culpable los intereses y derechos de las víctimas, es comprensible que la cuestión sobre cómo tratar adecuadamente a los sospechosos y autores de abuso haya pasado a un segundo plano.
